### Reflection 302 — the root seed of a recursive-deliverable producer reuses the FLAT derivation's slice/decomposition verbatim and swaps only the body producer; the slice bridge is producer-agnostic

`(i'-b-descend-root-provider)`'s ROOT instance LANDED: `seqRoot_safeBodyUnit` (commit `f892397a`) delivers `SafeBodyUnit ContentStartTok ((tokens.toList.take (tokens.size - 2)).drop 2)` — the `provider` at the outer seq window `[2, size-2)` — directly from emission, with no recursion. The next-step note instructed: *locate, in the existing `scanFiltered_emitSeq_nonempty_structure` derivation, how the outer window's windowed `SafeBodyUnit` is obtained, and that slice bridge is the root provider verbatim.* The locate paid off in an unexpectedly clean way.

**The slice bridge is the flat lemma's OWN `take`-decomposition, and it is producer-agnostic.** `scanFiltered_emitSeq_nonempty_structure` establishes `h_take_eq : tokens.toList.take (tokens.size - 2) = (s₂.tokens.filter p).toList` — the interior slice equals the body block, because the two trailing pushes (`tok_fse`, `streamEnd`) are exactly what `take (size-2)` drops. It uses this to transport the body's *flat* `WellTyped` fact onto the windowed slice. The decisive observation: this identity is about the TOKEN ARRAY'S STREAM-WRAP STRUCTURE (`[` open, body, `]` close, `streamEnd`), not about what the body producer delivered — so it transfers verbatim to ANY fact over the body block. The root provider replays the SAME chain (`scanNextToken_flow_open_init` → body → `scanNextToken_flow_close_seq_outermost_ext` → `scanFiltered_tokens_eq_of_chain_short_stack` → decomp → `h_take_eq`), changing exactly ONE step: the body producer. Where the structural lemma calls the FLAT `emitList_body_filtered_characterization` (giving `WellTyped`/dyck/succ), the root provider calls the RECURSIVE `emitList_body_recseqbody` (giving `RecSeqBody` over the body block). Then `RecSeqBody.toSafeBodyUnit` projects through `h_take_eq` to the windowed `SafeBodyUnit`. Build green **556 jobs**, frontier holds at **4**, axiom-clean **`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`** (the standard triple — `Classical.choice` is the upstream scan-replay's, no `sorryAx`, no new axiom).

**Why swapping the producer loses nothing.** The flat facts the structural lemma extracts (`WellTyped`, dyck, `bodySucc`) are all PROJECTIONS of the recursive deliverable (`RecSeqBody.toWellBracketed`, etc. — R287/R290's projection family). So the recursive producer is strictly stronger at the body step: it delivers everything the flat one did PLUS the recursive structure. Re-running the derivation with it swapped in cannot fail for lack of the flat facts (they re-project), and it gains the `SafeBodyUnit` the flat path discarded. This is the consume-side dual of [[ref-recursive-producer-mirrors-flat-over-shared-induction]] (which BUILT the recursive producer by mirroring the flat one over the shared induction): here we CONSUME it by mirroring the flat consumer's chain-replay and swapping only the body step.

The transferable rule: to land the ROOT seed of a recursive-deliverable producer, do not author fresh windowing/decomposition reasoning — find the existing FLAT-fact derivation over the same input, observe that its slice/window identity is producer-agnostic (it is about the container's framing, not the body's content), and re-run it with the recursive body producer swapped for the flat one, projecting the richer deliverable through the unchanged slice identity. The flat facts re-project, so nothing is lost; the recursion is gained. The root seed costs one chain-replay you already have a verbatim template for, not a new induction. See [[ref-recursive-producer-mirrors-flat-over-shared-induction]] (the BUILD-side dual), [[ref-reduction-by-import]] (the windowed `SafeBodyUnit` retypes the residual to "the descent recursion"), [[ref-universal-producer-root-seed-first]] (root instance before the recursion), [[ref-guarded-universal-fold-relocates-guard]] (R301, the fold whose `provider` this discharges at the root), and [[ref-array-wrapper-window-generalization]] (the slice/window bridge as the reusable seam).

### Reflection 303 — probing the deferred `provider` universal before producing the descent caught a FALSE universal: the head-blind gate admits spurious windows where the `SafeBodyUnit` route is undischargeable

Following the de-risk discipline ([[ref-probe-deferred-universal-before-producing]], [[ref-minimal-pair-extracts-the-gate]]) BEFORE authoring `(i'-b-descend-root-provider-descent)`, the `provider` universal that `seqInteriorSeparators_of_safebody_provider` (R301) reduces the carrier to turns out to be **FALSE in general** — and the probe both proved it and named why.

**The minimal pair, on the real filtered scan of `[[1, 2], 9]`.** `scanFiltered (emit …)` yields the filtered token stream (`#eval`-confirmed): `streamStart [ [ "1" , "2" ] , "9" ] streamEnd` at indices `0..10`. The `provider` must deliver `SafeBodyUnit ContentStartTok ((take b).drop a)` at EVERY window `[a,b)` satisfying the gate `SeqTypedInterior tokens a b` (`flowBracketBalance tokens a b = 0` ∧ enclosing-seq `btFold`-top `= some true`). The decidable filter `tokens[a]! = .flowEntry ∧ balance a (a+1) = 0 ∧ btFold-top(take a) = some true` returns **`[4, 7]`** — the two depth-`0` commas BOTH satisfy the gate at `[a, a+1)` (balance `0`; the comma's `btStep` leaves the enclosing-seq `true` on top). Yet each window's slice is `[comma]`, and a `SafeBodyUnit` forces a `ContentStartTok` head (`SafeBodyUnit_head_Q`), which `.flowEntry` is not (`ContentStartTok_ne_flowEntry`). So `provider 4 5 …` and `provider 7 8 …` are **unprovable**: the gate is strictly too weak.

**The discriminator is necessary but NOT sufficient — the gate cannot locally characterize the good windows.** Content-start-alignment (`ContentStartTok tokens[a]!`) excludes the lone commas, but is still insufficient: the gated, content-start-headed window `[3, 5)` = `"1" ,` is a *trailing-separator* slice that is also not a `SafeBodyUnit` (a trailing `fe :: []` would need `SafeBodyUnit Q []`, refuted by `single`'s `e ≠ []`). The family of windows on which `SafeBodyUnit` holds — real seq-body interiors `[opener+1, close)` and their comma-suffix advance-tails — is closed under "drop a leading comma-separated prefix" but has **no simple window-absolute local gate**: bracket-framing `tokens[a-1] = [ ∧ tokens[b] = ]` picks out the interiors but EXCLUDES the comma-suffix tails (whose left boundary is a comma) the recursion's ADVANCE step instantiates.

**Yet the carrier's asserted facts are TRUE at every gated window** — they reference the boundary token PAST the slice, not the slice's `SafeBodyUnit`-ness. At the lone comma `[4, 5)`: `bodySuccFact` holds vacuously (`tokens[4]` IS a `.flowEntry`, refuting its premise) and `noTrailingSepFact` holds because `tokens[5]` = `"2"` is `isFlowContentStart`. So the carrier `SeqInteriorSeparators` is TRUE; only the chosen INTERMEDIATE (a uniform per-gated-window `SafeBodyUnit`) is too strong. The fold `seqInteriorSeparators_of_safebody_provider` is type-correct but has an **undischargeable hypothesis** for general `lo, hi` — a dead end if pursued literally.

**What landed (the kernel of the finding, commit `35437c6c`, both axiom-clean `[propext]`):**

* `SafeBodyUnit_head_Q {Q} (h : SafeBodyUnit Q body) (h_ne) : Q (body.head h_ne).val` — a `SafeBodyUnit` forces a `Q`-satisfying head (general, reusable; `cases` on the inductive, `e ≠ []` ⇒ body-head = entry-head).
* `not_safeBodyUnit_of_head_flowEntry (h_head : (body.head _).val = .flowEntry) : ¬ SafeBodyUnit ContentStartTok body` — the dead-end guard: a separator-headed window is no `ContentStartTok` `SafeBodyUnit`.

**The redirect.** Because the carrier's facts are true everywhere gated and reference the global stream, the descent must discharge them DIRECTLY — not via a uniform `SafeBodyUnit` provider. The promising route (to probe next): the whole-output deep guard `FlowBodyContentDeep tokens 2 (size-2)` recurses into nested brackets and may already carry depth-relative separator facts at every nested level, entailing `bodySuccFact`/`noTrailingSepFact` at arbitrary gated sub-windows with NO per-window `SafeBodyUnit` and NO descent recursion at all. This is [[ref-probe-deferred-universal-before-producing]] paying off exactly as designed: one `#eval` minimal pair, taken before producing, converted a planned multi-brick descent recursion into a single retargeted discharge — and the false intermediate is now fenced off by a proven lemma rather than discovered after a sorry. See [[ref-minimal-pair-extracts-the-gate]] (the pair confirms the gate INSUFFICIENT, names content-start as the would-be but failing discriminator), [[ref-guarded-universal-fold-relocates-guard]] (R301, the fold whose intermediate this bounds), and [[ref-reduction-by-import]] (the kernel retypes the residual from "produce the provider" to "discharge the facts directly").

### Reflection 306 — the new sub-fact reuses the WEAKER structure's existing wrapper via a strong→weak COERCION, not a mirrored wrapper: the producer's stronger refinement coerces down for free, the coercion's only gap closed by a head guard the inductive already carries

`(i'-b-encfacts)` needed ONE new fact — interior depth-`0` `feContentStart` (every interior separator of a seq body is followed by content) — to complete the three-fact enclosing bundle the R305 `provider` delivers. The next-step's de-risk asked whether this is a *direct `RecSeqBody.cons` projection* or *needs a new `SafeBodyUnit_array_*` window bridge*. The de-risk's answer turned out to be **neither**: the fact has *exactly the shape* of an EXISTING wrapper's output — `SafeBody_array_flowEntry_window` already proves "a depth-`0` `.flowEntry` at `k ∈ [lo,hi)` is followed by a `Q`-head at `k+1 < hi`" — but that wrapper consumes the WEAKER `SafeBody`, while the substrate the producer naturally delivers (and the bundle is keyed on, per [[ref-fold-consumer-chain-to-producer-contract]]) is the STRONGER `SafeBodyUnit`.

**The move: coerce strong→weak, reuse the wrapper — don't mirror it.** The instinct (and the next-step's fallback) would be to author `SafeBodyUnit_array_flowEntry_window`, a verbatim mirror of the `SafeBody` wrapper. Instead, observe that `SafeBodyUnit`'s extra strength over `SafeBody` is *more of the same constraint plus a head guard*: per-entry, `EntryUnit e` (`pbalance e = 0 ∧ ∀ i, 0 < i → i < |e| → pbalance (e.take i) ≥ 1`) strengthens `EntrySafe e` (`pbalance e = 0 ∧ ∀ i, e[i] = .flowEntry → pbalance (e.take i) ≥ 1`) at *every interior position* — its `≥ 1` for ALL proper nonempty prefixes subsumes `EntrySafe`'s `≥ 1` only-at-`.flowEntry` for every `i > 0`. The ONLY gap is the head (`i = 0`): `EntrySafe` would demand `pbalance [] = 0 ≥ 1` if `e[0] = .flowEntry`, which `EntryUnit` alone permits (a lone `.flowEntry` IS an `EntryUnit`). And that gap is closed by a field the `SafeBodyUnit` inductive ALREADY carries: the `Q`-head `h_head : Q (e.head).val` with `hQ : ∀ v, Q v → v ≠ .flowEntry` forbids a `.flowEntry` head, making the `i = 0` obligation vacuous. So `EntryUnit_entrySafe hQ` is a 6-line lemma, and `SafeBodyUnit_safeBody hQ` is a 4-line two-constructor induction — and the entire `SafeBody` wrapper library is reusable on a `SafeBodyUnit` substrate without duplication.

**What landed (commit `53ca7dea`, axiom-clean).** `EntryUnit_entrySafe` / `SafeBodyUnit_safeBody` (the coercion, `[propext]` only); `seqInteriorFeContentStart_of_windowed_safebodyunit` (coerce, then apply `SafeBody_array_flowEntry_window`; the `Q`-successor conclusion `ContentStartTok (tokens[k+1]).val` IS `isFlowContentStart (tokens[k+1]).val` — *definitionally identical predicates*, so the bridge is free); `seqEnclosingFacts_of_windowed_safebodyunit` (the bundle = the two prior facts via `seqSeparatorFacts_of_windowed_safebodyunit` + the new `feContentStart`), whose conjunction is *exactly* the `provider`'s deliverable shape. De-risked on `[[1,2],9]`: enclosing seqs `[3,6)`/`[2,9)`, interior commas at `4`/`7` followed by content at `5`/`8` — all `true`. Build green 560 jobs, frontier holds at 4.

**The transferable rule** ([[ref-coerce-to-weaker-reuse-wrapper]]). When a needed fact has the shape of an EXISTING wrapper's output but your substrate-in-hand is a STRONGER refinement than the wrapper consumes, test whether the strengthening is *monotone-plus-a-head-guard*: does the stronger per-entry predicate IMPLY the weaker one everywhere except possibly the head, and does the inductive's own head field (with a `hQ`-style exclusion) close that one gap? If so, write the strong→weak coercion (cheap) and reuse the wrapper, rather than mirroring the wrapper onto the stronger substrate (expensive, and it duplicates the wrapper's whole proof). This keeps the producer delivering ONE substrate and lets the consume side weaken on demand — the dual of [[ref-reduction-by-import]] (there: wire an unconsumed consumer to retype a residual; here: weaken a substrate to consume an existing producer-lemma). Sharpens [[ref-fold-consumer-chain-to-producer-contract]] (the bundle stays keyed on one `SafeBodyUnit`).

### Reflection 307 — the ROOT seed of a universal-over-gated-windows producer carries a DISCRIMINATOR hypothesis the gate cannot supply: the gate is satisfied by the descent's own targets, so root-membership is strictly stronger and the seed defers "which windows are root-level" to the descent

`(i'-b-locator)`'s base case asked: produce the enclosing-facts `provider` (the residual of `seqInteriorSeparators_of_enclosing_provider`) at the OUTER seq `[2, size-2)`, where `seqRoot_safeBodyUnit` already delivers the windowed `SafeBodyUnit` directly from emission with NO recursion. The de-risk read confirmed `seqEnclosingFacts_of_windowed_safebodyunit` consumes exactly that `SafeBodyUnit` and emits the three provider facts at `loS=2, hiS=size-2`, so the root brick is a pure packaging composition — `⟨2, size-2, ha, hb, hbal, seqEnclosingFacts_of_windowed_safebodyunit … (seqRoot_safeBodyUnit …)⟩`, axiom-clean, a dozen lines.

**The non-obvious part — the root seed's discriminator is NOT a projection of the universal's gate.** The full `provider` is universally quantified over gated windows `[a,b)` with hypothesis `SeqTypedInterior tokens a b` (balanced ∧ `btFold`-top `= some true`). The instinct is to make the root brick consume that SAME gate. But the gate is satisfied by *every* seq-typed window at *any* nesting depth — including the descent's own targets (a window two brackets deep is still seq-typed-and-balanced). So the gate ALONE cannot tell a root-level window (enclosed by the outer seq) from a nested one; `flowBracketBalance tokens 2 a = 0` (the window starts at the OUTER seq's depth) is strictly STRONGER than the gate and is NOT derivable from it. The root brick therefore carries that **top-level discriminator** as an explicit extra hypothesis — and that is correct, not a defect: the discriminator is precisely the balance-from-enclosing-origin quantity the descent step THREADS (each `descend` re-seats the origin to the located child opener, re-establishing `flowBracketBalance loS a = 0` at the new level). The root seed pins the producer at one fixed enclosing window and DEFERS "which windows are at this level" to the descent, where the located bracket supplies the discriminator constructively.

**The transferable rule** ([[ref-root-seed-discriminator-not-from-gate]]). When splitting a universal producer `∀ window, Gate window → Deliverable window` into a ROOT seed + a DESCENT (per [[ref-universal-producer-root-seed-first]]), check whether the seed needs a SECONDARY membership predicate the gate does not imply. It usually does, because the gate — being the WHOLE producer's domain — is satisfied by the descent's targets too (that is what makes them descent targets). So the gate cannot discriminate root-level windows from nested ones. Give the root brick the membership discriminator as an explicit hypothesis (here `flowBracketBalance tokens loS a = 0` for the fixed root origin `loS`), and recognise it as the SAME quantity the descent re-establishes per level — the root seed and the descent step share one discriminator, the seed receiving it as a hypothesis and the descent producing it from the located child. This keeps the seed a pure packaging of the infra-delivered deliverable ([[ref-root-seed-recursive-producer-swap]]) and isolates ALL the locate/descend analysis in the inductive step. Contrast [[ref-guarded-universal-fold-relocates-guard]] (there the guard is the producer's GIFT, narrowing its domain); here the discriminator is the seed's DEBT, a hypothesis it cannot discharge locally and must receive — because it names a fact about the window's position RELATIVE to the chosen root, which only the locator knows.

### Reflection 308 — after the root seed lands, FACTOR the descent before authoring it: a FROM-LOCATED assembler (located witness + its deliverable as hypotheses) discharges the existential trivially and makes the root a corollary; the de-risk then reveals the locator's DIRECTION is the residual's true shape — a bottom-up producer needs an INNER→OUTER locator the top-down recursion machinery does not provide

The 155th-revision "Next step" set `(i'-b-locator descent)` and optimistically predicted the existing seq-body locator (`recseqentry_seqbracket_oracle` / `flowBodyContentDeep_descend`) would "feed the locator with no extra reconstruction." The mandated de-risk — reading that machinery and `#guard`-probing `[[1, 2], 9]` (`Tests/Guards/Proofs/SeqDescentLocatorProbe.lean`) — sharpened the picture and corrected the prediction.

**What the probe confirmed.** On `[[1, 2], 9]` (filtered `streamStart [ [ "1" "," "2" ] "," "9" ] streamEnd`, outer seq body `[2,9)`, inner seq body `[3,6)`): the nested window `[3,6)` is gated (`flowBracketBalance 3 6 = 0`, `btFold`-top at `3` `= some true`) and NESTED (`flowBracketBalance 2 3 = 1`, so the R307 root discriminator fails). A BACKWARD scan (`locateEnclosingLoS`: largest `p < a` whose bracket opened at `p` is still open at `a`) locates the enclosing opener `p = 2` → `loS = 3`, and a forward close-scan gives `hiS = 6`, with `flowBracketBalance loS a = 0`, `loS ≤ a`, `b ≤ hiS`. Crucially the gate's `btFold`-top at the located `loS` is `some true`, MATCHING the located opener `tokens[2] = .flowSequenceStart` — so once the opener is located, its seq-vs-map TYPE need not be separately reconstructed; the gate already classifies it.

**What the probe corrected — the locator's DIRECTION.** The existing recursion machinery (`flowBodyWindow_descend`, `recseqentry_seqbracket_oracle`) goes TOP-DOWN: given a known outer window it descends INTO nested brackets (outer→inner). But the `provider` is quantified BOTTOM-UP — `∀ gated interior window [a,b), ∃ enclosing [loS,hiS)` — so it needs an INNER→OUTER locator: from an arbitrary interior position `a`, find its innermost enclosing opener. No such backward matching-open / enclosing scan exists in the codebase (`WellBracketed.lean` has the forward `flowBracketBalance_matching_close` and the bottom-of-stack `btFold_getLast?_preserved`, but nothing that locates where the current stack TOP was pushed). So the descent's residual is GENUINELY NEW infrastructure, not a reuse of the descend oracle — the 155th map's "no extra reconstruction" was about the TYPE (true), not the LOCATION (false: the location is the whole cost).

**The move this revision — factor the descent before authoring it.** Rather than write the descent as a monolith, extract the shared ASSEMBLE: `seqEnclosingFacts_provider_of_located (tokens a b loS hiS) (h_loS_a : loS ≤ a) (h_b_hiS : b ≤ hiS) (h_hiS : hiS ≤ size) (h_bal0 : flowBracketBalance tokens loS a = 0) (h_safe : SafeBodyUnit ContentStartTok ((take hiS).drop loS)) : ∃ loS hiS, …` — lift the locator's eventual output (the located enclosing `[loS,hiS)` + its windowed `SafeBodyUnit`) as hypotheses and discharge the provider's existential in ONE line via `seqEnclosingFacts_of_windowed_safebodyunit`. This is [[ref-parametric-assembler-extraction]] applied to the PRODUCER side (the consumer side was already factored by `seqInteriorSeparators_of_enclosing_provider`). The **root seed becomes a corollary** — `seqEnclosingFacts_provider_root` is now literally `seqEnclosingFacts_provider_of_located tokens a b 2 (size-2) … (seqRoot_safeBodyUnit …)`, making the sharing of the assembler between root and descent literal ([[ref-root-seed-discriminator-not-from-gate]]: root = the from-located assembler at the fixed root witness). The **descent becomes** "produce the located enclosing + its `SafeBodyUnit` for nested windows" = the inner→outer locator residual, now cleanly isolated with the trivial assemble removed.

**Why the assembler is not vacuous (de-risk, per [[ref-probe-provider-satisfiable-before-assembler]]).** The probe witnessed the lifted hypotheses SATISFIABLE on a NESTED window: `[3,6)` has a located enclosing (`loS=3,hiS=6`) with all preconditions true and the inner seq's `SafeBodyUnit` available — so the assembler is real, the residual genuine, and the only owed piece is the locator. The locator's existence (the backward scan ran correctly on real output) de-risks that the residual is dischargeable; its DIRECTION tells us it is new infrastructure to build, not an oracle to reuse.

**What landed (commit forthcoming, axiom-clean `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`).** `seqEnclosingFacts_provider_of_located` in `SeqInteriorSeparators.lean`, and `seqEnclosingFacts_provider_root` rewritten as its corollary. Probe `SeqDescentLocatorProbe.lean` registered in `Tests.Guards`. Build green 562 jobs, frontier holds at 4.

### Reflection 309 — a backward locator mirrored from a forward one needs NO standalone backward-matching-open primitive (the strong induction recovers the matching opener inline + an existing pair-skip lemma jumps the matched block); and size the locator's DELIVERABLE to what the consumer actually reads — drop conclusions the assembler never consumes (here the Dyck floor)

The 156th-revision "Next step" set `(i'-b-backward-locator)` and, per R308, FEARED that the closer case "likely needs a NEW backward matching-OPEN companion of `flowBracketBalance_matching_close`" plus a floor conclusion `∀ i ∈ [p+1,a], balance (p+1) i ≥ 0`. Authoring the lemma — after de-risking on `[[1,2],9]` and the deeper `[[[1]],2]` — corrected BOTH fears.

**What landed (`flowBracketBalance_backward_open_locate`, ParserGrammableBase.lean, axiom-clean `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`).** `(tokens) (a) (h_a_sz : a ≤ tokens.size) (h_open : flowBracketBalance tokens 0 a ≥ 1) : ∃ p, p < a ∧ flowBracketDelta tokens[p]!.val = 1 ∧ flowBracketBalance tokens (p+1) a = 0`. A `Nat.strongRecOn` on `a` cases the last prefix token (index `a-1`): **opener** (`delta=+1`) → `p=a-1`, `balance a a = 0`; **neutral** (`delta=0`) → IH at `a-1`; **closer** (`delta=-1`) → IH at `a-1` to find the closer's own matching opener `p'`, then `flowBracketBalance_bracket_pair_skip` to get `balance 0 a = balance 0 p'`, then IH at `p'` to continue outward. Added `flowBracketDelta_le_one` (upper companion of `flowBracketDelta_ge_neg_one`) to pin the scanned delta to `{-1,0,1}`. Build green 564 jobs, frontier holds at 4.

**Correction 1 — the backward matching-open is FREE inside the strong induction, no new primitive.** The forward `flowBracketBalance_matching_close` uses a fuel `find`-scan; the backward direction does NOT need its mirror image. The `Nat.strongRecOn` on `a` recovers the closer's matching opener INLINE: at a closer at `a-1`, the IH at `a-1` already returns the innermost-open-at-`a-1` position, which IS that closer's matching opener `p'` (innermost open just before a close = the bracket the close matches). The matched block is then jumped by the EXISTING `flowBracketBalance_bracket_pair_skip` (`balance 0 a = balance 0 p'`), and a second IH at `p'` walks outward. So the recursion structure itself IS the backward matching-open — the feared standalone companion of `flowBracketBalance_matching_close` was never needed. Mirroring a locator backward sheds machinery rather than adding it ([[ref-near-leaf-mirror-sheds-machinery]], here on the matched-block-skip axis): the forward lemma scans for a *first return*; the backward lemma *descends through* matched blocks, which a strong induction does for free.

**Correction 2 — size the deliverable to the consumer, not to the forward lemma's symmetric shape.** Both the de-risk and the 156th map spec'd a floor conclusion `∀ i ∈ [p+1,a], balance (p+1) i ≥ 0` (the forward lemma has the symmetric `∀ i ∈ (k,j], balance lo i ≥ 1`). But the actual consumer — `seqEnclosingFacts_provider_of_located` — reads ONLY `loS ≤ a` and `flowBracketBalance tokens loS a = 0` (its `h_loS_a`/`h_bal0`); it never consumes a floor. The floor was the EXPENSIVE part (the closer case's floor-extension across the skipped block: nested `i ≤ p'` / `i ∈ (p',a-1]` / `i = a` sub-cases). Dropping it ≈ halved the proof and lost nothing the assembler needs. The locator's deliverable shape is set by what the FROM-LOCATED assembler CONSUMES ([[ref-from-located-assembler-direction]]: the assembler's hypotheses ARE the locator's exact contract), not by the forward lemma's conclusion-set or an early prediction. Authoring corrected the fear: the bridge needed NO induction at all — it is a two-line composition of two ALREADY-PROVEN lemmas.

Proof: case the fold; in the `some s` branch the mark forces `s ≠ []` (a non-empty stack has a head), `btFold_length` gives `(s.length : Int) = pbalance (tokens.toList.take a)`, `flowBracketBalance_eq_pbalance` gives `flowBracketBalance tokens 0 a = pbalance (tokens.toList.take a)`, and `s.length ≥ 1` ⇒ balance ≥ 1 by `omega`. **Correction — the metric equality was already proven; the "two counts diverge?" fear was a non-issue.** The structural metric (typed-stack length after the prefix) and the numeric metric (`flowBracketBalance tokens 0 a`) are NOT two independent counts that need reconciling: they are BOTH equal to `pbalance (tokens.toList.take a)` — the stack length by `btFold_length` (proved long ago), the balance by `flowBracketBalance_eq_pbalance`. `pbalance` is the SHARED SUBSTRATE through which they were already equated. The reason they cannot diverge is structural and uniform: every opener (`[` AND `{`) does TWO things in lockstep — `btStep` pushes exactly one stack element AND `flowBracketDelta` contributes exactly `+1` — so seq/map are counted identically by both metrics, and no per-step induction relating `btStep` to `flowBracketDelta` is needed (that induction is, in effect, `btFold_length` itself, which already exists). Transferable: when a brick looks like "bridge metric X (a structural/typed count) to metric Y (a numeric count) and they might count differently," FIRST look for an existing `length`/`count` lemma stated against EACH — if both reduce to a common substrate (here `pbalance`), the bridge is their composition, and the feared per-step reconciliation was already discharged when that substrate lemma was proved. Don't re-derive it. This sharpens [[ref-probe-deferred-universal-before-producing]] on the same axis R309 did (the de-risk is honestly pessimistic; authoring tests the real cost) but for METRIC UNIFICATION specifically: the probe should ask "is there already a count lemma for each metric?" not "do I need a new induction?"

Sizing a lemma to BOTH consumers costs nothing when the proof is blind to the value that distinguishes them — the dual of sizing a deliverable DOWN to the consumer ([[ref-backward-locator-mirrors-forward]] correction 2): here we size the hypothesis UP to the widest value the proof tolerates. ### Reflection 311 — a downstream consumer's de-risk can FALSIFY a deliberately-narrowed UPSTREAM deliverable: when a minimal pair shows the dropped conjunct is the discriminator AND it is independent of the producer's other outputs, restore it in the PRODUCER, not re-derive it at the consume site

The 158th-revision "Next step" set `(i'-b-locator-glue-opener-type)` and, per the standing de-risk discipline, FEARED only a structural-link subtlety — whether the located innermost opener `p` is the bracket whose push sits at the typed-stack TOP after `[0,a)` — and HOPED to "re-derive the floor HERE from global well-bracketedness, NOT reinstated in the locator (keep the locator sized to its OTHER consumer)." The minimal-pair probe corrected the fear in a sharper direction: the brick is **FALSE on the bare locator deliverable**, and the floor is **not re-derivable at the consume site** — it must go back into the producer.

**The minimal pair (`#guard`-backed, `SeqDescentLocatorProbe.lean §(N)`, on the emittable witness `[{}, ["9"]]`).** Tokens `0:SS 1:[ 2:{ 3:} 4:, 5:[ 6:"9" 7:] 8:] 9:SE`. At the gated window start `a = 6`, the backward locator's three BARE facts — `p < a`, `flowBracketDelta tokens[p]!.val = 1`, `flowBracketBalance tokens (p+1) a = 0` — are satisfied by BOTH `p = 5` (the true innermost `[`, a seq) AND `p = 2` (a spurious `{`, whose body `} , [` over `[3,6)` nets `-1 + 0 + 1 = 0`). The gate-top at `a = 6` is `some true` (the innermost open IS a `[`). So a brick consuming only the bare existential would conclude `tokens[2] = .flowSequenceStart` — FALSE, `tokens[2]` is a `{`. This is the [[ref-minimal-pair-extracts-the-gate]] move applied to a PRODUCER's deliverable: probe one concrete object for a holding witness AND a failing sibling, and the differing structural feature IS the discriminator — here the interior FLOOR `∀ i ∈ [p+1, a], flowBracketBalance tokens (p+1) i ≥ 0`: it holds at the single point for `p = 5` (`balance 6 6 = 0`) and is VIOLATED for `p = 2` (`balance 3 4 = -1`, the `}`).

**Why the floor must be restored in the PRODUCER, not the consumer (the correction over the 158th next-step's hope).** The floor is INDEPENDENT of the three delivered facts AND of the gate (the gate is about `a`'s stack-top, identical for both candidates). The ONLY source of innermost-ness is the locator's CONSTRUCTION (it scans backward to the *last* unmatched opener). This is the **dual of [[ref-backward-locator-mirrors-forward]] correction 2**: there the deliverable shape was set by the FIRST consumer's reads (size down); here a SECOND consumer's reads force restoring a conjunct (size up). The deliverable is sized to the UNION of consumers, and a de-risk that surfaces a new consumer can RE-OPEN a producer thought finished.

### Reflection 312 — a type-blind numeric invariant (the floor) cannot CREATE a typed fact (fold-definedness); it can only license its TRANSPORT across a frame boundary, and moving definedness from a verified LARGER context to a SMALLER sub-context needs the CONVERSE of the forward framing lemma, not the forward lemma itself

The 159th "Next step" set `(i'-b-locator-glue-opener-type)` and, per the de-risk discipline, predicted the HEAD-PRESERVATION route with a strong preference for **route (B)**: "prove `btFold (some [b]) interior = some [b]` from the floor (= the interior is `WellTyped`-relative-to-`[b]`, i.e. local-Dyck floor + balance-0), then `btFold_frame` extends `[b] ++ s_p → [b] ++ s_p`." Authoring corrected the route in a precise way: **the floor cannot prove `btFold (some [b]) interior = some [b]`** — and the fix is not the forward `btFold_frame` but its CONVERSE.

**Why route (B) as written is FALSE.** "Local-Dyck floor + balance-0 ⇒ `btFold (some [b]) interior = some [b]`" silently assumes the interior fold is even DEFINED (`= some _`). It need not be: the floor and balance are NUMERIC (`pbalance`/`flowBracketBalance`), and a numeric invariant is TYPE-BLIND. The interior `[ }` has `pbalance` prefixes `0,+1,0` (floor `≥ 0` ✓) and total `0` (balance ✓), yet `btFold (some []) [.flowSequenceStart, .flowMappingEnd] = none` — the `}` cannot pop the `[`. So no amount of floor/balance reasoning yields fold-definedness; definedness is a TYPED fact that only the real (well-typed) token stream supplies.

**Where definedness actually comes from, and the direction of transport.** The gate `(btFold (some []) (take a)).bind (·.head?) = some true` already forces `btFold (some []) (take a) = some S` — the whole-prefix fold IS defined, because it is the real stream. The brick must move that definedness DOWN to the interior sub-fold framed by `b :: s_p`. The existing `btFold_frame` runs the WRONG way (it lifts a proven SMALL fact UP to a larger frame); what is needed is its CONVERSE — **`btFold_frame_inv`**: if `btFold (some (s ++ extra)) l = some m'` (definedness in the LARGER context) and the absolute floor `0 ≤ s.length + pbalance (l.take k)` holds (the numeric guard that no pop reaches `extra`), then `btFold (some s) l = some m` and `m' = m ++ extra`. The floor LICENSES the transport (every pop the big fold makes targets a within-`l` push, never the frame, so the smaller fold replays the identical, defined decisions); the larger context SUPPLIES the truth. Applied with `s = []`, `extra = b :: s_p`: the interior fold from `[]` is defined, has length `0` (`btFold_length` + balance-0), hence `= []`, so the whole stack at `a` is `b :: s_p`, head `= b`, fixed by the gate to `true` ⇒ `tokens[p] = .flowSequenceStart`.

**The forward/converse split of responsibility ([[ref-converse-forward-invariant-asymmetry]] applied to framing).** `btFold_frame` (forward) needs NO numeric hypothesis — it just carries a proven small fold up. `btFold_frame_inv` (converse) needs the floor — because dropping frame elements can underflow unless the floor forbids it. A property and its converse over the same structure need DIFFERENT invariant strengths: forward is free, the converse is floor-guarded. The de-risk's route-(B) error was to expect the floor to do the FORWARD lemma's job (create the small fact), when the floor's real role is to license the CONVERSE (transport definedness down). De-risk route (A) (a bespoke `btFold_head?_preserved`) was also avoidable: the head is NOT preserved across the interior (a push mid-interior changes it), only RECOVERED at the end by balance-0 — which `btFold_frame_inv` captures uniformly without a head-specific primitive.

**What landed (axiom-clean).** `WellBracketed.lean`: `flowBracketDelta_eq_one_iff` (the only delta-`+1` tokens are the two openers), `btStep_frame_inv` (one-step converse, `0 ≤ s.length + delta` excludes popping into the frame), `btFold_frame_inv` (the fold converse, `[propext, Quot.sound]` — no `Classical.choice`), `btFold_some_prefix` (a defined fold's prefix is defined). `SeqInteriorSeparators.lean`: `seqOpenerType_of_located_and_gate` (`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`). The data fact was pre-confirmed by `SeqDescentLocatorProbe.lean` §(B)/§(N): the gate-top equals the FLOORED located opener's type at every gated window, including the R311 spurious-map minimal pair. Build green (567 jobs), frontier holds at 4.

### Reflection 313 — a de-risk for the forward-CLOSE brick surfaced that the gate `SeqTypedInterior` was FLOOR-BLIND, making the carrier FALSE on a valid witness; the predicted matching-close route was broken the same way (the floor from an opener cannot survive past its own enclosing close), and the single fix — adding the local Dyck floor to the gate — resolves BOTH

The 160th "Next step" set `(i'-b-locator-glue-close)`: locate the matching close `hiS` of the now-typed opener `p` via `flowBracketBalance_matching_close`, predicting base `k = p` over `[p, tokens.size)` with "the Dyck floor over `[p, size)` from global well-bracketedness." Per the de-risk discipline ([[ref-probe-deferred-universal-before-producing]]) I probed the route FIRST — and, as with R312, the prediction was wrong in a precise way, and the probe surfaced a DEEPER issue in the gate.

**Finding I — the predicted matching-close route is BROKEN.** The floor from an opener `p` CANNOT survive past `p`'s own enclosing close: a complete bracket value is depth-transparent, so once `p`'s enclosing bracket closes the running balance from `p` goes negative. On `[[1, 2], 9]` (`p = 2`, the inner `[`): `flowBracketBalance 2 11 = -1 ≠ 0` (`h_total` FAILS) and the floor dips to `-1` at `i = 10` (`h_dyck` FAILS). The matching-close locator's enclosing window CANNOT be `[p, size)`; it must be `[p, hi)` where `hi` is the **enclosing recursion window end** (balance `0`, floored) — which the recursion already carries. `#guard`: `balance 2 9 = 0`, floor over `[2, 9)` holds, and the locator then returns `j = 6` (the inner `]`). This is the R312 lesson restated for the close direction.

**Finding II (the deeper one) — the gate `SeqTypedInterior` was FLOOR-BLIND, so the carrier `SeqInteriorSeparators` was FALSE on a VALID witness.** Probing whether the matching close satisfies the consumer's `b ≤ hiS` exposed CROSS-SIBLING gated windows. On `[[1], [2]]` (two sibling inner seqs) the window `[3, 7)` — from inside the first inner seq to inside the second — is depth-`0`-balanced (`balance 3 7 = 0`) and seq-enclosed (`btFold`-top at `3` is `some true`), so it passes the bare TWO-conjunct gate; yet (i) its innermost enclosing seq is `[3, 4)` with close `4 < 7`, so `b ≤ hiS` is FALSE, and (ii) **`bodySuccFact [3, 7)` is outright FALSE** (`tokens[3] = "1"` is depth-`0`-complete but `tokens[4] = ]`, not a `.flowEntry`). So the carrier `SeqInteriorSeparators tokens 2 9` — which the root producer must deliver for this valid flow value — is FALSE as the gate was defined. This is exactly [[ref-probe-provider-head-blind-gate]] for a FLOOR-blind gate: a too-weak gate admits spurious windows the deliverable (`bodySuccFact`, an enclosing-seq provider) cannot inhabit ⇒ the carrier/provider is FALSE.

**The single fix resolves both.** Cross-sibling windows DIP below `0` (crossing the first sibling's close: `balance 3 5 = -1`), so the local-Dyck floor `∀ i, a ≤ i → i ≤ b → flowBracketBalance tokens a i ≥ 0` excludes EXACTLY them. A full enumeration on `[[1], [2]]` confirms `floored ⟹ bodySuccFact` at every gated window, and the three bodySuccFact-failing gated windows `{[3,7), [3,8), [4,8)}` are exactly the non-floored ones. Adding the floor as the gate's **third conjunct** (R313) makes the carrier TRUE; and the SAME floor discharges the consumer's `b ≤ hiS` for FREE (a window crossing the located opener's matching close `j` would have `balance a (j+1) < 0`, contradicting the floor at `j+1 ∈ [a,b]`). The floor is window-ABSOLUTE (keyed on `a,b` only), so the carrier stays a subset restriction ([[ref-window-absolute-gate-subset-restriction]]): it restricts to any `[a',b'] ⊆ [a,b]` by `flowBracketBalance` composition.

**Blast radius — one file (the carrier has no downstream consumer yet).** `SeqTypedInterior`/`SeqInteriorSeparators` are confined to `SeqInteriorSeparators.lean` (elsewhere only IMPORTED). Repairs: `flowBracketBalance_pos_of_seqTypedInterior` reads the mark via `.2.1`; `seqTypedInterior_of_opener` takes the floor as a new hypothesis and supplies it as `.2.2` (at a genuine seq body the floor comes from `flowBracketBalance_interior_dyck` re-based to the body level — already in `ParserGrammableBase.lean`); the providers/root seed FORWARD the gate (never destructure it) so are untouched. This is the gate-domain dual of [[ref-downstream-derisk-restores-upstream]] (R311 restored a dropped *producer* conjunct; here the missing conjunct is in the *gate*).

**What landed (de-risk increment).** `SeqInteriorSeparators.lean`: the 3-conjunct `SeqTypedInterior`, the two repaired lemmas. `Tests/Guards/Proofs/SeqGateFloorProbe.lean`: `#guard`-backed evidence (the cross-sibling window passes the bare gate but fails `bodySuccFact`; `floored ⟹ bodySuccFact`; the bodySucc-failing set is exactly the non-floored set; the predicted `[p, size)` route's `h_total`/`h_dyck` both break). Build green (569 jobs), frontier holds at 4.

### Reflection 314 — the forward-CLOSE brick LANDED R313's prediction; the consumer's containment bound on a located matching-close is a TWO-FLOOR RELAY (a single underflow witness at `close+1`, refuted by whichever of two ADJACENT-domain floors tiles it), and the seq-specialized packaged locator already bundled matching-close + typed-close

R313 redirected `(i'-b-locator-glue-close)` and predicted its exact shape. This brick EXECUTED that prediction, sorry-free, with two refinements worth recording.

**The infra was less pessimistic than the route (echoes [[ref-metric-bridge-is-composition]] / [[ref-backward-locator-mirrors-forward]]).** The 161st "Next step" predicted invoking the GENERIC `flowBracketBalance_matching_close` and then `matching_close_typed_generic` SEPARATELY (matching-close, then close-type). But `flowBracketBalance_matching_close_seq` (WellBracketed.lean) already PACKAGES both: fed `lo`, `k := p`, the enclosing total `balance lo hi = 0`, the window Dyck floor, the opener type `tokens[p]! = .flowSequenceStart`, and `WellTyped` of the enclosing slice, it returns `j` with `p < j < hi`, `balance (p+1) j = 0`, AND `tokens[j]! = .flowSequenceEnd` in one call. So the brick used base `lo` directly (no re-basing to `p`, no `flowBracketBalance_dyck_shift` — the window floor IS the matching-close `h_dyck` verbatim) and read the close delta `-1` off the close TYPE. Search for the SPECIALIZED packaged lemma before composing the generic primitives the route names.

**The two containment bounds are a TWO-FLOOR RELAY — the real generalization of R313.** R313 said "the floor discharges `b ≤ hiS` for free." Executing it revealed the bound needs not one floor but a TILING by two adjacent-domain floors, refuting ONE underflow witness. The matching close at `j` makes the next step underflow for ANY base `β ≤ j`: `balance β (j+1) = balance β j + flowBracketDelta tokens[j]! = balance β j − 1`. The span the bound must reach, `[p+1, b]`, is tiled by two SEPARATELY-SOURCED floors — the locator floor over `[p+1, a]` and the GATE floor over `[a, b]`:

* `a ≤ j` — else `j+1 ≤ a`, so `j+1` lands in the LOCATOR floor's domain: `balance (p+1)(j+1) = balance (p+1) j − 1 = 0 − 1 = −1 < 0` contradicts `balance (p+1)(j+1) ≥ 0`.
* `b ≤ j` — else `j+1 ≤ b`, and (having `a ≤ j` ⇒ `a ≤ j+1`) `j+1` lands in the GATE floor's domain: `balance a (j+1) = balance a j − 1 = −1 < 0` (with `balance a j = 0` by composition `balance (p+1) j = balance (p+1) a + balance a j = 0 + balance a j`) contradicts `balance a (j+1) ≥ 0`.

So you do NOT need one unified floor over the whole span — two adjacent floors that tile it suffice, and you case-split on which domain `close+1` falls into. The first bound (`a ≤ j`) is the GUARD that lets the second floor's lower edge (`a ≤ j+1`) hold; the relay is ordered. This is the general mechanism behind R313's "for free" claim and applies wherever a located boundary's containment must reach across floors of different provenance ([[ref-two-floor-relay-close-bound]]).

**What landed.** `SeqInteriorSeparators.lean`: `seqClose_of_located_and_enclosing` (a b lo p hi) — lifts the enclosing window `[lo, hi)` facts (discriminator `balance lo p = 0`, total, window floor, `WellTyped`), the located-opener facts (`balance (p+1) a = 0`, locator floor over `[p+1, a]`), the opener type (from `seqOpenerType_of_located_and_gate`), and the GATE floor over `[a, b]`, and delivers `∃ hiS, a ≤ hiS ∧ b ≤ hiS ∧ hiS ≤ size ∧ balance (p+1) hiS = 0 ∧ tokens[hiS]! = .flowSequenceEnd` — the exact shape `seqEnclosingFacts_provider_of_located` consumes (`hiS = j`, `loS = p+1`, the body slice `[p+1, j)` feeding brick (4)). `(i'-b-child-safebodyunit)`, brick (4) of the seq descent. The 162nd "Next step" predicted reading how `seqRoot_safeBodyUnit` obtains the outer window's `SafeBodyUnit` from emission and asked whether the SAME slice path applies at a nested child. The answer is **no, and it does not need to** — the root and the child take DIFFERENT routes, and the child's is strictly simpler ([[ref-near-leaf-mirror-sheds-machinery]]: the locate boundary's PRODUCER-side simplification).

**The root and the child diverge.** `seqRoot_safeBodyUnit` is whole-stream specific: it replays the open-bracket → body → close-bracket scan chain from the concrete `h_scan : scanFiltered ("[" ++ emitList items ++ "]") = .ok tokens`, feeds the body through the recursive producer `emitList_body_recseqbody`, and projects the resulting `RecSeqBody` through the literal slice identity `h_take_eq`. None of that transfers to a nested child located by the descent (there is no per-child `h_scan`). The child instead rides the EXISTING seq-bracket oracle `recseqentry_seqbracket_oracle` (NonemptyStructure.lean:3861), which already packages the descend: from the enclosing `FlowBodyWindow`/`FlowBodyContentDeep`/`FlowBodyContent` `[p, hi)` with head opener `tokens[p] = .flowSequenceStart` and the width-recursion IH, fed the close facts, it reconstructs the interior window guards (via `flowBracketBalance_compose` + `flowBodyContentDeep_descend`), runs the IH on `[p+1, j)`, and returns `RecSeqBody ((take j).drop (p+1))` as its FIRST conjunct (the second is the trailing separator, brick (3)'s concern). `RecSeqBody.toSafeBodyUnit` projects that to the windowed `SafeBodyUnit ContentStartTok` verbatim.

**So brick (4) is a one-liner** — `(oracle … j h_pj h_jhi h_jclose h_inner h_floor).1.toSafeBodyUnit`. The thinness is the point: the brick NAMES the deliverable `seqEnclosingFacts_provider_of_located` consumes, isolating the oracle invocation, and pushes the genuine work into brick (5) (instantiate the IH; supply `j` + the floor).

**What the de-risk actually sharpened: the oracle's witness-dependent input is the interior floor `≥ 1`, not `≥ 0`.** Brick (3)'s `flowBracketBalance_matching_close_seq` returns only `balance (p+1) j = 0` + the typed close — it DROPS the interior floor (the seq-specialized locator's economy). But the oracle requires `∀ i ∈ (p, j], balance p i ≥ 1` (the matched-bracket depth floor, `≥ 1` because the opener at `p` pushes the running balance to `1` and the interior never returns to `0` until the close). This is the GENERIC `flowBracketBalance_matching_close`'s output, not the seq-specialized one's. The probe (`Tests/Guards/Proofs/SeqChildSafeBodyProbe.lean`) confirms on `[[1, 2], 9]` (`p = 2`, `j = 6`: `balance 2 3 = 1`, floor `≥ 1` over `(2, 6]`) and `[[1], [2]]` (both inner seqs) that this floor holds — so the wrapper is not vacuous ([[ref-probe-provider-satisfiable-before-assembler]]). The lesson for brick (5): it must source `j` + the interior floor from the GENERIC matching-close locator (the floor `≥ 1`), not from brick (3)'s packaged seq locator — the two locators feed DIFFERENT consumers (brick (3) the bounds, brick (4) the oracle), and the floor distinguishes them.

**The genuinely new lesson: bypass-vs-restore for a sized-down intermediate brick.** Brick (3) `seqClose_of_located_and_enclosing` was sized DOWN to ITS consumer (the provider's bounds + typed close) and DROPPED both `j < hi` and the interior floor `≥ 1` that the child-`SafeBodyUnit` consumer needs (R315). **The de-risk finding — the carrier is on Route A's critical path, and R317's re-derivation is circular.** Reading the full consumer chain settled three things the prior maps had left tangled:
1. **`SeqInteriorSeparators` IS on the path to the frontier sorry.** The sorry `FlowSubrangesOk tokens` is discharged by `flowSubrangesOk_of_window_producers` (Route A — fully assembled), which consumes the per-window `RecSeqBody` producer. That producer's `windowWidth_strongRecOn` step needs, per window, a `FlowBodyContent` to drive `recseqentry_window_dispatch`. `flowBodyContent_of_deep` builds `FlowBodyContent` from the deep guard PLUS the two separator facts (`bodySucc` / `noTrailingSep`) — and **those separator facts are exactly what `SeqInteriorSeparators` carries** (instantiate at `a = lo`, `b = hi`). So the carrier supplies the one content field the deep guard cannot project (R296's "no all-depth balance-free form" fact). `SeqInteriorSeparators` is not a parallel exploration — it is the separator-fact source for B3.
2. **B1 is the trivial alias `RecSeqBody.toSafeBodyUnit`** — confirmed: the recursion's `P := RecSeqBody ((take hi).drop lo)` (the oracle's IH and conclusion slice) maps by `RecSeqBody.toSafeBodyUnit` straight onto the dispatcher's `h_safe : SafeBodyUnit ContentStartTok ((take hi).drop lo)`, no new slice lemma. So B1 carries zero proof content.
3. **R317's re-derive-per-window is CIRCULAR.** R317 resolved the `G`-conjunct-vs-re-derive question in favour of re-deriving `SeqInteriorSeparators` per window via the dispatcher. But at a DESCENDED window the dispatcher's `h_safe` (the window's own `SafeBodyUnit`) has only one source — `RecSeqBody.toSafeBodyUnit` of that window's own `RecSeqBody` — which is **precisely the recursion's output the B3 step is producing**. A step that needs its own output to run does not exist. The trivial B1 alias only ever fed this circular route.

**The correct architecture — narrow-from-root.** `SeqInteriorSeparators` is a SUBSET RESTRICTION (`SeqInteriorSeparators_narrow`: its quantifier body is `lo`/`hi`-free except through the domain bounds). So establish it ONCE at the outer span `[2, size-2)` and let `narrow` lift it to every B3 sub-window `[lo,hi) ⊆ [2, size-2)` for free. At the ROOT the `SafeBodyUnit` is **flat** — `seqRoot_safeBodyUnit`, scanned off emission, with no `RecSeqBody` involved — so the dispatcher is invoked exactly once, here, with no circularity. The B3 recursion then reads its per-window separator facts off the narrowed carrier (an ambient hypothesis), never re-invoking the dispatcher. B1 is unneeded; R317's `G`-conjunct/re-derive dichotomy is superseded by "establish-once-and-narrow" (neither horn).

**The generalizable trap.** A per-window re-derivation of a subset-restriction carrier is circular exactly when the per-window input is sourced from the recursion's own output. The fix is structural, not a stronger invariant: source the carrier at the ROOT from the FLAT (non-recursive) producer, then narrow down — the flat producer breaks the cycle because it does not depend on the recursion. This sharpens [[ref-window-absolute-gate-subset-restriction]] (the root seed is costly, the edges free — here the edge is `narrow` and the root is the flat dispatcher seed) and applies [[ref-universal-producer-root-seed-first]] (the root seed is the first landable brick) with a circularity-detection rider. **The genuinely-new finding — the PUSH/FRAME edge asymmetry.** `SeqEnclosed tokens lo := (btFold (some []) (take lo)).bind (·.head?) = some true` reads the TOP of the typed bracket stack. Its two recursion edges depend on the parent's top in OPPOSITE ways:

### Reflection 322 — the B3-fixpoint de-risk found the IH-re-versioning is BLOCKED by import direction (the IH-supplying oracle is UPSTREAM of the guard it must thread), forcing PARAMETRICITY over an abstract guard `Q` rather than the de-risk's planned in-place edit

`(i'-b-B3-fixpoint)`, sub-brick 1. The 169th "Next step" authorized the B3-fixpoint with a mandatory FIRST de-risk: read `recseqentry_window_dispatch` (5006) and `recseqentry_seqbracket_oracle` (3861), confirm the IH-re-versioning (2-conjunct → 3-conjunct, adding `SeqEnclosed lo'`) is a LOCAL edit, then author the fixpoint. The de-risk **overturned its own premise**: the in-place edit (option A) is impossible.

**The de-risk finding (the import blocker).** Option A — "edit the oracle's IH type in place to add `→ SeqEnclosed tokens lo'`" — requires the oracle to NAME `SeqEnclosed`. But `recseqentry_seqbracket_oracle` and `recseqentry_window_dispatch` live in `NonemptyStructure.lean`, and `SeqEnclosed` lives in `SeqInteriorSeparators.lean`, which `import`s `NonemptyStructure` (verified: `SeqInteriorSeparators.lean:5`). The oracle is strictly UPSTREAM of the guard it must thread — it cannot reference it without an import cycle. Worse, even the downstream `seqChild_safeBodyUnit` (SeqInteriorSeparators:586) sits BEFORE `SeqEnclosed`'s own definition (1089) in the same file, so define-before-use forbids it too. Option B (adapt a 3-conjunct producer DOWN to the unchanged oracle's 2-conjunct IH slot by dropping `SeqEnclosed`) is also impossible: the oracle's lone IH call at `(lo+1, j)` genuinely NEEDS `SeqEnclosed (lo+1)`, and a 2-conjunct adapter closure cannot reconstruct it (the closure is typed for a general `lo'`, cannot assume `lo' = lo+1`, and `FlowBodyWindow lo' hi'` carries no prefix-stack fact). So neither option the 169th map enumerated survives contact with the import graph.

**The resolution — import-forced parametricity.** Make the ENTIRE IH-threading chain parametric over an abstract predicate `Q : Nat → Prop` on the window-start, taking the descend output `Q (lo+1)` as an OPAQUE hypothesis; bind the concrete guard `Q := SeqEnclosed tokens` only at the downstream fixpoint (which comes after `SeqEnclosed`'s definition, so it CAN name it). The import boundary that blocks the naive edit is exactly what parametricity satisfies: the upstream oracle never learns what `Q` is, it just transports `Q (lo+1)` into the recursive call.

**What landed (one green sub-increment — the IH interface fix).** Four lemmas re-versioned from a 2-conjunct IH to a `Q`-parametric 3-conjunct IH:
- `recseqentry_seqbracket_oracle` (NonemptyStructure): `+ (Q : Nat → Prop) (h_q_succ : Q (lo + 1))`; IH gains `→ Q lo'`; the single IH call supplies `h_q_succ` verbatim.
- `recseqentry_window_dispatch` (NonemptyStructure): `+ (Q : Nat → Prop) (h_q_descend : tokens[lo]!.val = .flowSequenceStart → Q (lo + 1))`; IH 3-conjunct; the seq-bracket branch feeds the oracle `Q` and `h_q_descend h_open`. The scalar/map branches (which never call the IH) are untouched — confirming the de-risk's only correct prediction (only the seq-bracket branch consumes the IH).
- `seqChild_safeBodyUnit` / `seqDescent_provider_of_located` (SeqInteriorSeparators): thread `Q + h_q_succ` through to the oracle. Kept parametric (NOT instantiated to `SeqEnclosed`) precisely because both sit before line 1089.

All four remain verified-but-unconsumed and axiom-clean `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`; build green (579 jobs); frontier holds at 4 pre-existing sorries (now NonemptyStructure.lean:6614/6855 + EmitterScannability.lean:833/873, line numbers shifted by the added params). `seqRoot_seqInteriorSeparators` (which takes `desc` as a lifted hypothesis, no IH) is UNCHANGED.

**The transferable nugget → NEW memory [[ref-import-forced-parametric-guard]]** with paired demo `Tests/Reflections/ImportForcedParametricGuard.lean`: when a recursion guard must be threaded through an IH-supplying lemma that lives UPSTREAM of the guard's definition (import order forbids naming it), do NOT move the guard up or edit the lemma to name it — make the upstream lemma PARAMETRIC over an abstract predicate `Q` on the recursion variable, taking the guard's descend-preservation output `Q (succ)` as an opaque hypothesis, and bind the concrete guard only at the downstream fixpoint. ### Reflection 323 — the B3-fixpoint LANDED, but the de-risk found the no-trailing-separator obligation the 170th map MISSED: the three-conjunct `G` + carrier cannot prove `m + 1 < hi`, because `noTrailingSepFact` is a VACUOUSLY-PROVEN POSITIVE that is consistent with the very trailing-comma window it was meant to forbid; the recursion's window-END invariant had to be threaded as a fourth `G`-conjunct

`(i'-b-B3-fixpoint)`, sub-brick 2 — the LAST seq producer brick. `seqWindowRecSeqBody` is authored and green. The step composition the 170th map predicted held verbatim: `seqWindow_flowBodyContent` (R320) projects the carrier to `FlowBodyContent`; `recseqentry_window_dispatch` (R322, `Q := SeqEnclosed tokens`, `h_q_descend := seqEnclosed_descend`) classifies the first entry; the IH adapter re-packages the `G` conjuncts; `recseqbody_window_assemble` (3121) folds the first entry with the advance tail (IH at `[m+1, hi)`), the tail guard rebuilt by `flowBodyWindow_advance` / `flowBodyContentDeep_advance` / `seqEnclosed_advance`. The advance-tail `WellTyped` segment `[lo, m+1)` (the discharge the map flagged) fell out of `WellTyped_subrange` over `h_win.wellTyped` with `balance lo (m+1) = 0` (the depth-`0` comma has delta `0`) — no new lemma.

**The de-risk finding (the obligation the 170th map missed).** The map's enumerated open obligations were the `Q`-adapter (trivial), the `desc`-closing `SeqEnclosed p` (deferred to the NEXT step), and the advance-tail `WellTyped` (above). It MISSED a fourth: the assembler's advance branch needs `m + 1 < hi` — there must be NO trailing separator, else the tail oracle demands `RecSeqBody []`, which is uninhabited. A draft with only `m + 1 < hi` left as `sorry` confirmed it is the SOLE remaining gap (everything else compiled).

**Why the carrier cannot close it.** The intuition was "the carrier's `noTrailingSepFact` forbids trailing commas." It does not — not in a usable form. `noTrailingSepFact tokens lo hi` is `∀ k, k+1=hi → tokens[k]=.flowEntry → balance lo k = 0 → isFlowContentStart tokens[hi]`. Its conclusion is a POSITIVE (`isFlowContentStart tokens[hi]`), proven VACUOUSLY at the root (`SafeBodyUnit_array_last_not_sep_window` refutes the premise — no trailing comma exists). But a vacuously-true `prem → pos` hands the CONSUMER only `pos`, never the refutation of `prem`. And `isFlowContentStart tokens[hi]` is CONSISTENT with the bad case: the three-conjunct `G` (balanced + Dyck + seq-enclosed) genuinely ADMITS a trailing-comma window `[a ,]` whose `tokens[hi]` is content — both `FlowBodyContentDeep` (whose `feContentStart` is gated `k+1 < hi`, vacuous at the boundary) and the carrier hold on it. So `G` + carrier provably cannot exclude `m + 1 = hi`. The recursion in fact maintains "`hi` is the enclosing close" as an invariant `G` never carried (root: `tokens[size-2] = ]`; descend: the oracle's located `tokens[j] = ]`; advance: `hi` inherited).

**The resolution — thread the window-END classifier as the fourth `G`-conjunct.** Add `tokens[hi]! = .flowSequenceEnd` to `G` and to the producer's signature. This is a CONCRETE (core-expressible, NOT import-blocked) predicate, so unlike R322's `Q` it needs no parametrization — but it must still reach the leaf producer through the same IH chain, so it is a one-conjunct EXTENSION of the R322 plumbing: the four IH-carriers (`recseqentry_seqbracket_oracle`, `recseqentry_window_dispatch`, `seqChild_safeBodyUnit`, `seqDescent_provider_of_located`) each gain `→ tokens[hi']! = .flowSequenceEnd` in their IH; the ONLY body change is the oracle's lone IH call, which supplies it from its already-located `h_close : tokens[j]! = .flowSequenceEnd`. At a trailing comma the boundary `feContentStart` then yields `isFlowContentStart tokens[hi]`, which now CONTRADICTS the fourth conjunct — closing `m + 1 < hi` by `simp [isFlowContentStart]`.

**What landed (one green sub-increment).** `seqWindowRecSeqBody` (SeqInteriorSeparators, after `seqWindow_flowBodyContent`) with the four-conjunct `G` and the extra hypothesis `h_close0 : tokens[hi]! = .flowSequenceEnd`. The four IH-carriers re-versioned (oracle body +1 arg; the other three type-only forwards). Build green (580 jobs); frontier holds at 4 pre-existing sorries (NonemptyStructure.lean:6616/6857 + EmitterScannability.lean:833/873); `seqWindowRecSeqBody` / `recseqentry_window_dispatch` / `seqDescent_provider_of_located` axiom-clean `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.

**The transferable nugget → NEW memory [[ref-vacuous-positive-cannot-exclude]]** with paired demo `Tests/Reflections/VacuousPositiveCannotExclude.lean`: a guard/carrier fact of shape `prem → pos` that is proven VACUOUSLY (its premise refuted internally) gives the consumer ONLY `pos`, never `¬ prem` — so it cannot EXCLUDE `prem` downstream when `pos` is consistent with the `prem`-case. If a consumer must rule out `prem`, do not lean on the vacuous positive; thread a DISCRIMINATOR that directly contradicts `pos`. Here the discriminator is the recursion's window-END invariant (`tokens[hi]` is the enclosing close, not content), made an explicit `G`-conjunct because the guard silently assumed it. Sharpens [[ref-probe-deferred-universal-before-producing]] (a draft-`sorry` on the suspected obligation surfaced the gap the map narrative hid) and [[ref-downstream-derisk-restores-upstream]] (a later consumer's de-risk re-opens a deliverable sized to an earlier one — here the window-END invariant restored into the guard/IH-thread, not the producer body).

**The de-risk finding — the obligation is `SeqEnclosed (p+1)`, not `SeqEnclosed p`.** The 171st (and 169th/170th) maps all flagged "the `desc` needs `SeqEnclosed p` at the located opener `p`, derivable from the gate's enclosure conjunct or threaded." Reading the actual consumer settled it: `seqDescent_provider_of_located` takes `Q : Nat → Prop` with seed `h_q_succ : Q (p+1)` (the enclosing seq BODY starts at `p+1`, so the IH and its seed read the POST-opener stack-top). **The `+1` form reconstructs in place — owing nothing threaded.** `SeqEnclosed (p+1)` is a [[ref-prefix-gate-reconstructed-from-boundary]] reconstruction (a second application): the gate's `btFold`-top `= some true` after `[0,a)` makes the whole `take a` fold `some S`, so its prefix `take p` folds to `some s` (`btFold_some_prefix`); the located opener is a `.flowSequenceStart` (`seqOpenerType_of_located_and_gate`, R312, from the same gate + the locator floor); and a `.flowSequenceStart` pushes `true` (`enclosingMark_true_of_opener`, R-prefix-gate) — exactly `SeqEnclosed (p+1)`. So the lemma's inputs are precisely the four locator outputs (`seqEnclosingOpener_of_gate`, R319) + the gate's mark, all already in scope at the `desc` discharge. **No `SeqEnclosed p` threaded as a locator output, no stronger invariant.** The general lesson (sharpening [[ref-reconstruct-in-place-over-relocate]] + [[ref-prefix-gate-reconstructed-from-boundary]]): before threading a pre-boundary invariant `X` down a recursion, check which side of the boundary the consumer READS — a consumer of the post-boundary state owes the SHIFTED `X(q+1)`, which the boundary token alone reconstructs, dissolving the threaded-`X(q)` obligation. ### Reflection 327 — the B2b authoring de-risk OVERTURNED R326 (as R326 overturned R325): the carrier-free `seqWindowRecSeqBody` compiles with EXACTLY ONE unfillable `sorry` — the IH adapter's `FlowBodyContent tokens lo' hi'`, whose sole missing field is `bodySucc`, a NON-restriction-across-descend fact that is ALSO a projection of the very deliverable it gates ⇒ unmanufacturable at the adapter AND regressive at the descend edge; `h_root_carrier` is STRUCTURALLY NECESSARY and the real break is to discharge the carrier's `desc` from EMISSION, not to drop the carrier

`(i'-b-B2b-fc-thread, authoring)` — executed the mandated FIRST de-risk (the carrier-free authoring draft) and it corrected the plan for the THIRD consecutive revision. No new lemma landed (the de-risk INVALIDATED the planned one); probe reverted, build green at the 4 pre-existing frontier sorries.

**The empirical de-risk.** Per the 174th map I dropped `h_root_carrier` from `seqWindowRecSeqBody`, added `FlowBodyContent tokens lo hi` as the FIFTH `G`-conjunct (and a fifth signature hypothesis `h_content0`), read `h_content` off `G`, and supplied the extra conjunct at the two VISIBLE IH call sites — ADVANCE via `flowBodyContent_advance` (no IH, pure re-basing) and the ROOT `key` application via `h_content0`. Result (targeted build): the ENTIRE recursion type-checks with EXACTLY ONE new `sorry` — the dispatch's IH adapter `fun lo' hi' h_lt h_w h_d h_q h_c => ih lo' hi' h_lt ⟨h_w, h_d, h_q, h_c, (sorry : FlowBodyContent tokens lo' hi')⟩`. So the residual is pinpointed to ONE term: `FlowBodyContent tokens lo' hi'` in a context holding only `(FlowBodyWindow, FlowBodyContentDeep, Q, close)` at an ARBITRARY sub-window `[lo', hi')`.

**Why that `sorry` is unfillable (the structural finding).** Reading the two structures settles it: `FlowBodyContent` has three fields — `headContentStart`, `bodySucc`, `feContentStart` — and `FlowBodyContentDeep` carries `headContentStart` (identical) + `openerContentStart` + an all-depth `feContentStart` (of which `FlowBodyContent.feContentStart` is the depth-`0` projection). So given `h_d : FlowBodyContentDeep`, the ONLY field of `FlowBodyContent lo' hi'` not already in hand is **`bodySucc`** — the depth-`0` separator well-formedness ("every depth-`0` non-separator position is followed by a separator or the close"), i.e. "the body is properly comma-separated". `bodySucc lo' hi'` at a sub-window comes ONLY from that window's OWN `RecSeqBody` (R325 `seqSeparatorFacts_of_recseqbody` ▸ `RecSeqBody.toSafeBodyUnit`) — which is the IH OUTPUT `ih lo' hi' …`. Supplying it as the IH INPUT is a literal regress (`ih`'s 5-conjunct `G` needs `FlowBodyContent lo' hi'` to PRODUCE `RecSeqBody lo' hi'`, but `FlowBodyContent lo' hi'`'s `bodySucc` needs `RecSeqBody lo' hi'`). **R326's `flowBodyContent_descend` cannot break it:** it too obtains the child `bodySucc` via `seqChild_safeBodyUnit` → `recseqentry_seqbracket_oracle` → the oracle's `h_ih (lo+1) j` call (NonemptyStructure:3918); under a 5-conjunct IH that call ALSO needs `FlowBodyContent (lo+1) j` = exactly what `flowBodyContent_descend` is producing — the SAME-window regress, now inside the oracle (and `flowBodyContent_descend` lives DOWNSTREAM of the oracle, so the oracle cannot even call it — the [[ref-import-forced-parametric-guard]] wall compounds the regress). The "produce the child `RecSeqBody` once and reuse" fallback the 174th map floated does NOT help: it only avoids DOUBLE production, never the need for child `bodySucc` BEFORE the child `RecSeqBody` exists.

**The classification (why this is a genuinely new shape).** `bodySucc` is the WORST kind of guard field: it is BOTH (i) a NON-restriction across descend (R296 — no depth-`0` parent fact restricts to the child's depth-`0`, since the child's depth-`0` is the parent's depth-`1`), AND (ii) a PROJECTION of the very deliverable it gates (the child's `bodySucc` ⟺ the child's `RecSeqBody`). Property (ii) is what defeats the [[ref-non-restriction-residual-root-seed]] escape: a plain non-restriction field can be ROOT-SEEDED and re-scoped as a bracket-type-context problem, but a field that needs the deliverable cannot be seeded as a `G`-conjunct at ALL — seeding it at the root still leaves every descended window needing its own copy, and that copy needs the descended deliverable. So `FlowBodyContent`/`bodySucc` is a [[ref-push-blind-frame-dependent]] FRAME-DEPENDENT edge whose frame CANNOT supply it — it is a global EMISSION-traceable precondition the producer must CONSUME, never thread, never produce. `h_root_carrier` (or an emission-global equivalent) is therefore STRUCTURALLY NECESSARY. R325's "clean strengthening, drop the carrier" and R326's "thread `FlowBodyContent` through `G`" are both FALSE; their lemmas (`seqSeparatorFacts_of_recseqbody`, `flowBodyContent_descend`) remain TRUE and axiom-clean but are SUPERSEDED on this path (kept as verified-but-unconsumed).

**The corrected architecture — keep the carrier, discharge `desc` from EMISSION.** The carrier↔producer circularity (carrier ⇐ `desc` ⇐ `seqWindowRecSeqBody` ⇐ carrier) is NOT broken by removing the carrier from the producer. It is broken by removing the PRODUCER from `desc`: discharge `seqRoot_seqInteriorSeparators`'s `desc` (the nested-window enclosing facts) from the recursive EMISSION characterization (`emitList_body_recseqbody` / `EmitScansInFlowRecEntry`, NonemptyStructure:909/890 — `seqRoot_safeBodyUnit` already extracts the ROOT body `RecSeqBody` straight off emission, and `RecSeqBody` is recursive, so it CONTAINS every nested seq entry's `RecSeqBody`). Projecting that root emission `RecSeqBody` to a located nested gated window yields the window's `bodySucc`/`noTrailingSep` WITHOUT invoking the token-recursion — so `desc` no longer calls `seqWindowRecSeqBody`, the circularity dissolves, and `seqWindowRecSeqBody` KEEPS `h_root_carrier` (the global `bodySucc` source it provably needs). The producer-with-carrier then feeds `flowSubrangesOk_of_window_producers` → `FlowSubrangesOk tokens` (NonemptyStructure:6616) → `flow_parser_ok_of_structure` → `ParseNodeFlowSeqOk` → `universal_roundtrip`.

**The general lesson (sharpening [[ref-push-blind-frame-dependent]] + [[ref-non-restriction-residual-root-seed]] + [[ref-converse-forward-invariant-asymmetry]]).** Before threading a guard field through a width recursion, classify it on TWO axes: (a) does it RESTRICT across descend? and (b) is it a PROJECTION of the deliverable the recursion produces? A field that fails BOTH (non-restricting AND deliverable-projecting) cannot be a `G`-conjunct under ANY seeding — its descended copy needs the descended deliverable, so the IH adapter cannot manufacture it and any descend edge regresses at the producer's own IH call. Such a field must be sourced GLOBALLY (a carrier / emission precondition the producer consumes). The cheap, decisive probe: author the carrier-free producer with the field as a `G`-conjunct, supply it at the visible (advance/root) IH sites, and read the residual `sorry` — if it is exactly that field at an arbitrary sub-window, the field is deliverable-projecting and the carrier is necessary. A type-level de-risk that lands a strictly-stronger lemma (R325) certifies the LEMMA, not the architecture; and a descend edge that "exists as a theorem" (R326 `flowBodyContent_descend`) is not the same as a descend edge that can be CALLED inside the producer's own recursion — consuming the IH means it cannot supply that IH's precondition.

### Reflection 330 — the measure/offset-rebasing de-risk RESOLVES to "trivial + standard": measure is `body.length` (structural recursion is impossible — the extract leaf returns an OPAQUE `RecSeqBody`), `decreasing_by` is `omega`, re-basing is `List.take`/`drop`/`dropLast` — landed the three-witness `#guard` probe `SeqNestedProjectProbe` confirming all three recursion moves

`(i'-b-B2c-nested-project, authoring)` — the first and smallest sub-brick was to settle the recursion's well-founded measure and the per-descend offset re-basing, PROBING on the witnesses before authoring the fixpoint. Both resolved cleanly, and the probe landed as the green increment.

**Structural recursion is RULED OUT — so the measure is `body.length` with a trivial `decreasing_by`.** The recursion's terminal move calls `recseqentry_seq_extract` (a THEOREM) to read an entry's stored `h_rec : RecSeqBody interior`. Lean's structural-recursion checker sees that theorem's result as an OPAQUE new term, NOT a structural sub-term of the `RecSeqBody` argument — so the "structural mutual recursion on `RecSeqBody`/`RecSeqEntry`" option the 177th map floated as *preferred* cannot be used as written (it would require the extract to be inlined as a `cases` whose `h_rec'` binding is a field, but then the position↔structure matching — which `recseqentry_seq_extract` encapsulates — leaks into the recursion body). The clean form is `termination_by body.length`, `decreasing_by` discharging the two edges by `omega`: ADVANCE gives `rest.length < body.length` (from `body = e ++ fe :: rest`, `e ≠ []`); DESCEND gives `interior.length < e.length ≤ body.length` (from the entry shape `e = op :: (interior ++ [cl])`, `e.length = interior.length + 2`). Both are local list-length facts — **no span-length lemma is owed** (the 177th map's pessimistic branch does NOT fire).

**The offset re-basing is standard slice algebra — `List.take`/`drop`/`dropLast`.** The producer threads the invariant `body = (tokens.toList.take H).drop lo` (the body sits at token window `[lo, H)`). One peel of the head entry `e` (length `e.length`) gives `e = body.take e.length = (toList.take (lo + e.length)).drop lo`, its interior `(e.drop 1).dropLast = (toList.take (lo + e.length - 1)).drop (lo + 1)`, and the advance tail `rest = body.drop (e.length + 1) = (toList.take H).drop (lo + e.length + 1)`. Each is a fresh `(toList.take H').drop lo'` — the invariant re-establishes itself across both edges with no balance re-basing. The probe CONFIRMS this concretely: at every recursive step the located interior `(toList.take j).drop (p+1)` equals the slice reached by peeling the parent window `B := (toList.take H).drop lo` (`(B.take e.length).drop 1 |>.dropLast`), token-for-token (compared as `.map (·.val)` lists).

Per move the probe pins the measure decrease (each recursive call's slice strictly shorter), the offset re-basing (located interior = parent-window peel), and the entry selection (located opener at `flowBracketBalance = 0` from the active base). Build green (582 jobs, +1 module); frontier holds at 4 pre-existing sorries; the probe is `#guard`-only (no proof obligation, no sorry).

So the probe's job was the COMPLEMENT: once the form is fixed to `termination_by body.length`, the probe certifies the two value-level facts the `decreasing_by` and the slice plumbing rest on (lengths shrink, slices re-base) on representatives of every move — and confirms NO further lemma is owed before the (now mechanical) fixpoint authoring. Probe the values; read the types for the form.

### Reflection 331 — the DIRECT-HEAD leaf's crux is a TWO-SIDED floor uniqueness: the consumer's external floor and the entry's internal floor each forbid an early return from opposite sides of the boundary, pinning `j + 1 = lo + e.length` — extract the internal floor as a CONSTRUCTOR-BLIND lemma (vacuous on the degenerate shapes, so it needs no head hypothesis)

`(i'-b-B2c-nested-project, authoring — the fixpoint)`, SMALLEST sub-brick — author the DIRECT-HEAD base case (R330's `[[1,2],9]` move) as a standalone leaf. It landed sorry-free as `recseqbody_head_seq_project`, and surfaced a sharper-than-expected matching argument plus two environment gotchas.

**The match of a located close to a structural entry span is a TWO-SIDED floor uniqueness.** The leaf must show the located close `j` (handed in by the locator, per [[ref-reconstruct-in-place-over-relocate]] — reconstruct AT `j`, never re-locate) coincides with the head entry `e`'s own structural close, i.e. `j + 1 = lo + e.length`. The single located floor (`h_floor`, `flowBracketBalance lo · ≥ 1` over `(lo, j]`) is NOT enough — it pins `j` only from OUTSIDE (forbids the balance returning to 0 before `j`). The entry's WellBracketedness gives `balance lo (lo + e.length) = 0`, but `balance (lo+1) · = 0` holds at MANY interior cuts (between nested sub-entries), so that alone does not pin the structural close either. What closes it is the PAIR of opposing floors: the located floor forbids `balance lo (c+1) = 0` for a structural close `c < j` (would force `≥ 1` at `c+1`), and the entry's OWN interior floor (`balance lo i ≥ 1` strictly inside `e`) forbids `balance lo (j+1) = 0` for `j < c` — two `omega` contradictions on a `Nat.lt_trichotomy`. The consumer's floor and the producer's floor are the two jaws; neither jaw alone bites.

**The internal floor is a CONSTRUCTOR-BLIND lemma — no head hypothesis.** `recseqentry_opener_interior_floor` (`∀ m, 1 ≤ m → m < e.length → pbalance (e.take m) ≥ 1`) holds for ALL FOUR `RecSeqEntry` constructors with no opener-delta premise: `scalar` (range `1 ≤ m < 1` is vacuous), `seqEmpty` (the lone interior cut is `[op]`, balance `+1`), `seq`/`map` (opener `+1` + interior WellBracketed prefix `≥ 0`). Stating it head-free makes it a one-`cases` reusable brick the uniqueness consumes opaquely — the de-risk's instinct to thread a "head is an opener" hypothesis was unnecessary; the property is intrinsic to the entry grammar (a single bracket pair never returns to 0 before its own close). The leaf then `cases h_e` only AFTER uniqueness fixes `e.length = j + 1 - lo ≥ 3`, so `scalar`/`seqEmpty` fall to length and `map` to the `.flowSequenceStart` head — the stored `h_rec` is returned directly (no need to re-invoke `recseqentry_seq_extract`, since casing already exposes the interior), and `interior = (toList.take j).drop (lo+1)` is pure `drop_take`/`take_take`/`take_left` slice algebra.

**Two environment gotchas, both now encoded in the committed proof.** (1) `conv_lhs`/`conv_rhs` are UNAVAILABLE in this Mathlib-free setup (`unknown tactic`); a one-sided rewrite that must avoid looping on a self-referential equation (`e = … e.length …`) is done instead by `Eq.trans` with an auxiliary `have` whose goal has no bare `e`, or by `rw [h]` only where the rewritten variable does not recur in an index. (2) `cases h with | single ent …` on `RecSeqBody.single` does NOT bind `ent`: `single`'s index is its bare first arg (`… : RecSeqBody e`), so `cases` keeps the TARGET var `l` and discards the pattern name — refer to `l` for the single entry; `cons` (index `e ++ fe :: rest`, a compound) DOES introduce its pattern name. The asymmetry is a property of whether the constructor's index is a bare variable.

**What landed (one green sub-increment).** `recseqbody_head_seq_project` + `recseqentry_opener_interior_floor` + `recseqbody_head_entry` (NonemptyStructure.lean, after `recseqentry_seq_extract`), all sorry-free. Full build green (582 jobs); frontier holds at exactly 4 pre-existing sorries (NonemptyStructure 6865/7106, EmitterScannability 833/873). Verified-but-unconsumed leaf (R225): the recursion's ADVANCE/DESCEND arms will bottom out here.

**The general lesson (sharpening [[ref-two-floor-relay-close-bound]] + [[ref-reconstruct-in-place-over-relocate]]).** [[ref-two-floor-relay-close-bound]] tiled two ADJACENT-domain floors to bound a SINGLE underflow witness; this is its dual — two OPPOSING floors (external consumer + internal producer) across a single boundary pin a single EQUALITY (the matched close), each floor refuting the trichotomy branch on its own side. When a "match the handed-in witness to the structure" obligation looks like it needs a uniqueness/first-return primitive, check whether the witness already carries ONE floor (it usually does, from the locator) and the structure supplies the OTHER (intrinsically, constructor-blind) — then uniqueness is two `omega`s, no primitive. Reconstruct-in-place ([[ref-reconstruct-in-place-over-relocate]]) plus this two-jaw match is the whole base case.
