### Reflection 332 — the ADVANCE arm is a WINDOW-ABSOLUTE one-step re-basing: dispatch on `flowBracketBalance lo p` (not the head entry's internal `e.length`), source the separator's delta STRUCTURALLY from `h_fe` (not by indexing the token), and let the `single` case fold vacuously — the interior floor that pinned the leaf's close now excludes `p` from the head entry's interior

`(i'-b-B2c-nested-project, the recursion driver)`, SMALLEST sub-brick — author the ADVANCE arm (R330's `[1, [2, 3]]` advance-then-head move) as a standalone one-step brick. It landed sorry-free as `recseqbody_advance`, alongside the structural split `recseqbody_head_or_cons`.

**The dispatch condition is WINDOW-ABSOLUTE, keyed only on `flowBracketBalance lo p` — never the head entry's internal `e.length`.** The 179th map floated phrasing the ADVANCE guard as "`p` past the head entry `e`" (`p > e-close`), which references `e.length` — a quantity that only exists AFTER the head entry is extracted inside the proof, so it cannot be a hypothesis. The clean guard is `flowBracketBalance lo p = 0 ∧ lo < p`: a top-level position strictly past the body's head. The constructor-blind interior floor `recseqentry_opener_interior_floor` (R331) does double duty here — it pinned the leaf's close from inside, and now it EXCLUDES `p` from the head entry's interior (strictly inside ⇒ balance `≥ 1`, contra `= 0`), forcing `p ≥ lo + e.length` WITHOUT naming `e.length` in the signature. This applies [[ref-window-absolute-gate-subset-restriction]]: keep the guard window-absolute (`lo`, `p`, global balance), and the head-entry length enters only internally, derived not assumed.

**The separator's delta is sourced STRUCTURALLY from `h_fe`, never by extracting the token at `lo + e.length`.** To exclude `p = lo + e.length` (the separator position, balance also `0`), the discriminator is token TYPE: the separator is `.flowEntry` (`flowBracketDelta = 0`), `p` is `.flowSequenceStart` (`flowBracketDelta = +1`). The instinct is to index `tokens.toList[lo + e.length]` and show it equals the stored `fe` — a getElem-across-equation plumbing chore. The cheaper route: `h_fe : fe.val = .flowEntry` is ALREADY in hand from the `cons`, so `pbalance (e ++ [fe]) = pbalance e + flowBracketDelta fe.val = 0 + 0 = 0` gives `flowBracketBalance lo (lo + e.length + 1) = 0` by the bridge (a `take_append` slice identity), and then `p = lo + e.length` makes `flowBracketBalance lo (p+1)` simultaneously `0` (the structural separator balance) and `0 + 1` (the located opener delta) — `omega` contradiction. No token is ever indexed; `h_fe` is the whole discriminator. [[ref-reconstruct-in-place-over-relocate]]: reconstruct the needed fact AT the structural data you already hold, don't re-locate it positionally.

**The `single` case folds vacuously — the same floor excludes it.** `recseqbody_head_or_cons` returns `single` (window IS one entry) ∨ `cons` (`e ++ fe :: rest`). The ADVANCE guard `flowBracketBalance lo p = 0 ∧ lo < p` is unsatisfiable in `single`: the lone entry spans the whole window (`e.length = H - lo`), so `lo < p < H = lo + e.length` puts `p` strictly inside `e`, and the interior floor forces balance `≥ 1`, contra `= 0`. So the ADVANCE arm never has to *produce* anything for `single` — it discharges by `exact absurd`/`omega`, mirroring [[ref-threaded-guard-prunes-case-tree]] (a guard strong enough to make a deliverable shape unreachable). The brick's output preserves the dispatch invariant (`flowBracketBalance lo' p = 0`, `lo' ≤ p`) so the wrapping recursion re-enters ADVANCE (or DIRECT-HEAD at `lo' = p`) with the same shape one entry rightward.

Verified-but-unconsumed brick (R225): the recursion driver iterates this until `lo' = p` (DIRECT-HEAD).

**The general lesson (applying [[ref-window-absolute-gate-subset-restriction]] + [[ref-reconstruct-in-place-over-relocate]]).** Two instincts the ADVANCE arm makes you resist. First, phrasing the recursion's guard in terms of a quantity (`e.length`) that only exists after the recursion's own extraction — keep guards window-absolute (global balance + endpoints), and let the internal quantities be derived. Second, reaching for positional token extraction when a STORED structural fact (`h_fe`) already carries the discriminator — convert "what is the token at position `k`?" into "what does the structure say about the balance across `k`?", which the `pbalance`/`flowBracketDelta` algebra answers without a single getElem. Both shrink the arm from a plumbing exercise to a balance argument.

### Reflection 333 — the DESCEND arm's dispatch is a WINDOW-ABSOLUTE FLOOR (not a bare `balance ≥ 1`), head-is-`.seq` is an irreducible DISPATCH hypothesis (balance can't tell seq from map opener), and the head entry's close is read off its OWN structure (no located `j`) — excluded via the non-dependent `getElem?` API because `rewrite` under a dependent `getElem` proof fails the motive check

`(i'-b-B2c-nested-project, the DESCEND arm)`, the bracket-level-down mirror of `recseqbody_advance`. It landed sorry-free as `recseqbody_descend`, and corrected two pieces of the R332 map's framing plus surfaced a recurring environment gotcha.

**A bare `flowBracketBalance lo p ≥ 1` does NOT mean "p is inside the head entry" — the complement of the ADVANCE guard is a FLOOR, not a single balance value.** The R332 map proposed `flowBracketBalance lo p ≥ 1` as the DESCEND guard, by symmetry with the ADVANCE guard `flowBracketBalance lo p = 0`. But the symmetry is false: `balance lo p = 0 ∧ lo < p` IS sufficient for "p past the head" (the interior floor forbids a top-level return-to-`0` strictly inside the head, so `p ≥ lo + e.length`), whereas `balance lo p ≥ 1` is NOT sufficient for "p inside the head" — `p` can be nested inside a *later* entry of the body (e.g. `[1, [2, [3]]]` with `p` the innermost opener: `balance(root) p ≥ 1` but `p` is in the SECOND entry, not the scalar head `1`). The correct DESCEND guard is the window-absolute FLOOR `∀ i ∈ (lo, p], flowBracketBalance lo i ≥ 1` — the exact mirror of the leaf `recseqbody_head_seq_project`'s `h_floor`. It forbids the balance returning to `0` anywhere in `(lo, p]`, so `p` cannot be past the head entry (whose own close drops the balance to `0` at `lo + e.length ≤ p`, which the floor would forbid). One `Nat.lt_or_ge` + the constructor-blind interior floor (`recseqentry_opener_interior_floor`, R331) on the entry's own balance-to-`0` discharges `p < lo + e.length`. **This is the dispatch-completeness finding the driver must respect:** ADVANCE and DESCEND are NOT a `balance = 0 / balance ≥ 1` dichotomy — they split on whether `p < lo + e.length` (the floor holds) or `p ≥ lo + e.length` (the floor breaks, balance hits `0` at the head's close). R332's balance-`0` ADVANCE handles only the sub-case where `p` is itself at top level; the driver's general advance-past-a-completed-entry (when `p` is nested in a later entry) is a SEPARATE move the assembly must supply.

**Head-is-`.seq` is an irreducible DISPATCH hypothesis — balance cannot distinguish a seq opener from a map opener.** The R332 map hoped the `.map` head was "excluded structurally under `≥ 1` balance". It is not: a `.flowMappingStart` is an opener with `flowBracketDelta = +1` exactly like `.flowSequenceStart`, so the floor holds identically whether the head entry is a seq or a map containing a nested seq. The seq-vs-map decision is genuinely NOT a balance fact; it enters as the hypothesis `h_lo_open : tokens[lo]! = .flowSequenceStart` (mirroring the leaf's `h_open`). In the driver this is the SEQ branch of a head-type case split — a `.flowMappingStart` head routes to the map mirror (`rec_map_body_nested_project`), since the seq seed `seqRoot_recseqbody` carries `RecSeqBody` only in `RecSeqEntry.seq.h_rec` fields, never under a `.map` entry's `WellBracketed` interior. So `cases h_e` is clean: `scalar` falls to length (`p` strictly inside needs `≥ 2`), `seqEmpty`/the entry close at `p` is a `.flowSequenceEnd` (excluded by `h_p_open`), `map` contradicts `h_lo_open`, and `seq` returns the stored `h_rec` directly.

**The head entry's close is read off its OWN structure — no located `j`, no two-sided uniqueness.** The leaf matched a *handed-in* located close `j` to the head entry's span by a two-sided floor uniqueness (R331). The DESCEND arm needs none of that: it descends into the head entry's OWN interior, whose close is structurally `lo + e.length - 1` (the `cl` of `op :: (interior ++ [cl])`). The only obligation is `p < H'` (strictly before that close), discharged by `h_p_open` — `tokens[close]! = .flowSequenceEnd ≠ .flowSequenceStart`, so `p ≠ close`. **The environment gotcha:** extracting `tokens.toList[close] = cl` from the slice identity `interior ++ [cl] = (drop (lo+1)).take (interior.length+1)` by `rw [h_tail] at hidx` on a `hidx : (interior ++ [cl])[interior.length] = cl` FAILS — `rewrite` cannot abstract a `getElem` whose `i < l.length` proof depends on the rewritten list `l` (the motive is not type-correct). The fix is the non-dependent `getElem?` (`l[i]?`) API — `List.getElem?_take` / `List.getElem?_drop` / `List.getElem?_append_right` carry no proof argument, so the list rewrites cleanly, and `List.getElem?_eq_getElem` + `Option.some.inj` converts `l[i]? = some cl` back to `l[i] = cl`. (Also: `rw [getElem!_pos …, ← Array.getElem_toList]` to go from `tokens[i]!.val` down to `tokens.toList[i].val` — the FORWARD `Array.getElem_toList` runs the wrong way.)

**What landed (one green sub-increment).** `recseqbody_descend` (NonemptyStructure.lean, after `recseqbody_advance`), sorry-free. Full build green (582 jobs); frontier holds at exactly 4 pre-existing sorries (NonemptyStructure 7156/7397, EmitterScannability 833/873). Verified-but-unconsumed brick (R225): the recursion driver dispatches into this on a `.flowSequenceStart` head with `p` floored strictly inside.

**The general lesson (applying [[ref-window-absolute-gate-subset-restriction]] + [[ref-minimal-pair-extracts-the-gate]]).** When you build the "other arm" of a dispatch by symmetry, PROBE that the complement guard actually characterizes the complement set — here `balance ≥ 1` looked like the negation of the ADVANCE guard `balance = 0` but admits a whole class (`p` nested in a later entry) the arm cannot serve; the true guard is the FLOOR, the window-absolute encoding of "p in the head bracket" ([[ref-window-absolute-gate-subset-restriction]]). And when a discriminator (seq vs map) is provably NOT a function of the available numeric invariant (both openers share `flowBracketDelta = +1`), stop trying to derive it — name it as a dispatch hypothesis and let the caller's case split supply it. The `[1, [2, [3]]]` minimal example that refutes the `balance ≥ 1` guard is the [[ref-minimal-pair-extracts-the-gate]] move: one concrete object whose holding/failing sub-windows separate the proposed gate from the real one.

### Reflection 334 — the GENERAL ADVANCE arm is BALANCE-FREE once the head's `cons` decomposition is explicit: the structural dispatch `p ≥ lo + e.length` makes the whole balance machinery of `recseqbody_advance` evaporate, leaving only one opener-vs-separator inequality

`(i'-b-B2c-nested-project, the GENERAL ADVANCE move)`, the SMALLEST-FIRST sub-brick of the driver. It landed sorry-free as `recseqbody_advance_general`, and the finding is how much SIMPLER the right arm is than its R332 predecessor.

**R332's `recseqbody_advance` did its hardest work to DERIVE `p ≥ lo + e.length` from a balance hypothesis.** Its guard was `flowBracketBalance lo p = 0 ∧ lo < p`; the bulk of its `cons`-case proof was: extract the head entry `e`, build the `pbalance`/`flowBracketBalance` bridge, run the constructor-blind interior floor to show `p` is at-or-past the head's structural close (`lo + e.length ≤ p`), then a SECOND balance-composition argument to exclude `p = lo + e.length` (the separator), arriving at `lo + e.length < p`. The balance-`0` guard is the SOURCE of `p ≥ lo + e.length` there. R333 found this guard is incomplete: it only fires when `p` is itself at top level (`balance lo p = 0`), missing a `p` nested in a LATER entry (`balance lo p ≥ 1`, e.g. `[1, [2, [3]]]`).

**The driver already HAS `p ≥ lo + e.length` — so the general arm need not derive it, and the balance machinery vanishes.** The driver, at each window, runs `recseqbody_head_or_cons` (getting `e`, `fe`, `rest`, and the cons identity `body = e ++ fe :: rest`) and dispatches on `Nat.lt_or_ge p (lo + e.length)`. The `≥` branch HANDS the general arm `h_p_ge : lo + e.length ≤ p` directly. So `recseqbody_advance_general` takes the `cons` decomposition + `h_p_ge` as hypotheses and needs NO balance reasoning at all: no `pbalance` bridge, no interior floor, no `flowBracketBalance_compose`, no balance output. The lemma is ~40 lines vs `recseqbody_advance`'s ~110. The ONLY positional obligation is `lo + e.length ≠ p` — and that is NOT a balance fact either: the separator at window position `lo + e.length` is `fe` (a `.flowEntry`, read off the cons identity via the non-dependent `getElem?` slice algebra, R333's gotcha), while `tokens[p]! = .flowSequenceStart` — distinct constructors, so `p ≠ lo + e.length`, giving `lo + e.length < p` and `lo' = lo + e.length + 1 ≤ p`. The `single` body is simply not passed to this arm (its lone entry spans the window, `lo + e.length = H > p`, impossible), so the lemma takes the `cons` decomposition as a given.

**Sibling, not generalization — additive.** Per [[ref-additive-parallel-type-over-shared-edit]], I authored `recseqbody_advance_general` as a NEW lemma rather than editing the landed `recseqbody_advance`. The driver will call the general arm for ALL advance steps (it subsumes the balance-`0` case — `balance lo p = 0` still satisfies `p ≥ lo + e.length`), so `recseqbody_advance` becomes a verified-but-unconsumed R332 artifact; keeping it costs nothing and avoids a structural edit to a green lemma. The general lesson: when the complement guard you first reach for (R333's balance-`≥ 1`) turns out wrong, the FIX is often not a stronger guard but a DIFFERENT decomposition — here, pushing the entry-extraction (`recseqbody_head_or_cons`) UP into the driver and passing the structural `cons` facts DOWN, so the arm's own job shrinks to pure slice algebra. The balance was never intrinsic to advancing; it was R332's way of RECONSTRUCTING the structural decomposition the driver now supplies for free.

**The refutation (the probe).** `SeqNestedProjectProbe`/`SeqDescentProviderProbe`/`SeqDispatchPartitionProbe` all use ALL-SEQ witnesses, so every gated window is reachable by walking the root `RecSeqBody`'s `.seq` interiors. The unprobed complement is a seq window whose PATH from the root crosses a `.map` entry. On `[{a:[b]}]` (tokens `SS [ { key "a" value [ "b" ] } ] SE`, size 12) the inner seq `[b]`'s body window `[7,8)` is gated SEQ-typed — `flowBracketBalance 7 8 = 0`, and the btFold-top after `take 7` is `some true` (the inner `[` at position 6 pushes `true`, so the window's IMMEDIATE enclosure is a SEQUENCE, putting it on the SEQ carrier, not the map mirror) — AND nested (`flowBracketBalance 2 7 = 2 ≠ 0`), so `desc 7 8` IS invoked. Yet the root body `[2,10)` is a SINGLE entry whose head at 2 is `.flowMappingStart` — a `RecSeqEntry.map` (NonemptyStructure:466–469) storing `h_wb : WellBracketed interior` ONLY, with NO `h_rec : RecSeqBody` field. So `[b]`'s `RecSeqBody` is buried in an opaque `WellBracketed`; `recseqbody_descend`/`recseqentry_seq_extract` both require a `.flowSequenceStart` head and read the `.seq` constructor's `h_rec`, which a `.flowMappingStart` head does not have. **`rec_seq_body_nested_project` as specced is NOT a total `desc` provider.**

**The general lesson (sharpening [[ref-stored-vs-projected-severs-recursion-edge]] + [[ref-probe-provider-head-blind-gate]]).** When a provider NAVIGATES a recursive deliverable, its reachable domain is bounded by the deliverable type's STORED edges: a member that PROJECTS rather than STORES ([[ref-stored-vs-projected-severs-recursion-edge]] — here `RecSeqEntry.map` projects to `WellBracketed`) SEVERS the navigation at that member, so windows behind it are unreachable however the navigator recurses. Meanwhile the consumer's gate can be PATH-BLIND — `SeqTypedInterior`'s `SeqEnclosed` conjunct constrains only the window's IMMEDIATE enclosing bracket, NOT the path from the root — so it admits windows off every navigable path. The two diverge exactly at the severed edge, and the divergence is INVISIBLE to a probe that only descends the navigable (all-seq) case. Catch it by probing the PATH: a witness routed THROUGH the projecting member ([[ref-probe-provider-head-blind-gate]]'s minimal-pair move, lifted from the window to the path — [[ref-minimal-pair-extracts-the-gate]]). The fix mirrors [[ref-coerce-to-weaker-reuse-wrapper]]: don't strengthen the navigator (forcing `RecSeqEntry.map` to carry a `RecMapBody` — a heavy mutual-recursion type edit); RESTRICT its domain (carry path-is-all-seq as a hypothesis) and serve the severed-edge windows from the WEAKER substrate they DO have — `WellBracketed`/flat emission — since a map-path-nested seq window is itself a genuine emitted seq body whose `SafeBodyUnit` comes straight off `seqRoot_safeBodyUnit`-style scanning, no recursion needed.

### Reflection 336 — the PATH-dispatch discriminator is the typed-bracket-stack TYPE history (`btFold` stack all-`true`), NOT the root-base balance: a minimal pair over the PATH collapses under balance (both `= 2`) but separates under the stack (`[true,false,true]` vs `[true,true,true]`)

`(i'-b-B2c-nested-project, the DISPATCH)`, the SMALLEST-FIRST sub-brick of the R335-reshaped driver: settle the predicate that partitions `desc`'s gated seq windows into ALL-SEQ-PATH (root-`RecSeqBody`-navigable) vs MAP-PATH-NESTED (servable only flat), by a [[ref-minimal-pair-extracts-the-gate]] PROBE over the PATH — read off real output, not invented.

**The minimal pair.** `[{a:[b]}]` (`M`, size 12) window `[7,8)`, reached THROUGH the `{` map entry; `[[[1,2]]]` (`D`, size 11) window `[4,7)`, reached through `[` seq entries only. Both windows pass the gate identically (`flowBracketBalance _ a b = 0`, immediate `btFold`-top `some true`) — the path-blindness that R335 exposed.

**Balance REJECTED (necessity by collapse).** The cheaper candidate discriminator — the root-base balance `flowBracketBalance tokens 2 a` — is `2` for BOTH windows (`M 2 7 = D 2 4 = 2`). It cannot separate the classes; it IS the path-blindness `SeqTypedInterior` already suffers. A [[ref-minimal-pair-extracts-the-gate]] earns its NECESSITY leg exactly here: the pair collapses the weaker candidate to one value.

**Typed-stack SEPARATES (sufficiency + naming).** The full `btFold` typed stack after `take a` is `[true,false,true]` for the map-path window (a `false`/map frame buried below the top `true`) vs `[true,true,true]` for the all-seq window. The predicate `pathAllSeq tokens a := (btFold (some []) (take a)).map (·.all (· == true))` is `false` vs `true`: it SEPARATES, it is SUFFICIENT (the all-seq window passes), and it NAMES the discriminator — the buried map frame is the exact feature the balance cannot see. `pathAllSeq` is the decidable `Bool` proxy for the un-`Bool`-able `RecSeqBody`-reachability (candidate 3): the navigator reaches a window iff every frame from the root to its opener is a seq, i.e. the stack is all-`true`.

**The general lesson (applying [[ref-minimal-pair-extracts-the-gate]] to a PATH-dispatch).** When a path-blind gate ([[ref-severed-edge-bounds-navigator-domain]]) admits windows a navigator cannot reach, the dispatch that re-partitions them is NOT a fresh invariant to invent — it is the existing computation that already DISTINGUISHES the navigable from the unreachable. Find it by a minimal pair: a balance-style aggregate (a `Nat` summary) discards the frame TYPES and collapses; the stack itself (the un-aggregated `btFold` state) retains them and separates. Probe the aggregate AGAINST the structured state on one holding + one failing window; the leg that the gate's own conjunct already exposes-but-discards (here `btFold`-top is the gate's `SeqEnclosed` — it reads only the HEAD of the same stack `pathAllSeq` reads whole) is the dispatch, read off not invented.

### Reflection 337 — de-risk a navigator's DOMAIN-RESTRICTION with a PRESERVATION/NEGATION pair: the KEPT edge maps the domain into itself, the EXCLUDED edge maps it OUT — and it is the NEGATION, not the preservation, that licenses dropping the excluded recursion arm

`(i'-b-B2c-nested-project, the domain-restricted DRIVER fixpoint)`, the FIRST and SMALLEST de-risk R336's dispatch handed forward: before assembling the fixpoint, confirm the domain restriction `SeqPathAllSeq` (the proof-side `pathAllSeq` — the whole `btFold` stack all-`true`, not just `SeqEnclosed`'s TOP) is SELF-MAINTAINING across exactly the recursion edge the navigator keeps, and provably ABANDONED across the edge it drops.

**The pair (the de-risk made into two proven lemmas).** `SeqPathAllSeq tokens lo := ∃ s, btFold (some []) (take lo) = some s ∧ s ≠ [] ∧ s.all (· == true)`.
- **PRESERVATION** (`seqPathAllSeq_descend`): a `.flowSequenceStart` head pushes a `true` (`btStep … = some (true :: s)`), so the whole stack stays all-`true` — the DESCEND arm's EXISTING head hypothesis `h_lo_open : tokens[lo]! = .flowSequenceStart` (R333) is EXACTLY what discharges the path hypothesis at the recursion edge. The descended window `[lo+1, …)` inherits the domain; the kept arm needs nothing new.
- **NEGATION** (`seqPathAllSeq_map_push_breaks`): a `.flowMappingStart` head pushes a `false` (`btStep … = some (false :: s)`), so the resulting stack is NOT all-`true` — the descended window FALLS OUT of the domain. This is what makes "no fifth (map-mirror) sub-branch" a THEOREM, not a hope: a map head cannot even stay in-domain, so it is served by the separate flat provider, never a deferred recursive arm.
- **DOMINANCE** (`seqEnclosed_of_seqPathAllSeq`): the all-`true` stack has TOP `true`, so the domain supplies the dispatch's `SeqEnclosed` (its head projection) for free — the restriction is strictly stronger than what the per-window dispatch consumes, no extra threading.

**The general lesson.** When a severed/projecting edge bounds a navigator's reachable domain ([[ref-severed-edge-bounds-navigator-domain]]) and you RESTRICT the domain to fence it out, de-risk the restriction BEFORE the fixpoint by proving a PRESERVATION/NEGATION pair over the domain predicate — not preservation alone. Preservation shows the KEPT edge maps the domain into itself (and pins which existing head hypothesis discharges it); NEGATION shows the EXCLUDED edge maps the domain OUT of itself, and it is the negation that LICENSES dropping the excluded arm (otherwise "we just won't recurse there" is an unproven gap). The whole-stack predicate's two-edge asymmetry (seq-push preserves all-`true`, map-push breaks it) is [[ref-converse-forward-invariant-asymmetry]] / [[ref-push-blind-frame-dependent]] lifted from the TOP (`SeqEnclosed`) to the whole un-aggregated structured state ([[ref-aggregate-collapses-structured-separates]]) — same single PUSH, but tracking every frame, not just the head.

**What landed (one green sub-increment).** Three proven lemmas in `SeqInteriorSeparators.lean` (after `seqEnclosed_advance`): `SeqPathAllSeq` (def) + `seqPathAllSeq_descend` (preservation) + `seqPathAllSeq_map_push_breaks` (negation) + `seqEnclosed_of_seqPathAllSeq` (dominance). ### Reflection 338 — a PRODUCER sidesteps a navigation-fatal severed edge by STOPPING AT it as a leaf; the domain restriction a NAVIGATOR needed becomes the CONSUMER's routing tag, the producer consuming only its weaker projection

`(i'-b-B2c-nested-project)`, the driver AUTHORED. The (a)/(b) question of the 185th-revision map resolves decisively to **(a)** — and the resolution turns on a distinction the navigation framing of R335 had blurred: **navigation and production cross a severed edge in OPPOSITE ways.**

**The deciding read.** `rec_seq_body_nested_project` must deliver `RecSeqBody` at every all-seq-path nested window. Two ways to get it:
- **NAVIGATE** the root `RecSeqBody` tree (`seqRoot_recseqbody`, R326) down to the window and read its stored proof. R335 REFUTED this: a seq window buried in a `RecSeqEntry.map`'s interior is unreachable — the `.map` member stores only `WellBracketed interior`, no `RecSeqBody` field (the severed edge). Navigation must ENTER the map to reach the window, and there is nothing to descend through.
- **PRODUCE** the `RecSeqBody` fresh from the window's own guards (`seqWindowRecSeqBody`, R323). Reading its `step`: a `{`-headed first entry routes through `recseqentry_window_dispatch`'s NEAR-LEAF map oracle (`recseqentry_mapbracket_oracle` — interior `WellBracketed`, **no IH**) to a `RecSeqEntry.map` **leaf**. The producer STOPS AT the map opener; it never re-enters it.

So the SAME severed edge that is fatal to navigation is invisible to production: **navigation crosses the edge inward (and dies); production stops at the edge (and is fine).** `seqWindowRecSeqBody` is therefore TOTAL on every window with its four guards — in fact total well beyond the all-seq-path domain, since it handles a map first-entry the same way at any depth. Because `RecSeqBody` is a `Prop` (proof-irrelevant), a freshly produced witness is interchangeable with a navigated one — there was never a need for the SAME proof the root carries.

**What that does to the domain restriction.** If the producer is total without `SeqPathAllSeq`, why carry it? Because the restriction's role MOVED: it is no longer the producer's totality precondition (R335's reading), it is the **CONSUMER's routing discriminator** (R336). The consumer (`desc`) must split its windows between this recursive provider and the flat map-path provider, and `SeqEnclosed` (top-only) cannot make that split — a window directly inside a `[` has top `true` whether or not its path dips through a `{` deeper down. Only the whole-stack `SeqPathAllSeq` distinguishes them. So the provider carries `SeqPathAllSeq` as the consumer's routing tag and consumes only its **weaker `SeqEnclosed` projection** (via `seqEnclosed_of_seqPathAllSeq`, R337 DOMINANCE) — [[ref-coerce-to-weaker-reuse-wrapper]]: the consumer threads the strong routing predicate, the producer weakens it on demand at the one point it actually reads enclosure.

**What landed (one green sub-increment).** `rec_seq_body_nested_project` in `SeqInteriorSeparators.lean` (after `seqWindowRecSeqBody`), a one-line composition: `seqWindowRecSeqBody tokens h_root_carrier lo hi h_win h_deep (seqEnclosed_of_seqPathAllSeq tokens lo h_path) h_close`. Signature carries `FlowBodyWindow ∧ FlowBodyContentDeep ∧ SeqPathAllSeq lo ∧ tokens[hi]! = .flowSequenceEnd`, KEEPING `h_root_carrier` (R327). Full build green (589 jobs); frontier holds at exactly 4 pre-existing sorries; no new sorry; verified-but-unconsumed until the dispatch routes the partition (R225 discipline). The four R331–R334 arms are now confirmed an ALTERNATIVE driver, not a necessity — they remain landed but unconsumed.

**The general lesson.** When a severed/projecting edge bounds a NAVIGATOR's domain ([[ref-severed-edge-bounds-navigator-domain]]), check whether the deliverable can be PRODUCED rather than navigated before restricting the domain to route around the edge. A producer that treats the severed member as a LEAF (stops at it, no recursive field needed) is total where navigation is not — the edge is fatal only to the direction that must traverse INTO the severed member. If the deliverable is a `Prop`, production and navigation are interchangeable, so prefer production: it sidesteps the edge entirely. The domain restriction the navigator needed then survives only in its weaker role as the CONSUMER's routing discriminator — carried, but consumed as its projection ([[ref-coerce-to-weaker-reuse-wrapper]]), never as the strong predicate the producer was feared to need.

### Reflection 339 — the probe of a would-be COMPLEMENT provider REFUTES its necessity: the consumer's GATE already supplies the producer's only path-sensitive hypothesis as a free definitional conjunct, so the partition the navigator framing demanded DISSOLVES and the same producer serves the whole gated domain

The R338 next-step note planned a SECOND provider — a "flat map-path complement" for windows where `SeqPathAllSeq` fails (path dips through a `{`) — and asked, as the smallest-first sub-brick, whether `seqRoot_recseqbody` generalizes to an arbitrary nested sub-value. Per [[ref-probe-provider-satisfiable-before-assembler]] / [[ref-probe-provider-head-blind-gate]] the probe ran BEFORE authoring, and it REFUTED the whole premise: **no complement provider is needed; `SeqPathAllSeq` is vestigial.**

Three reads settle it, none guessed:

1. **The producer is path-blind.** `seqWindowRecSeqBody` (R338, `SeqInteriorSeparators.lean`) threads `G := FlowBodyWindow ∧ FlowBodyContentDeep ∧ SeqEnclosed lo ∧ close` — NOT `SeqPathAllSeq`. Its SOLE descend edge (the `recseqentry_window_dispatch` seq-bracket arm) fires on `tokens[lo]! = .flowSequenceStart` via `seqEnclosed_descend`; a `{` head routes to the map LEAF with NO IH ([[ref-producer-stops-at-severed-edge]] / R338). So the recursion descends only through `[`, STOPPING at every map; the map-path-nested seq windows the partition was built to route are **never reached**.

2. **`SeqEnclosed` is PATH-INVARIANT.** `SeqEnclosed tokens a := (btFold (some []) (take a)).bind (·.head?) = some true` reads only the stack TOP after `take a` — and `a` is a body-start sitting right after the window's OWN `[`, whose push puts `true` on top, for EVERY seq body regardless of the deeper path. The map-vs-seq distinction `SeqPathAllSeq` tracks lives in the deeper stack the producer never reads.

3. **The gate IS the enclosure.** The consumer contract `seqInteriorSeparators_of_safebody_provider` quantifies its `provider` under `SeqTypedInterior tokens a b`, whose SECOND conjunct (`def`, `SeqInteriorSeparators.lean:68`) is `(btFold (some []) (take a)).bind (·.head?) = some true` — *definitionally* `SeqEnclosed tokens a`. So the producer's only path-sensitive hypothesis is handed to it FREE by the very gate the consumer threads, IDENTICALLY for all-seq-path and map-path windows. This is [[ref-conjunct-of-projection-is-free-field]] AT THE GATE: a producer need that is definitionally a conjunct of the consumer's gate is a free projection, never a threaded obligation, and never a reason to partition the domain.

Landed as the one-line `seqEnclosed_of_seqTypedInterior tokens a b (h) : SeqEnclosed tokens a := h.2.1`. The `seqRoot_recseqbody` generalization question is MOOT (it replays a fresh `ScannerState.mk'` scan of `"[" ++ emitList items ++ "]"` — the R330 scan-context gap, not merely an offset rebasing — but we never need to re-root it). **Transferable rule:** when a navigator framing demands a domain partition + a second (complement) provider, before authoring the complement PROBE whether (i) the producer is actually sensitive to the partitioning predicate, and (ii) the consumer's gate already supplies the producer's weaker real need as a free conjunct. If the producer reads only a path-invariant projection that the gate definitionally contains, the complement provider is unnecessary, the partition predicate is vestigial, and one producer serves the whole gated domain. The size-up dual of a real partition ([[ref-downstream-derisk-restores-upstream]] RESTORES a dropped discriminator when a later consumer genuinely needs it; here the probe finds the discriminator was never needed — the gate carried it all along).

### Reflection 340 — a balance/enclosure/floor gate is END-FREE: it underdetermines a window's CLOSE, so a provider quantified under it cannot read its close off the window END `b` — it must locate the enclosing genuine structure and read the close off ITS matching boundary, the gate window SELECTED inside by a proven containment

The `(i'-b-B2c-provider-from-gate)` next-step note suspected the seq `desc` provider might read its structural close straight off the gated window's end `b` — i.e. that the gate `SeqTypedInterior tokens a b` forces `tokens[b]! = .flowSequenceEnd`. Per [[ref-probe-provider-satisfiable-before-assembler]] / [[ref-probe-provider-head-blind-gate]] the probe (`Tests/Guards/Proofs/SeqGateWindownessProbe.lean`) ran BEFORE authoring, and it **REFUTED** the suspicion.

The gate's three conjuncts (`flowBracketBalance a b = 0`, enclosing-seq `btFold`-top `= some true`, local-Dyck floor `∀ i ∈ [a,b], balance a i ≥ 0`) are all **END-FREE**: none mentions the token AT `b`. The existing `SeqDescentProviderProbe` masks this — it only exercises gated windows where the end `b` happens to coincide with the enclosing close `j` (`[3,6)`, `[5,8)`). Picking a `b ≠ j` window exposes it: on `[[1,2],9]` the gated window `[3,5)` (`"1" ,`) satisfies all three conjuncts (`balance 3 5 = 0`, top `= some true`, floor `≥ 0`) yet `tokens[5]!` is the scalar `"2"`, **not** `.flowSequenceEnd`; likewise `[5,7)` (`"2" ,`) on `[1,[2,3]]`. So `b` is a FREE choice anywhere inside the enclosing seq body, and the provider can NOT read its close off `tokens[b]!`.

**What this confirms.** The provider must LOCATE the enclosing genuine seq body `[loS, hiS)` and read `tokens[hiS]! = .flowSequenceEnd` off ITS matching close, with the gate window SELECTED inside via a proven containment `b ≤ hiS`. This is **exactly** what `seqDescent_provider_of_located` (`SeqInteriorSeparators.lean:728`) already does: it never inspects `tokens[b]!`; it locates `j = hiS` via `flowBracketBalance_matching_close`, proves `tokens[j]! = .flowSequenceEnd` (brick (3)), and proves `b ≤ j` (the [[ref-two-floor-relay-close-bound]] relay). So `(i'-b-B2c-provider-from-gate)` is NOT a fresh authoring task — that provider exists and is correctly stated INSIDE the parent recursion step. The residual reverts to the `desc` **driver** (locate `p`, thread the IH via `windowWidth_strongRecOn`).

**On the note's secondary suggestion — collapse `seqChild_safeBodyUnit` → `(seqWindowRecSeqBody …).toSafeBodyUnit`.** This must NOT be done blindly: `seqWindowRecSeqBody` is **carrier-dependent** (it takes `h_root_carrier : SeqInteriorSeparators tokens 2 (size-2)` and derives each window's `FlowBodyContent` from it via `seqWindow_flowBodyContent`), whereas `seqDescent_provider_of_located` is carrier-FREE (it takes `h_content` as a hypothesis and an external IH). Since `desc` is consumed to PRODUCE that very carrier (`seqRoot_seqInteriorSeparators`), routing `desc` through `seqWindowRecSeqBody` would be carrier-circular. The carrier↔recursion co-construction (R318's "carrier established once at the root from the FLAT `seqRoot_safeBodyUnit`, recursion driven by it") remains the live tension the driver must navigate — the producer choice does not dissolve it.

**Transferable rule.** When a window gate constrains only window-INTERNAL invariants (balance, enclosure mark, Dyck floor) but says nothing about the token AT the window's end `b`, it is END-FREE and underdetermines the structural close. Before assuming a provider can read its boundary off `tokens[b]!`, PROBE a `b ≠ close` window (one whose end is interior to the enclosing structure): if it passes the gate yet `tokens[b]!` is not the close token, the provider must instead locate the enclosing genuine structure and read the close off ITS boundary, the gate window selected inside by a proven containment. This is the END-dual of [[ref-probe-provider-head-blind-gate]] (a HEAD-blind gate admits spurious-headed windows; an END-free gate admits spurious-ended ones) and of [[ref-boundary-residual-end-dual]] (a window-END fact discharges by refuting a premise about a token PAST the window); here the END token is genuinely free, so the close is sourced from the enclosing frame, not the window.

This is [[ref-from-located-assembler-direction]] run the OTHER way: there the locator's output is lifted as hypotheses and the root seed is the corollary; here the locator is CONSUMED and the enclosing-facts/IH supplier is lifted — both factor the locate boundary, choosing which side to internalize by which half is already proven.

If it is, the genuine smallest brick is usually the FOLD that consumes the landed piece: compose the two existing halves and lift their join-point as a single hypothesis shaped as the next producer's contract. The fold costs ~10 lines, retires the "author the locator" item by exhibiting it as already-done, and re-types the residual from a vague "build the driver" into one named hypothesis `h_enc` whose discharge IS the fixpoint — [[ref-reduction-by-import]]: the retype is the progress. ### Reflection 342 — a co-construction cycle breaks at its BASE: when both recursion edges are landed, the only genuinely-open per-window source is the carrier-free ROOT SEED — and it is the SAME edge chain fed the FLAT producer in place of the IH

`(i'-b-B2c-desc-fixpoint)`, the per-window `FlowBodyContent` source. R341's `h_enc` requires, at the located enclosing opener `p`, the window `[p, hi)`'s `FlowBodyWindow`/`FlowBodyContentDeep`/`FlowBodyContent` + the width-IH. The first two are pure bracket/Dyck facts the recursion already carries; `FlowBodyContent` is the one field the deep guard cannot project (R296), classically sourced from the carrier `SeqInteriorSeparators tokens 2 (size-2)` via `seqWindow_flowBodyContent` — but that carrier is what `desc` is PRODUCING, so the source is circular (the R318/R340 carrier↔recursion co-construction tension).

**The probe (per [[ref-narrow-from-root-breaks-rederivation-cycle]] / [[ref-probe-deferred-universal-before-producing]]): is per-window `FlowBodyContent` re-derivable carrier-free, seeded once at the root and propagated by the recursion's own edges?** It CLOSED — and the decisive observation is that BOTH edges were ALREADY theorems, each having independently resolved the obstruction the carrier was papering over:

* DESCEND (`flowBodyContent_descend`, R325/R326) does NOT re-base the parent's `bodySucc` — which has no all-depth balance-free form (R296: a child's depth-`0` is the parent's depth-`1`, where the parent fact is silent, and inside a `{…}` it is outright FALSE). Instead it sources the child separator facts from the child's OWN `SafeBodyUnit`, drawn carrier-free from the width IH (`seqChild_safeBodyUnit`). So the descend edge SIDESTEPS R296 by consuming the recursion's own `RecSeqBody` output — the [[ref-converse-forward-invariant-asymmetry]] split (descend is genuinely recursive, advance pure re-basing) the deep guard already exhibited.
* ADVANCE (`flowBodyContent_advance`) is a pure depth-`0` re-basing across the separator, no IH.

**So the only genuinely-open piece was the BASE case** — and it is built by the SAME chain the descend edge uses, with one substitution: `seqSeparatorFacts_of_windowed_safebodyunit ▸ flowBodyContent_of_deep`, fed the FLAT `seqRoot_safeBodyUnit` (scanned straight off emission, no `RecSeqBody`) in place of the IH's child `SafeBodyUnit`. `seqRoot_flowBodyContent` is that 4-line composition. This is [[ref-universal-producer-root-seed-first]] in its sharpest form: when a recursion's edges are already landed, the producer's FIRST (and here ONLY) genuinely-open brick is the root seed — and [[ref-recursive-producer-mirrors-flat-over-shared-induction]] tells you where to find it: the leaf/base is the recursive edge with its IH-sourced ingredient swapped for the flat producer's output (here the child `SafeBodyUnit` → the root `SafeBodyUnit`).

**The general lesson.** A co-construction cycle (X sourced from a carrier that consumes X) breaks at its BASE, not its recursive steps. Before fearing the whole fixpoint, inventory the edges: if descend and advance are landed (often because each already had to resolve the obstruction the carrier was masking), the carrier dependency survives ONLY at the root window — replace it there with the flat producer and the cycle is severed. The root-seed lemma is then the recursive edge's chain fed the flat ingredient, not a fresh derivation. What remains is pure assembly (thread the now-carrier-free conjunct through `windowWidth_strongRecOn`), where the live design point is the IH adapter — re-packaging the step's `ih` to supply each recursive call's `FlowBodyContent`, the place the descend edge's IH-entanglement actually bites. Sharpens [[ref-narrow-from-root-breaks-rederivation-cycle]] (the move's outcome NAMED: edges landed ⇒ residual is the root seed) and [[ref-universal-producer-root-seed-first]] (root seed = the landed edge with the flat ingredient swapped in).

### Reflection 343 — eliminating a carrier oracle by threading its per-window fact as a recursion guard hits a CONTEXT-FREE-ADAPTER knot: the step's IH reaches the recursion's edges only through a context-free universal, so a fact whose only carrier-free sources are context-dependent cannot be supplied at the adapter — and the dispatch's same-window need closes the knot into a per-window cycle the carrier alone broke

The R342 next-step posed a binary probe ([[ref-probe-deferred-universal-before-producing]] at the adapter): with `FlowBodyContent` threaded as a fifth `G`-conjunct of the carrier-free `seqWindowRecSeqBody`, does the IH ADAPTER build each child `FlowBodyContent` from the descend/advance edge BEFORE invoking `ih` (clean ordering, the thread closes mechanically), or is there a true co-recursive knot? **The probe closed on the latter — a genuine knot — confirmed three independent ways.**

**(1) The context-free adapter cannot supply the fact.** The step's `ih` reaches the descend recursion only through the dispatch's `h_ih` (`recseqentry_window_dispatch`, NonemptyStructure.lean:5618), a *context-free* universal `∀ lo' hi', hi'-lo' < hi-lo → FlowBodyWindow → FlowBodyContentDeep → Q lo' → close → RecSeqBody` — quantified over an arbitrary sub-window, carrying NO enclosing context and NO `FlowBodyContent`. Threading `FlowBodyContent` as a 5th `G`-conjunct forces the adapter `fun lo' hi' h_lt h_w h_d h_q h_c => ih lo' hi' h_lt ⟨h_w, h_d, FBC', h_q, h_c⟩` to materialise `FBC' : FlowBodyContent tokens lo' hi'` for that arbitrary `lo' hi'`. The only carrier-free sources are the edges — `flowBodyContent_descend` (needs the ENCLOSING opener `p` and window `[p, hi)`) and `flowBodyContent_advance` (needs the PRECEDING separator `m` and the parent's `FlowBodyContent`) — both context-DEPENDENT. The adapter, handed only `lo' hi'`, has neither. It cannot build `FBC'`.

**(2) The dispatch's input closes a same-window cycle.** `recseqentry_window_dispatch` consumes the *current* window's full `FlowBodyContent` as genuine input: `headContentStart` (line 5634), `bodySucc` (5647, scalar branch), and pass-through to `recseqentry_seqbracket_oracle` / `recseqentry_mapbracket_oracle` (5654/5658). And `FlowBodyContent W` is obtainable carrier-free only from `RecSeqBody W`'s own `SafeBodyUnit` at the SAME window (R296: the separator facts `bodySucc`/`noTrailingSep` have no balance-free form). So `FlowBodyContent W ⟸ RecSeqBody W ⟸ dispatch ⟸ FlowBodyContent W` — a *same-window* cycle. Width recursion delivers only strictly-smaller windows, so it cannot break it, and strengthening `P := RecSeqBody ∧ FlowBodyContent` does NOT untie it (the dispatch still needs the same window's `FlowBodyContent` as input, before `P W` exists).

**(3) The carrier was the device that broke it.** The ambient carrier `SeqInteriorSeparators tokens 2 (size-2)` is a GLOBAL oracle answering `FlowBodyContent` at ANY window WITHOUT recursion (`seqWindow_flowBodyContent` is a narrow-and-lookup, no IH). Removing it reinstates the cycle that was always latent. The descend edge alone is clean-but-entangled (`flowBodyContent_descend` consumes a `RecSeqBody`-IH); the advance edge is genuinely clean (`flowBodyContent_advance` re-bases the parent's `FlowBodyContent`, context-available at the step) — so the knot lives entirely at descend.

**The resolution the knot forces.** Cut it by removing `FlowBodyContent` from the dispatch's INPUT. Its three uses are all HEAD / FIRST-ENTRY facts, not the whole-window separator structure: `headContentStart` (the window head is content-start — already sourced at descended children from the parent's `FlowBodyContentDeep.openerContentStart`), `bodySucc` (the scalar head's first successor), and the two oracles' first-entry needs. Reconstruct each carrier-free from the (already-carried) `FlowBodyContentDeep` guard + the boundary opener / enclosing context ([[ref-prefix-gate-reconstructed-from-boundary]] / [[ref-reconstruct-in-place-over-relocate]]). Then `seqWindowRecSeqBody` produces `RecSeqBody` with the EXISTING 4-conjunct `G` and no carrier, and `FlowBodyContent W` drops out as a pure downstream COROLLARY of the produced `RecSeqBody W` (the same-window edge `RecSeqBody W → FlowBodyContent W`, a CYCLE under the input-dispatch, becomes a one-way DERIVATION under the `FlowBodyContent`-free dispatch).

**The general lesson.** Before eliminating an external carrier oracle by threading its per-window fact `X` as a recursion `G`-conjunct, PROBE the IH adapter, not just the universal: the step's IH reaches the recursion's edges as a CONTEXT-FREE universal `∀ lo' hi', (cheap guards) → P`, so if `X`'s only carrier-free sources are context-DEPENDENT, the adapter cannot supply `X` for an arbitrary sub-window — a knot, usually a same-window cycle `X ⟸ P ⟸ dispatch ⟸ X` that width recursion cannot break and `P := P ∧ X` cannot untie. The carrier was the global no-recursion oracle that hid it. Cut the knot by making the DISPATCH `X`-free (reconstruct its few head/first-entry `X`-uses carrier-free); then `X` is a downstream corollary of `P`, not a threaded guard. This is NOT [[ref-cycle-breaks-at-base]] (that cycle is ROOT-only, broken by the flat producer; this one is per-window) and the carrier is precisely [[ref-narrow-from-root-breaks-rederivation-cycle]]'s narrowed oracle, here unreachable by narrowing because the `X`-need is per-window. Sharpens [[ref-probe-deferred-universal-before-producing]]; the descend-vs-advance asymmetry is [[ref-converse-forward-invariant-asymmetry]] / [[ref-push-blind-frame-dependent]]. Demo `Tests/Reflections/ContextFreeAdapterKnot.lean` (toy `Rec`/`Content`/`dispatch`/`content_of_rec`: positive carrier route closes, negative guarded thread needs the carrier, resolution via the `Content`-free dispatch).

### Reflection 344 — a multi-field guard INPUT localizes its dependency knot to ONE load-bearing field; audit field-by-field against the already-carried guard before concluding the whole guard is needed

R343's de-front pivot ("remove `FlowBodyContent` from `recseqentry_window_dispatch`'s input") posed a follow-up question the 191st-revision map mandated: of the THREE fields of `FlowBodyContent`, which does the dispatch (and its two forwarded oracles) actually read, and is each reconstructible carrier-free? The naïve reading treats the guard wholesale ("the consumer needs `FlowBodyContent`, `FlowBodyContent` needs the carrier, cycle"). The AUDIT — the correct granularity — reads the three consumers field-by-field. **The result is decisive: of three fields, ONE is free, ONE is dead, ONE is the genuine residual; the knot is exactly that one field.**

**The field-by-field finding.** Against the `FlowBodyContentDeep` guard the recursion ALREADY carries (NonemptyStructure.lean:4278):

* **`headContentStart`** (`isFlowContentStart tokens[lo]!.val`, read at the dispatch line 5634, all three head branches) — a **FREE projection**: it is definitionally the SAME proposition as `FlowBodyContentDeep.headContentStart` (:4279). The recursion already threads `h_deep`, so `h_deep.headContentStart` IS the dispatch's `h_content.headContentStart`. Zero residual. ([[ref-conjunct-of-projection-is-free-field]])
* **`feContentStart`** — **DEAD**: not consumed by the dispatch, the seq oracle, OR the map oracle. (It serves a *sibling* consumer — `flowBodyContent_advance`'s head re-seat on the tail — never the head-shape dispatch.) `FlowBodyContent` is OVER-PROVISIONED for this consumer.
* **`bodySucc`** (read at the dispatch's scalar branch :5647 @ `k = lo`; the seq oracle :4538 @ close `j`; the map oracle :4632 @ close `j`) — the **GENUINE RESIDUAL**: R296, no all-depth balance-free form (`SeqInteriorSeparators.lean:627`, :1484-1491), NOT a field of `FlowBodyContentDeep` (whose fields are all opener-`delta=1` / `.flowEntry` triggers, never a balanced-prefix END). It is the lone load-bearing field, and the one R296 says needs the window's `SafeBodyUnit`.

**What the audit settles.** The knot is NOT "`FlowBodyContent`" wholesale — it localizes to a SINGLE field, `bodySucc`, used at a SINGLE kind of position (the first entry's END: `lo` for a scalar head, the located close `j` for a bracket entry), and at exactly ONE instance per branch (not the universal field). Two of three fields evaporate. So the "knot is deeper" branch the R343 next-step anticipated fired: the de-front does NOT escape the knot by reconstruction; it **relocates** it to a precisely-named first-depth-0-separator successor fact. The de-front debt shrinks from "the whole `FlowBodyContent` guard" to "`bodySucc` at the first-entry-end" — a far smaller, more local obligation (a FIRST-separator emission fact, potentially derivable from a PREFIX `SafeBodyUnit` or root-emission rather than the whole window's `RecSeqBody`; the next session's probe).

**The general lesson.** Before concluding a consumer needs a whole multi-field guard `X` — and before believing `X` is what creates a dependency knot — AUDIT `X` field-by-field against the guard the recursion already carries. Each consumed field is (a) a FREE projection (definitionally a field of the carried guard), (b) DEAD (unconsumed by this consumer; over-provisioned, it serves a sibling), or (c) the genuine RESIDUAL. The knot is never `X`; it is exactly the residual field(s). The free + dead fields MASK which single field is load-bearing. Localizing to the residual shrinks the producer's debt to its minimum and, when the residual is itself irreducible, turns "`X` creates a cycle" into "field `f` at position `p` creates a cycle." This is the per-field-granularity sharpening of [[ref-incomplete-projection-still-factors]] (there a carrier projects most of a TARGET; here a consumer-input's fields are mostly free/dead w.r.t. an already-carried guard — the dual direction); the free-field mechanism is [[ref-conjunct-of-projection-is-free-field]]; the dead field is the over-provisioning of [[ref-additive-parallel-type-over-shared-edit]] seen from the consumer side; it localizes the knot of [[ref-context-free-adapter-knot]] and is the precondition for its resolution ([[ref-prefix-gate-reconstructed-from-boundary]]). Demo `Tests/Reflections/FieldAuditLocalizesKnot.lean` (toy `Deep`/`Guard` with a shared `head` target: positive `dispatch_defront` inhabitable from the carried `Deep` + lone residual `succ` with NO `feStart` field; negative `deep_holds_without_succ`/`defront_needs_succ` — `Deep` holds while `Succ := False`, so `succ` is irreducible and must be supplied standing).

### Reflection 345 — a bracket-typed invariant is SEPARATOR-BLIND, so a separator-placement fact is provably not a projection of it; refute de-front-by-reconstruction at the SUBSTRATE level

`(i'-b-B2c-bodySucc-first-entry)`, the probe of R344's lone residual. R344's audit had localized the
whole dispatch-defront knot to a single field, `FlowBodyContent.bodySucc`, instantiated at the
first-entry END. The de-front (`recseqentry_window_dispatch` made `FlowBodyContent`-free) works ONLY if
that one fact is reconstructible **carrier-free** — from the guards the recursion already carries
(`FlowBodyWindow`, whose `wellTyped` field is the typed-bracket invariant `WellTyped`, and
`FlowBodyContentDeep`). The smallest-first sub-brick was the PROBE, not the discharge. It **REFUTED**
the reconstruction — and did so not by failing to find a lemma, but by proving no lemma can exist.

**The mechanism — read the step function.** The decisive observation is mechanical and does not require
surveying derivability. `WellTyped` is a typed-bracket-stack fold (`btFold`/`btStep`,
`WellBracketed.lean:900-915`); its per-token step matches the separator token `.flowEntry` under the
`| _ => some s` **identity catch-all** (`WellBracketed.lean:906`) — the SAME branch a `.scalar` content
token takes. So `WellTyped` is **separator-blind**: its value is invariant under inserting, removing, or
relocating separators. An invariant that does not even read the separator token cannot witness its
PLACEMENT. (The balance invariant `flowBracketBalance` is blind the same way — the separator's
`flowBracketDelta = 0`.)

**The minimal pair** ([[ref-minimal-pair-extracts-the-gate]]). Take the window `[content, content]` (two
adjacent scalars, NO comma) versus `[content, sep, content]`. Both are `WellTyped` (`= some []` — the
blind fold accepts either); `FlowBodyContentDeep` holds VACUOUSLY on the first (no interior openers or
separators to constrain); yet `bodySucc` at `k = lo` FAILS on the first (`tokens[lo+1]` is a content
scalar, neither the window-end nor a `.flowEntry`) and holds on the second. So the FULL carried-guard set
`FlowBodyWindow ∧ FlowBodyContentDeep` is satisfied by the unseparated member while `bodySucc` fails ⇒
**no function `(carried guards) → bodySucc` can exist**. This is an impossibility at the substrate level,
not a missing-lemma gap.

**The candidates fall too.** The next-step's (a)/(b) — a PREFIX `SafeBodyUnit` / `seqRoot_safeBodyUnit`
restricted to the prefix — do NOT escape: those are EMISSION substrates (carrier-DEPENDENT), not
carrier-free. The probe asked "carrier-FREE, smaller than `RecSeqBody`"; smallness is irrelevant once
carrier-freeness fails. Every substrate that yields `bodySucc` must contain separator/emission
information, which no bracket-typed or balance invariant carries.

**What this settles.** `bodySucc`-at-first-entry-end is genuine EMISSION information — it lives only in
the emitter's `emit entry ++ [comma] ++ …` structure (`SafeBodyUnit`), exactly R296's obstruction
sharpened: not merely "no balance-free form" but "no typed-bracket-free form," now PROVEN via the
explicit separator-blindness of `btStep` rather than asserted. The de-front does NOT escape the
carrier↔recursion knot; the "if none" branch R343/R344 anticipated has FIRED. The cycle direction is
confirmed at `flowBodyContent_descend` (`SeqInteriorSeparators.lean:646`): the child's `FlowBodyContent`
is built from the child's `SafeBodyUnit` via `seqChild_safeBodyUnit`, which consumes the width-IH's
`RecSeqBody` (`FlowBodyContent[child] ⟸ RecSeqBody[child]` — the same-window cycle). The resolution is
NOT a `FlowBodyContent`-free dispatch; it is to KEEP the emission carrier `h_root_carrier` (R327) and
route `FlowBodyContent` per window from IT (the [[ref-narrow-from-root-breaks-rederivation-cycle]] move
from the EMISSION carrier), distinct from the desc-circular `seqWindowRecSeqBody` carrier lookup R340
forbade (that one reads `desc`'s OWN deliverable `SeqInteriorSeparators tokens 2 (size-2)`;
`h_root_carrier` reads the emission side, which is non-circular because `scanFiltered_emitSeq_nonempty_structure`
already has `EmitScansInFlowRecEntry`).

This is a FINDING increment (no proof-code change): build stays green (Tests.Reflections 69 jobs, full
build unchanged), frontier holds at 4. The demo `Tests/Reflections/SeparatorBlindTypedInvariant.lean`
machine-checks the mechanism: a separator-blind toy fold `WT`, a `firstSucc` toy of `bodySucc`, the
minimal pair `noSep`/`withSep` equal under `WT` but unequal under `firstSucc`, and the non-existence
`¬ ∀ l, WT l → firstSucc l = true`. The reflection is [[ref-separator-blind-typed-invariant]];
it sharpens R296, refines [[ref-type-blind-invariant-transports-via-converse-frame]] (separator-placement
is the specific fact a type-blind invariant cannot CREATE), and discharges the residual
[[ref-field-audit-localizes-knot]] named, resolving the "if none" branch of [[ref-context-free-adapter-knot]].

### Reflection 347 — a PARENT-RELATIVE recursion-guard conjunct rides the recursion's structural SITES, not the uniform IH adapter; widen the IH SIGNATURE and discharge at the descend/advance sites where the parent–child relation is in scope

The R347 PROBE (the mandated SMALLEST-FIRST sub-brick of `(i'-b-B2c-ih-recseqbody-step)`, the IH-availability ordering, BEFORE the step) ran the next-step's three sub-questions on the seq `RecSeqBody` fixpoint and **settled the route** — refining BOTH the R343 knot diagnosis and the R346 escape framing.

**Probe-Q1 — what the dispatch reads, and what it forwards.** `recseqentry_window_dispatch` (`NonemptyStructure.lean:5613`) consumes `h_content : FlowBodyContent tokens lo hi` ONLY at the first entry: `h_content.headContentStart` (`:5634`) and `h_content.bodySucc` (`:5647`). It forwards the PARENT's `h_content` + the four-conjunct uniform IH (`:5618`, `FlowBodyWindow ∧ FlowBodyContentDeep ∧ Q ∧ close → RecSeqBody`) into the seq oracle (`:5654`); the oracle's child `SafeBodyUnit` comes from `seqChild_safeBodyUnit` reading the PARENT's `h_content`, so the recursion itself never demands the CHILD's `FlowBodyContent`. `FlowBodyContent` has exactly three fields `⟨head, succ, fe⟩` (`flowBodyContent_advance` destructure `:4211`).

**Probe-Q2/Q3 — all three `FlowBodyContent` edges are landed, and the descended-window `SafeBodyUnit` is IH-fed (not `desc`-re-entrant).** ROOT `seqRoot_flowBodyContent` (`SeqInteriorSeparators.lean:1563`, off the flat emission `seqRoot_safeBodyUnit`, recursion-independent); DESCEND `flowBodyContent_descend` (`:646`, builds the child `[p+1,j)`'s `FlowBodyContent` from the PARENT's `h_content` + the four-conjunct IH via `seqChild_safeBodyUnit`); ADVANCE `flowBodyContent_advance` (`NonemptyStructure.lean:4205`, pure depth-`0` re-basing, no IH). `seqChild_safeBodyUnit` (`:606`) draws the child `SafeBodyUnit` from the width IH (de-risked `Tests/Guards/Proofs/SeqChildSafeBodyProbe.lean`), NOT by re-entering `desc`.

**The decisive finding — a parent-relative conjunct cannot ride the uniform adapter; it rides the structural sites.** `FlowBodyContent`'s descend edge CONSUMES THE PARENT–CHILD RELATION (the parent's `h_content` + the opener/close/floor). The recursion's IH is a single UNIFORM arrow over all strictly-smaller windows, and its adapter (`:5629`, `fun lo' hi' h_lt h_w h_d h_q h_c => ih lo' hi' h_lt ⟨h_w, h_d, h_q, h_c⟩`) receives only the child's INTRINSIC facts — never how the child descends from its parent — so it CANNOT invoke `flowBodyContent_descend` (no parent in scope). This is exactly the R343 [[ref-context-free-adapter-knot]] knot. **But the four conjuncts already in `G` are NOT re-established in the adapter either — the adapter just FORWARDS them; they are established at the recursion's STRUCTURAL CALL SITES (the seq oracle's descend, the assembler's advance), where the parent–child relation IS in scope.** So the knot is cut not by a `Content`-free dispatch (R343's anticipated route) but by WIDENING the dispatcher's IH SIGNATURE by the `FlowBodyContent` conjunct and discharging it at those two sites via the landed edges. The adapter still just forwards.

**Why route (A) — `seqSeparatorFacts_of_recseqbody` — is OFF the critical path (correcting R346's framing).** Reading `FlowBodyContent` off the window's OWN `RecSeqBody` is a SAME-WINDOW CYCLE for the producing window (its output is the step's deliverable, not an input — an endo `Content → Content` with no seed, the shape R346's `carrier_route_is_a_loop` already exhibited) and REDUNDANT for child windows (the descend edge already builds the child's `FlowBodyContent` from the parent's). So the lemma R346's next-step title named is not the route; the three threaded `FlowBodyContent` edges (root/descend/advance, all landed) are.

**Why the conjunct is NECESSARY (not avoidable).** At a nested window the step needs its OWN `bodySucc`, whose only carrier-free source is the parent's `FlowBodyContent` via the descend edge — which needs the parent relation, in scope only if `FlowBodyContent` is threaded parent→child. A four-conjunct recursion at a nested window knows only its intrinsic facts, so it cannot manufacture its own `FlowBodyContent`; hence the ambient carrier was introduced, and hence going carrier-free FORCES threading `FlowBodyContent` as the fifth `G`-conjunct.

**Resolution charted.** Drop `h_root_carrier` from `seqWindowRecSeqBody` (`:1606`); make `G` the five-conjunct `FlowBodyWindow ∧ FlowBodyContentDeep ∧ SeqEnclosed ∧ close ∧ FlowBodyContent`, seeded at the root by `seqRoot_flowBodyContent`; widen the dispatcher / seq oracle / assembler IH interfaces by the `FlowBodyContent` conjunct; discharge each child's `FlowBodyContent` at the descend site via `flowBodyContent_descend` and at the advance site via `flowBodyContent_advance`. ### Reflection 348 — a carrier-free IH thread's DESCEND edge re-enters its OWN window: the five→four IH projection runs UP the strength order, and the combined deliverable relocates the same-window cycle without breaking it

The R347 next-step's step (3) mandated a PROBE before authoring: is `flowBodyContent_descend`'s FOUR-conjunct `h_ih` obtainable by PROJECTING the widened FIVE-conjunct recursion IH? The R348 PROBE ran it mechanically, sorry-free, against the real definitions (`Tests/Guards/Proofs/DescendIHProjectionProbe.lean`), and the answer is the next-step's SECOND fork — a genuine arity entanglement — which on tracing further is NOT resolved by the named fallback either.

**Probe — the projection runs UP the strength order.** The widened recursion hands its step a FIVE-conjunct IH `IH5 : Intrinsic → FlowBodyContent → RecSeqBody`; the descend edge consumes a FOUR-conjunct `IH4 : Intrinsic → RecSeqBody` (produces the child's `RecSeqBody` WITHOUT the child's `FlowBodyContent`). `IH4` delivers `RecSeqBody` from FEWER inputs, so it trivially yields `IH5` (`ih5_of_ih4`, sorry-free): **`IH4` is STRICTLY STRONGER than `IH5`.** The needed direction `IH5 → IH4` must therefore SUPPLY the dropped `FlowBodyContent` at each strictly-smaller child from only its intrinsic facts — a `provider : ∀ child, Intrinsic child → FlowBodyContent child`. The projection closes IFF that provider exists (`ih4_of_ih5_iff_provider`, sorry-free — the residual is a named hypothesis, not a `sorry`). And that provider is exactly the carrier-free `FlowBodyContent`-from-intrinsics that does NOT exist (its `bodySucc` has no all-depth balance-free form, R296, and is invisible to the separator-blind `WellTyped`, R345). So the five→four projection is a GENUINE arity entanglement — the next-step's second fork, NOT a mechanical "drop the premise."

**The entanglement LOCATES at the descend edge — the edge asymmetry.** The two `FlowBodyContent` edges differ decisively. ADVANCE (`flowBodyContent_advance`, `:4205`) supplies the tail's `FlowBodyContent` by pure re-basing from the parent's — NO IH, NO child `RecSeqBody` — a clean parent→child arrow, exactly R347's optimistic toy shape. DESCEND (`flowBodyContent_descend`, `:646`) supplies the child `[p+1,j)`'s `FlowBodyContent` only through the child's OWN `RecSeqBody` (`seqChild_safeBodyUnit` `:606`, whose oracle invokes `h_ih` at `[p+1,j)`), because `bodySucc` cannot re-base DOWN a nesting level (R296). So discharging descend's `FlowBodyContent` re-enters the recursion at that SAME child window: `FlowBodyContent [p+1,j) ⟸ RecSeqBody [p+1,j) ⟸ dispatch ⟸ FlowBodyContent [p+1,j)` — a same-window 2-cycle, not a width-decreasing call. **R347's toy abstracted descend as a clean parent→child arrow (`F.descend : F plo phi → F lo hi`), hiding this `RecSeqBody` re-entry — so the descend edge is NOT a "landed clean edge" and the widened-IH route does not mechanically close.**

**The combined-deliverable fallback does NOT break it either.** The next-step's second fork named "fall back to the combined `RecSeqBody`+`FlowBodyContent` deliverable in one `windowWidth_strongRecOn` pass." Tracing it: `FlowBodyContent W` is read OFF `RecSeqBody W` (`seqSeparatorFacts_of_recseqbody` `:182`) while `RecSeqBody W`'s dispatch needs `FlowBodyContent W`'s `bodySucc` as INPUT. Composed, that is an endo with no seed (`same_window_loop`, the shape of R346's `carrier_route_is_a_loop`, now at a SINGLE window). The combined `P W := RecSeqBody W ∧ FlowBodyContent W` does not dissolve it — both fields of the step's output trace back through the same `FlowBodyContent W` input (`combined_step_still_cyclic`): combination RELOCATES the same-window cycle from the recursive edge INTO the step, because `FlowBodyContent` is simultaneously a PROJECTION of `RecSeqBody` and a PRECONDITION of it.

**The break.** Only an EMISSION source of `FlowBodyContent` independent of `RecSeqBody` opens the cycle (`break_via_emission`): then `FlowBodyContent W` is a genuine recursion INPUT, the four-conjunct `G` suffices, and no thread or combination is needed. The forward route is to generalize the flat root seed (`seqRoot_safeBodyUnit` / `seqRoot_flowBodyContent`, which deliver `FlowBodyContent` for the TOP window `[2,size-2)` straight off emission) to each NESTED sub-value, so `FlowBodyContent W` comes from `W`'s sub-value emission + `FlowBodyContentDeep` via `flowBodyContent_of_deep`, never from `RecSeqBody W`. This is the `seqRoot_recseqbody`-generalization the earlier `(i'-b-B2c-map-path-provider)` step flagged, now identified as the cycle-breaker the whole carrier-free arc requires.

The reflection is [[ref-projection-up-strength-order]]; it SHARPENS and CORRECTS [[ref-parent-relative-g-conjunct]] (R347's "discharge via landed edges" is too optimistic — the descend edge re-enters its own window), applies [[ref-push-blind-frame-dependent]] / [[ref-converse-forward-invariant-asymmetry]] (advance re-base vs descend re-entry), recognises the same-window loop as [[ref-carrier-provenance-not-type]]'s shape, and threads the irreducible `FlowBodyContent` [[ref-separator-blind-typed-invariant]] proved (R296/R345). Finding increment, no proof code: the projection probe + reflection demo are both sorry-free and built (Tests.Guards 168 jobs, Tests.Reflections 72), frontier holds at 4.

### Reflection 350 — a position-indexed navigator splits DECISION from CORRECTNESS: the bottom-up locator's branch dispatch is pure offset/length arithmetic, balance is demoted to the correctness side

`(i'-b-B2c-nested-fbc-emission-locator)` asked whether the emission-spine-walk locator — at an
all-seq-path interior window `[a,b)`, find the enclosing `RecSeqEntry` stored in `seqRoot_recseqbody`
and prove `(take (b+1)).drop lo = op :: (interior ++ [cl])` — is **(a)** a single offset-tracked
`body.length` recursion or **(b)** needs a separate balance-locate front end. The probe
(`SeqNestedEntryLocateProbe.lean`) found **(a)**, and the reason generalizes.

**A position-indexed navigator over a recursive deliverable splits into two pieces that use DIFFERENT
machinery: a DECISION procedure (which branch to take) and a CORRECTNESS justification (why that branch
is right). The decision is the cheap part.** Walking `RecSeqBody body` with the absolute base offset
`off` of `body`, the head entry `e` occupies `[off, off+e.length-1]`, so its interior window is
`[off+1, off+e.length-1)`. The target window start `a` selects the move by comparing `a` against
`off+1` and `off+e.length` **alone** — a pure trichotomy (`move_trichotomy`, one `omega`):
`a = off+1` → LEAF; `off+1 < a < off+e.length` → DESCEND (off' = off+1); `off+e.length < a` → ADVANCE
(off' = off+e.length+1); `a = off+e.length` is the impossible close/separator position, so the
trichotomy is exhaustive on valid windows and the branches are exclusive (`move_exclusive`, needs only
`1 ≤ e.length`). The recursive structure already STORES each entry's length and the offset-slice
invariant `body = (take H).drop off` ties structure to absolute token positions — so the navigator
NEVER calls balance to decide.

**Balance is demoted to the CORRECTNESS side.** R330's TOP-DOWN projection (`rec_seq_body_nested_project`)
selected the entry by `flowBracketBalance = 0` from the active base — because it was given a token
coordinate and had to FIND the structural entry. This BOTTOM-UP locator is keyed on the window `[a,b)`
itself, so the structural walk + offset arithmetic locate the entry directly; balance enters only the
PROOF that the located slice equals the target window (via the all-seq-path / `WellTyped` hypotheses),
never the branch selector. The forward locate's expensive machinery (a balance front end) is the part
the backward/bottom-up navigator sheds — the same shape as [[ref-backward-locator-mirrors-forward]]
(mirroring backward needs no standalone primitive) and [[ref-near-leaf-mirror-sheds-machinery]] (the
storage asymmetry has opposite signs across the locate boundary), here sharpened to: **the machinery a
locate needs for its DECISION can collapse to arithmetic on the opposite direction, leaving balance as a
pure correctness-side obligation.**

**Transferable rule.** Before importing a locate's heavy front end (balance, search, a matching-bracket
primitive) into a navigator that descends the same structure, ask which part of the locate is the
DECISION (which child to recurse into) vs the CORRECTNESS (why). If the recursive deliverable stores the
positional data the decision needs (entry lengths, child spans) and an offset-slice invariant ties it to
absolute coordinates, the decision is a length-arithmetic trichotomy — pure `omega` — and the heavy
front end belongs only to the correctness proof, not the recursion. Probe the trichotomy on concrete
witnesses (exercise each move once) BEFORE authoring; if it classifies cleanly, that is the (a)
single-recursion answer. Sharpens [[ref-from-located-assembler-direction]] (the bottom-up direction's
single-step shape) and [[ref-metric-bridge-is-composition]] (the feared machinery was already paid for
elsewhere — here, by the structure's stored lengths).

### Reflection 351 — the LEAF (the only deliverable-PRODUCING move of a position-navigator) is balance-FREE even on the CORRECTNESS side: its window identity is a pure prefix-slice fact; balance is confined to the non-producing interior MOVES

`(i'-b-B2c-nested-fbc-emission-locator-author)` authored the LEAF of `nestedSeq_recseqentry_locate` —
the bottom-up `body.length` navigator R350 settled as option (a). R350 split the navigator into a
DECISION (which child — arithmetic) and a CORRECTNESS (why — balance) and demoted balance to the
correctness side. AUTHORING the leaf **sharpens** that: R350's "correctness needs balance" is too coarse.

**The leaf's correctness is a PREFIX SLICE, not balance.** The leaf is the single move that PRODUCES the
deliverable (descend/advance only re-base `off` and recurse). Its whole correctness obligation is the
window identity `(L.take (off+e.length)).drop off = e` (`lo = off`, `b+1 = off+e.length`, `e` the head
entry). It follows from the navigator's offset-slice invariant `(L.take H).drop off = e ++ rest` (`e` a
prefix) + the fit bound `off + e.length ≤ H`, by pure `take`/`drop` algebra: `List.take_take` re-bases
the outer cut to `H`, `List.drop_take` swaps the order, `List.take_append_of_le_length` reads off the
prefix. NO `pbalance`, no Dyck floor, no matching-bracket. So at the leaf BOTH halves of R350's split are
cheap: the decision is length arithmetic (`a = off+1`), and the correctness is prefix slicing. The PROBE
(per [[ref-probe-deferred-universal-before-producing]]) confirmed the slice fact closes axiom-clean
BEFORE authoring; the leaf then produced the full `locator` existential (`head_entry_slice` +
`nestedSeq_recseqentry_locate_leaf`, both in `NonemptyStructure.lean`, sorry-free).

**Balance is confined to the non-producing MOVES.** The only place balance can enter the locator is the
DESCEND / ADVANCE navigation — proving the target window lies in the head entry's INTERIOR vs in `rest`
(which child). Those moves produce NOTHING; the leaf produces EVERYTHING. The producing move and the
balance-using moves are DISJOINT. "The producing case is the easy case."

**Transferable rule.** When a position-navigator over a recursive deliverable stores its children as
prefixes/segments and carries an offset-slice invariant tying structure to coordinates, AUTHOR THE LEAF
FIRST and expect its correctness (the window identity) to be PURE SLICE ALGEBRA, not the metric (balance)
the forward/top-down locate used. If you reach for balance to justify the leaf's output, you are
over-engineering — balance belongs to the interior MOVES, never the leaf's PRODUCTION. Sharpens
[[ref-navigator-dispatch-is-arithmetic]] (R350: this LOCATES where balance enters — not even the leaf's
correctness, only the interior moves) and [[ref-near-leaf-mirror-sheds-machinery]] (the leaf sheds even
the correctness-side metric); the slice fact is the window identity
[[ref-from-located-assembler-direction]]'s assembler consumes.

### Reflection 352 — read-ahead the CONSUMER chain to de-alarm a terse downstream step-list: a one-line "step (N) follows" can hide a feared obligation that is ALREADY PROVEN, OR a whole parallel effort; verify proof-state before pacing

A trajectory reassessment ("are we converging or circling?") prompted a READ-AHEAD de-risk of steps (3)–(6)
below the two `FlowSubrangesOk tokens := sorry` sites — BEFORE grinding the mechanical locator bricks
(descend/advance/wrapper). The dependency map listed (3)–(6) as terse one-liners ("drive
`seqWindowRecSeqBody` … thread … compose … wire …"), which READS as either trivial plumbing or hidden deep
work — the prose alone can't tell you which. Pulling the EXACT statements + proof-state of every symbol in
the chain settled it concretely.

**Finding — two feared obligations were already discharged, and a third front was overstated.** (α) A
first-pass survey flagged `EmitScansInFlowRecEntry` as "definition only, no proof" — a heavy per-value
scanner-correspondence obligation. FALSE: `emit_scans_in_flow_rec_entry` (NonemptyStructure.lean:2418)
PROVES it from `Grammable v inFlow` by induction. The `h_all` feeding `seqRoot_seqInteriorSeparators` is
supplied. (β) The per-window facts `seqWindowRecSeqBody` consumes (`FlowBodyWindow`/`FlowBodyContentDeep`/
`SeqEnclosed`) are carrier-supplied INSIDE the already-proven driver, not separate open producers. (γ) The
map mirror is substantially BUILT (RecMapBody step-lemmas already landed), not barely-begun. **Net: no
hidden deep obligation lurks in (3)–(6); the single open funnel per side is `desc`** — the descent argument
the `nestedSeq` locator is built to produce — plus pure proven-lemma composition.

**The lesson — proof-STATE, not prose, sets the pace.** A consumer-chain step described in one line is a
proof-state question, not a prose one: it can be (i) already proven (the feared obligation was discharged
sessions ago and forgotten — verify by grepping for a producer theorem, not a definition), (ii) trivial
plumbing of proven pieces, or (iii) a whole parallel effort duplicating what you just did (the map mirror).
These are indistinguishable in the map's one-liner but obvious from the actual `theorem … := by` vs `:=
sorry`. Before committing to a per-brick pace down a deep chain, READ-AHEAD the consumers and read their
proof-state off source — a survey that reports a definition as "unproven" without checking for its producer
will over-alarm (here it inverted the verdict: the chain is SHALLOWER than feared, gated on one `desc` per
side, the rest proven). The de-risk's payoff is a pacing decision: the mechanical bricks can now be BATCHED
because the de-risk confirmed there is no wall behind them. Complements
[[ref-probe-deferred-universal-before-producing]] (probe a deferred PRODUCER target before proving it; this
probes a deferred CONSUMER chain before pacing toward it) and the consumer-first family
[[ref-fold-consumer-chain-to-producer-contract]] / [[ref-consumer-joint-before-producer]] (read the
consumer to define the producer's contract; here, read the consumer to size the REMAINING WORK and catch
already-paid debts). Cross-checks a multi-agent survey against source — a survey is a lead, source is the
