Then axis-2 (keying) sizes each fix: a window-absolute field is discharged `:= g.field` VERBATIM in every constructing arm (zero proof); a walking-keyed field needs that arm's transport. The audit collapses to a two-step mechanical loop: (1) add the field, read off the missing-field errors = the constructing set; (2) per error, `:= g.field` if window-absolute else re-establish. Here adding `path : SeqPathAllSeq tokens (a-1)` produced "Fields missing: `path`" at precisely `step_descend`/`step_advance` and none at `step_leaf` — and because `path` is window-absolute (R374's target-anchored twin, [[ref-target-anchored-twin-refutes-walk-break]]), both were `path := g.path`, confirming the window-absolute ⇒ free-pass-through prediction with no manual arm-classification. ### Reflection 376 — a degenerate-case exclusion the carrier "should" supply may be UNDERIVABLE from its window-absolute fields; the dropped discriminator is often ALREADY NAMED by a field whose DOC claims more than its TYPE asserts — scan docs against types, refute with ONE witness, strengthen in place

Don't author the refutation against an assumed-derivable target — probe it first ([[ref-probe-deferred-universal-before-producing]]). Scanning field docs against their types surfaces the dropped discriminator BEFORE the probe — the de-risk then CONFIRMS rather than discovers it. **Two further economies.** The "minimal pair" degenerates to a SINGLE witness when the new conclusion is a plain inequality one object directly falsifies (no second disagreeing witness needed — {this witness} vs {any good one}); and the restore is an IN-PLACE strengthening of the too-weak field (`a ≤ b → a < b`), not a new additive field, since the discriminator IS an existing field stated below intent — and strengthening is consumer-compatible (`< ⇒ ≤`, every prior `≤`-reader still typechecks; here two verbatim pass-throughs + one omega weakening, zero new work, contrast the additive-field per-arm cost of [[ref-additive-field-cost-by-keying]]). ### Reflection 377 — one position-DELTA discriminator refutes a whole FAMILY of adjacent boundaries; the standalone boundary-exclusion brick is the sibling arm's INLINE refutation lifted and made delta-generic (and probe-before-producing has two outcomes: KILL the discriminator, or merely CORRECT the spec's geometry while confirming it)

The locator's dispatch owes TWO distinct `a ≠ <boundary>` exclusions: `move_trichotomy`'s `h_ne : a ≠ off + e.length` (the post-close cut, BRICK C-ii) and the sibling ADVANCE arm's inline `h_ne_boundary : a ≠ off + e.length + 1` (the post-separator cut). **Both are refuted by ONE field** — `opener : flowBracketBalance tokens (a-1) a = 1` (the target start's predecessor is a real bracket, δ=+1). The refutation of any candidate `a = m+1` is mechanical: the single-token balance at `a-1 = m` is `flowBracketDelta tokens[m]!` (via `flowBracketBalance_single`); if `≠ 1`, it contradicts `opener`. The two boundaries differ ONLY in the token's delta — separator `.flowEntry` δ=0, seq close `.flowSequenceEnd` δ=−1 — so they are the SAME proof modulo one delta-lemma `rw`. **The move:** don't re-derive per boundary or bury each in its dispatch arm; find the sibling arm's INLINE refutation, LIFT it into one DELTA-GENERIC standalone brick, instantiate per boundary ([[ref-near-leaf-mirror-sheds-machinery]] at the boundary layer — the mirror DROPS to the bare opener + delta lemma). **The probe-outcome nuance** sharpens [[ref-probe-deferred-universal-before-producing]]: a mandatory probe of a queued spec can land two ways — C-i (R376) KILLED the discriminator (the window-absolute fields could not exclude the empty-seq target → restore a strengthened field), while C-ii CORRECTED the spec's GEOMETRY (the predecessor is the CLOSE, not the separator) yet CONFIRMED the discriminator (`opener` still refutes). So a spec's geometric mislabel ("which token") is independent of whether its discriminator ("which field") is sound — probe BOTH on real `#guard` output, and a wrong geometry does not condemn the field. Demo: `Tests/Reflections/DeltaGenericBoundaryFamily.lean` — the delta-stream `boundary_excluded` brick + its two instantiations (`post_close_excluded` δ=−1, `post_separator_excluded` δ=0, ONE proof), plus `geometry_mislabeled`/`discriminator_still_sound` capturing the probe-outcome nuance.

### Reflection 378 — a positional-read lemma keyed on PREFIX LENGTH reads ANY structured element by re-association; the feared "close bridge" is the separator bridge with a re-bracketed prefix, and the maximal-risk arm-composition lands in one pass when the seams were pre-fit

### Reflection 380 — a metric-keyed dispatch DEGENERATES at the metric's minimum; the boundary brick that guards exhaustiveness in the generic case is the lever that LINEARIZES the degenerate one

The scalar-head CONS cell crystallized a pattern the seq/seqEmpty siblings (R378) had only half-shown. The locator's per-window dispatch is `move_trichotomy off e.length a` — a pure length-arithmetic 3-way split keyed on the head ENTRY's METRIC `e.length`: LEAF (`a = off+1`) / DESCEND (`off+1 < a < off+e.length`) / ADVANCE (`off+e.length < a`), exhaustive GIVEN the boundary exclusion `a ≠ off+e.length`. The reachable-arm count is **a DECREASING function of `e.length`, not a constant 3**, and the three landed CONS cells trace the gradient exactly: nonempty seq (`e.length ≥ 3`) → all THREE arms; empty seq (`e.length = 2`) → the DESCEND interval `(off+1, off+2)` is EMPTY, so LEAF + ADVANCE (R378's seqEmpty kept the 3-way `rcases` with a vacuous middle); scalar (`e.length = 1`, the METRIC MINIMUM) → the LEAF position `off+1` COINCIDES with the boundary `off+e.length = off+1`, so the boundary exclusion `a ≠ off+1` ALSO kills LEAF, and DESCEND was already empty → only ADVANCE survives, **straight-line, no `rcases` at all**. The lever is the SAME boundary brick the generic case needs for exhaustiveness: at the minimum it does DOUBLE DUTY — excluding the boundary also excludes the LEAF, because boundary = LEAF position. So the prescriptive rule: when a recursion's dispatch is keyed on an element METRIC and you reach a minimal-metric element, do NOT replicate the generic N-arm `rcases`; check whether the DESCEND interval collapses AND the LEAF position coincides with the excluded boundary, and if so write the cell straight-line (the boundary brick + the lower-bound field force the single surviving arm by one `omega`). This is the metric-driven analogue of [[ref-threaded-guard-prunes-case-tree]] (a GUARD field's type makes a constructor unreachable, pruning by guard STRENGTH) and a corollary of [[ref-structural-moves-complete-recursion]] (positional moves fewer than constructors) — here the pruner is element LENGTH, not a guard; it consumes [[ref-delta-generic-boundary-family]] (the scalar's δ=0 is the second distinct delta the boundary lift unlocked). Demo: `Tests/Reflections/MetricMinimumCollapsesDispatch.lean` — the toy `trichotomy` (omega, any `L`), the generic POSITIVE (all three arms at `L=4`), the degenerate `degenerate_advance_only` (straight-line ADVANCE at `L=1`), the NEGATIVE `degenerate_leaf_is_boundary` (LEAF = boundary at the minimum, so the LEAF arm is unreachable not merely unused), and the `reachableArms` `#guard`s tracing the 3/2/1 gradient.

### Reflection 381 — a search recursion's TERMINAL (separator-free / HEAD) branch is cleaved by container SATURATION; SHORT separator-free entries close VACUOUSLY by slice arithmetic, with no structural refutation at all

The two short-entry HEAD cells crystallized the HEAD-branch DUAL of R380's CONS-branch metric-degeneracy. The `recseqbody_head_or_cons` dispatch has a CONS branch (head entry `e` has a SUCCESSOR past a separator) and a TERMINAL / HEAD branch (`body = e`, `single`, NO separator, no successor). The question for the terminal branch: does it need the interior cells' machinery (the move trichotomy, the boundary brick, BRICK B refutations)? **No — it is cleaved by container SATURATION.** A separator-free container spans its whole window: the slice field forces `body.length = H - off`, i.e. `off + e.length = H` (the entry IS the window). The target being searched is a STRICTLY-INTERIOR `[a,b)` with `off+1 ≤ a < b < H`; since `H = off + e.length`, split the terminal branch by `Nat.lt_or_ge a (off + e.length)`: the **`a ≥ off + e.length` half is a pure ARITHMETIC CONTRADICTION** (`a ≥ H > b > a`), FREE from saturation, needing NO structure and even subsuming the boundary exclusion `h_ne` the interior branch needs; only the **`a < off + e.length` half** is genuine interior, refuted by the structural bricks (reusing the seq CONS carve's arm calls with `rest := []`). For a SHORT entry the interior half is itself empty — `e.length = 1` (scalar) ⇒ `off+1 ≤ a < b < off+1`; `e.length = 2` (empty seq) ⇒ `off+1 ≤ a < b < off+2` — so the WHOLE terminal branch is ONE `omega`, zero structural refutation. The prescriptive rule ([[ref-saturation-cleaves-terminal-branch]]): don't reflexively port the interior cells' refutations onto a search recursion's terminal branch; derive the container's SATURATION equation from the slice, cleave with `Nat.lt_or_ge a (off + container-length)`, and SHORT separator-free containers fall out vacuously while only spacious ones (`e.length ≥ 3`) need structure. This is the HEAD-branch dual of [[ref-metric-minimum-collapses-dispatch]] (which collapses the CONS-branch DISPATCH at the metric minimum) — together they give the full "short metric ⇒ cheap on BOTH branches" story; it refines [[ref-structural-moves-complete-recursion]] (a terminal-branch positional move can be ZERO moves — pure refutation) and is the slice-length companion of [[ref-threaded-guard-prunes-case-tree]] (there a GUARD field prunes the case tree; here the SLICE length does). ### Reflection 383 — a search-recursion's FIXED N-arm dispatch assigns each arm a ROLE of PRODUCE / REFUTE / VANISH, and for a SUM-TYPED head the role FACTORS as head-TYPE × head-METRIC

Landing the map CONS cell completes the eight-cell `h_step` matrix (4 CONS × {scalar, seqEmpty, seq, map}, plus the 4 HEAD cells), and the full matrix reveals a tight structure ([[ref-dispatch-role-factors-type-metric]]). The naive reading was a 4×3 grid of bespoke cells; the real structure is ONE fixed three-arm skeleton (LEAF/DESCEND/ADVANCE) whose every cell takes one of three ROLES — PRODUCE (emit the deliverable / shrink to the IH), REFUTE (the arm is REACHED but contradicts the deliverable's invariants; killed by a structural brick), VANISH (the arm's index range is empty; closed by `omega`) — with the role of each arm a pure function of two INDEPENDENT scalars of the head: the head's TYPE (does this constructor inhabit the seq deliverable? seq → PRODUCE, map → REFUTE, scalar → boundary-collapse) and the head's METRIC/length (which arm ranges are inhabited? short ⇒ DESCEND/middle arms VANISH). This UNIFIES the two prior dispatch reflections as the two AXES of one factorization: R380 ([[ref-metric-minimum-collapses-dispatch]]) is the METRIC axis (length-driven VANISH on the CONS branch), R381/R382 ([[ref-saturation-cleaves-terminal-branch]]) the HEAD branch's VANISH-by-saturation, and the map cells (R382/R383) add the TYPE axis (constructor-driven REFUTE). **REFUTE ≠ VANISH** is the practical lever: a VANISHed arm never runs (`omega` on an empty range), a REFUTEd arm RUNS and needs a brick; conflating them either over-builds (a refutation for an empty range) or under-builds (an `omega` where a brick is owed) — the tell is whether the arm's index range is inhabited under the guard. So K constructors give K distinct dispatch SHAPES from ONE arm skeleton — you assign a role per (type, metric) cell and reuse the SAME seams (`…step_{leaf,descend,advance}`/`…cons_boundary_delta`) rather than authoring K proof architectures; the producing arms share their seams across constructors, the refuting arms share one brick, the vanishing arms are `omega`. Refines [[ref-structural-moves-complete-recursion]] (one MOVE per constructor-composition → one ROLE per arm×head) and is the dispatch-layer companion of [[ref-threaded-guard-prunes-case-tree]] (a guard making a constructor UNREACHABLE = the VANISH role lifted to a whole branch). Demo: `Tests/Reflections/DispatchRoleFactorsTypeMetric.lean` — the `role`/`shape`/`producingArms` table (four distinct shapes), `role_factors` (POSITIVE, the role depends only on the two scalars), and the REFUTE-vs-VANISH pair (`vanish_range_empty` empty range / `refute_range_inhabited` nonempty range).

The proof is a GLUE-FREE 2×4 dispatch: `recseqbody_head_or_cons g.recBody` (HEAD vs CONS) then `cases h_e` (scalar/seqEmpty/seq/map), one `exact <cell> …` per arm. It typechecked FIRST TRY because every cell was carved (R378–R383) so its leading `h_eq : body = <pattern>` is EXACTLY the equation `cases`'s index-substitution produces (scalar → `body = [t]`, seq → `body = op :: (interior ++ [cl])`, …), and the CONS siblings `h_fe`/`h_rest` (independent of the eliminated index `e`) survive `cases h_e` un-reverted and slot straight in — no `rw`/`simp`/reorder/`.symm` glue. ### Reflection 384 — CARVE the leaf lemmas of a dispatch to the ELIMINATOR's output shape, and the assembler is a GLUE-FREE fan-out (the assembler is the literal INVERSE of the carve)

The eight `h_step` cells were each landed as standalone leaves over the prior sessions (R378–R383); R384 folds them, and the fold cost ZERO glue ([[ref-carve-leaves-to-eliminator-output]]). The reason: when you factor a dispatch into leaf lemmas BEFORE the assembler, you CHOOSE each leaf's hypotheses — and the right choice is EXACTLY what the destructor hands you at that arm. Two mechanics make this pay off. (1) `cases h_e` on the indexed family `RecSeqEntry e` (with `e` a local var) AUTO-REVERTS the hyps mentioning the index — notably the splitter's `h_eq : body = e` — substitutes the constructor's LITERAL index, and re-intros, so `h_eq` re-emerges as `body = [t]` (scalar), `body = op :: (interior ++ [cl])` (seq), etc.; carve each cell's `h_eq` to THAT literal pattern and `exact <cell> … h_eq` needs no rewriting. ORIENTATION is part of the shape: the splitter yields `body = e` (subject on the LEFT), so cells take `h_eq : body = <pattern>`, never flipped (a flipped leaf costs a `.symm` at every call site — the demo's negative). (2) sibling hyps NOT depending on the eliminated index `e` — the CONS branch's `h_fe : fe.val = .flowEntry` and `h_rest : RecSeqBody rest` — survive `cases h_e` un-reverted, keep their names, and slot straight into the cell calls. So the whole assembler is `intro; rcases recseqbody_head_or_cons g.recBody; cases h_e with | C flds => exact cell_C <ctx> h_eq <flds>` — one `exact` per cell, no glue. **The assembler is the literal INVERSE of the carve**: the intellectual work lived entirely in sizing each cell's hypotheses (R378–R383) to its per-arm need AND to the destructor output; the fold is mechanical bookkeeping. Corollary discipline: if a dispatch assembler ever needs `simp`/`rw`/reorder/`.symm` glue, that is a SIGNAL a leaf was carved to a "cleaned-up" shape rather than the destructor's literal output — fix the leaf, not the assembler. This is the engineering companion of [[ref-dispatch-role-factors-type-metric]] (that tabulates each arm's ROLE; this glues the role-tabulated cells) and the assembly half of [[ref-structural-moves-complete-recursion]] (one positional move per constructor-composition → one leaf per arm → one glue-free `exact` per leaf); it reads [[ref-parametric-assembler-extraction]] in the consume direction (lift per-arm work into leaves whose hypotheses ARE the assembler's local context). ### Reflection 387 — a conjunctive / multi-axis universal consumer cannot be discharged by a single-axis producer, however complete that axis's chain; recursion makes the "obviously single-axis" object's orthogonal conjunct NON-vacuous

The CONSUME plan asked whether the seq sorry could close on the seq locator alone before building the map side. A conjunction is gated by its weakest-covered conjunct; covering one axis perfectly closes nothing. The trap is the "main axis looks total" intuition: assuming the map conjunct is vacuous because the object's top-level type is a SEQUENCE. It is not — recursion MIXES the axes (a seq nests a map, `[{a: b}]`), and `FlowSubrangesOk` quantifies over ALL sub-windows, so the nested `{…}` window forces `MapBodyProps` and `h_map_rec` is owed. The planning discipline: when asked "can deliverable X close sorry S alone?", DECOMPOSE S's consumer into its independent conjuncts FIRST (read the `structure`/`∧` shape, not the producer); if `S = (P_seq ∧ P_map)` and X serves only `P_seq`, the answer is NO by the consumer's structure — record it before sinking effort into finishing the seq chain expecting it to close S; confirm the orthogonal conjunct is non-vacuous on a concrete witness; then land the smallest genuine brick on the axis you DO have as a clean [[ref-reduction-by-import]] consume (here `nestedSeq_safeBodyUnit_of_locator`). This is the CONSUMER-gating dual of [[ref-entry-boundary-input-shape-split]] (which tells you whether a BRICK mirrors seq/map — i.e. which producers you must WRITE; this tells you the goal stays open until you have written them all). ### Reflection 392 — a deferred universal consumed only by RESTRICTION lemmas hides its own falsity; probe the ROOT (the un-restricted instance) before producing it

R391 reduced the per-window `FlowBodyContentDeep` provider to the single root seed `FlowBodyContentDeep tokens 2 (size-2)` and queued its production (an emitter induction) with a sibling-search de-risk. R392 ran the de-risk's #eval-probe FIRST ([[ref-probe-deferred-universal-before-producing]]) and found the root seed FALSE — the cheaper finding, again. The pattern ([[ref-restriction-hides-root-falsity]]): a deferred universal `P window` whose ONLY lemmas are RESTRICTIONS (`P` wide→`P` narrow — descend/advance/`window_of_root`) has its truth UNTESTED, because every such lemma is CONDITIONAL on `P` holding at the wider window; the whole family typechecks green whether or not `P` is ever true. `P`'s truth is exercised nowhere except the ROOT — so probe THERE before authoring the producer. Why this `P` is false: the balance-FREE strengthening that made the restriction edges trivial (R290, the [[ref-converse-forward-invariant-asymmetry]] dividend) is exactly what makes `P` quantify over SUB-STRUCTURES with different conventions (flow-MAP interiors: `{`→`.key`, `,`→`.key`; empty brackets: `[]`→`]`), false there but never consumed there (maps/empties route to leaves). The sharper consequence: a restriction-only universal can be a consumer's EXCLUSION lever (`recseqentry_window_dispatch` reads `openerContentStart` to rule out empty brackets), so its falsity makes that exclusion UNSOUND for real inputs — `[[]]` is real. ### Reflection 399 — a producer field and the consumer hypothesis it must feed can be the SAME predicate under two module-local names: check definitional equality FIRST (the bridge is `exact h`, not a content proof), and a consumer guard premise the producer asserts unconditionally is SLACK — discarded, not discharged

Building the head-bridge that feeds `OpenerAdj_wrap_seq`'s `h_head` from `EmitScansInFlowBlock`'s content-start head field (Block.lean:107) looked like a real lemma — a producer field of shape `∃ hne, ContentStartTok (block.head hne).val` versus a consumer hypothesis of shape `∀ h0, (block[0]).val ≠ .flowSequenceEnd → isFlowContentStart (block[0]).val`. Two surface differences (`block.head` vs `block[0]`; an extra guard premise; two different predicate names in two different modules) suggested threading. Both collapsed. **(1) The two predicate NAMES are one predicate.** `ContentStartTok` (Block.lean, the emitter-scannability layer's "first filtered token is a content-start") and `isFlowContentStart` (ParserGrammableBase.lean, the parser layer's "`parseNodeContent` dispatches here") are DEFINITIONALLY identical — both `(∃ c s, · = .scalar c s) ∨ · = .flowSequenceStart ∨ · = .flowMappingStart` — they arose independently because the producer side and the consumer side were formalized in separate modules and each coined its own name for the same notion. The bridge is `exact hcs`, NOT a structural proof. **The lesson:** when wiring a producer field into a consumer hypothesis, FIRST check whether they are the same predicate under different module-local names (common when producer/consumer layers evolved separately) — if so, do not write a content proof; the coercion is `id`. **(2) A consumer guard premise the producer asserts unconditionally is SLACK.** The wrapper's `h_head` is guarded by `(block[0]).val ≠ .flowSequenceEnd`, but line 107 asserts the content-start head for EVERY non-empty block, unconditionally. So the guard is never needed — `intro _` DISCARDS it, it is not discharged. A consumer that is stricter (carries a guard) than the producer requires is slack at that premise; recognize slack and drop it rather than hunting for the fact that would satisfy it. This is the DEGENERATE (zero-gap) case of [[ref-coerce-to-weaker-reuse-wrapper]] — there the strong→weak coercion had a real head gap closed by the inductive's own head field; here the gap is exactly zero (definitional equality) AND the consumer over-specifies with a slack guard, so even the head field is unneeded. It also complements [[ref-conjunct-of-projection-is-free-field]] (a field that is definitionally a conjunct of what is projected is free) — here the WHOLE field is definitionally the consumer's need. The brick: `openerAdj_head_of_block_contentStart` (Block.lean). Demo: `Tests/Reflections/SynonymBridgeAndSlackGuard.lean`.

### Reflection 400 — a closure algebra's BRIDGE hypothesis is a WEAKER fact than the rich field it builds, and is often a CONSEQUENCE of an existing INVARIANT conjunct of the carrier: test derivability before adding+threading a new structural field

R397 ([[ref-orthogonal-invariant-algebra-before-threading]]) ruled the FULL `OpenerAdj` field orthogonal to the balance carrier (EntrySafe/WellBracketed/EntryUnit track balance + `.flowEntry` separators, not `.flowSequenceStart` adjacency) ⇒ a new field. The plan therefore queued a NEW structural "block-ends-non-opener" field for the `OpenerAdj_append` BRIDGE `h_tail`. **The sharpening:** that orthogonality verdict is about the FULL field; the BRIDGE `h_tail` is a strictly WEAKER fact — a single BOUNDARY claim (the LAST token isn't an opener), not adjacency everywhere — and it IS a consequence of an existing invariant conjunct, `EntryUnit` (`pbalance e = 0 ∧ ∀ i, 0<i<e.length → pbalance (e.take i) ≥ 1`): an opener last-token (δ `+1`) would force the `length-1` prefix to balance `-1` (or a singleton to balance `+1 ≠ 0`), contradicting `EntryUnit`. So `lastNonOpener_of_entryUnit` derives the bridge from the carrier's OWN conjunct in ~15 lines. **The rule:** "the rich field F is orthogonal to the carrier" does NOT imply "every BRIDGE F's algebra consumes is orthogonal too"; before adding a structural field to a widely-consumed predicate and threading it, check whether the fact is a CONSEQUENCE of an existing conjunct — if so, a derivation lemma (derive-on-demand, zero blast radius) beats add-and-thread (the field analog of [[ref-reduction-by-import]]). Two cautions that bit here when I DID add the field: (a) a grep enumerating the destructure sites by the field-ENDING shape OVER-MATCHED the PARALLEL `EmitScansInFlowRecEntry` predicate (same 21 shared conjuncts + extra `RecSeqEntry` + same head field) — verify each candidate's ACTUAL predicate (the `:= <applied hyp>` source) before adding a binder; the real break set was 4, not the ~7 the grep suggested; (b) a down-coercion B→A where A gains a field owes that field at the coercion — derive it from a conjunct B shares with A (`lastNonOpener_of_entryUnit block h21`), don't mirror the field through B's whole def+producer ([[ref-coerce-to-weaker-reuse-wrapper]]). The bricks: `lastNonOpener_of_entryUnit`/`lastNonOpener_singleton`/`lastNonOpener_wrap` + the field. ### Reflection 402 — mirroring a pre-staged side-input onto a parallel predicate is not a copy: shed, distinct-shape, cross-file

R401 pre-staged the seq body's head+tail side-inputs; R402 mirrors them onto the parallel map-body predicate (`EmitPairListScansInFlowBlock`). The lesson: a mirror of a staged side-input across a sibling predicate has THREE asymmetries the seq side hides. **(1) The consumer wrap can SHED a side-input.** `OpenerAdj_wrap_map` needs only `h_tail` (its `{` head makes `OpenerAdj_cons`'s head premise vacuous), so the map prereq is ONE field, not two — read which side-inputs the wrap consumes off the WRAP LEMMA's hypotheses, not off the seq mirror. **(2) A sibling arm can need a DISTINCT append shape.** The map producer's multi-pair body is the `Y ++ [feTok] ++ block_rest` seam (reuses `lastNonOpener_append3`), but its single-pair body is a RIGHT-append `block_kc ++ block_v` ending in the value block — the seam helper does NOT cover it, so it needs its own `lastNonOpener_append_right` (`getLast?_append` short-circuits to `b.getLast?` once `b ≠ []`); the non-emptiness comes FREE from the value's content-start head existential (`∃ (h : block ≠ []), …`, whose witness IS the non-emptiness — `obtain ⟨hne, _⟩`). **(3) The final-conjunct re-bundle break is CROSS-FILE.** Appending a FINAL conjunct to a shared predicate re-bundles `WellTyped ∧ <new>` into any consumer whose LAST destructure binder was `WellTyped`, breaking wherever it is used at its old type (`wrap_map_typed … h_body_wt`). The break is a TYPE mismatch at the USE site, invisible at the destructure — and it propagates to EVERY consumer file, not just the obvious producer. I grepped `BlockProducers` for `h_body_wt` but not `NonemptyStructure`; the build caught two more there. Lesson: before building, grep the WHOLE `Proofs/` tree by the last-binder NAME, not the predicate name. This SHARPENS [[ref-prestage-consumer-boundary-facts]] (the mirror is not a copy) and extends its caution (b) from `replace_all`-over-match to cross-file last-binder re-bundling. Demo: `Tests/Reflections/PrestageConsumerBoundaryFacts.lean` adds `lastNotOpener_append_right`/`bodyTailOk_singletonMap` (POSITIVE — the right-append shape + the map singleton producer keeping the tail field off `block_v`) and `append_right_needs_nonempty` (NEGATIVE — the `b ≠ []` premise is necessary: `[content, opn] ++ []` tails in `.opn` yet `[]` vacuously satisfies the field).

R403 lands the two `OpenerAdj` PRODUCER-COMPOSITION lemmas the flat list-producers need to discharge `OpenerAdj`'s body conjunct, the producer-side mirror of R401/R402's consumer FIELDS: **`OpenerAdj_seam`** (`a ++ [feTok] ++ rest` — the seq-body cons arm's `block₁ ++ [.flowEntry] ++ block_rest` AND the map-body multi-pair arm's `Y ++ [.flowEntry] ++ block_rest`; two `OpenerAdj_append` steps, the inner tail bridge `a ++ [feTok]`-ends-in-`feTok` via `lastNonOpener_append_right`) and **`OpenerAdj_map_single`** (`(key :: (block_k ++ [value])) ++ block_v` — the map singleton-pair body; a head-non-opener cons wrap of `block_k` + outer append onto `block_v`, the inner tail via `lastNonOpener_wrap`). Both in `WellBracketed.lean`, the `OpenerAdj` mirror of R401/R402's `lastNonOpener_append3`/`lastNonOpener_append_right`. Green, unconsumed (no predicate touched yet) ⇒ frontier 4. ([[ref-prestage-consumer-boundary-facts]] producer-composition variant.)

**Scope discovery (why (a-iii) is FIVE predicates, not three — `RecSeqEntry.map` blocks projecting `OpenerAdj`):** Adding `OpenerAdj` to `EmitScansInFlowBlock` forces it through the whole producer cluster, and the cluster is bigger than the surface "value + seq-body + map-body": **(P4)** the map body's `OpenerAdj` needs the KEY block's `OpenerAdj` — a seq key `[a]: v` makes the per-pair delta `key :: (block_k ++ [value]) ++ block_v` start its key part with `[`, so `EmitScansInFlowSavedKeyBlock` JOINS the cascade (needs `OpenerAdj` + a tail-not-opener field; produced by `emit_scans_block_combined`'s 3 SAVEDKEY arms). **(P5)** the down-coercion `emitScansInFlowBlock_of_flowRecEntry : EmitScansInFlowRecEntry → EmitScansInFlowBlock` must now OUTPUT `OpenerAdj`, and — unlike R400's `h_tail` (a balance/`EntryUnit` consequence) — full `OpenerAdj` is NOT derivable from any conjunct the coercion holds. The natural fix "derive it via `RecSeqEntry.toOpenerAdj`" is **BLOCKED**: `RecSeqEntry.map` stores ONLY `WellBracketed interior` (R244/R335 severed edge), and a `WellBracketed` interior can violate opener-adjacency (`[ , ]` is balanced, `[` followed by `.flowEntry`); and you CANNOT add `OpenerAdj` to the constructor because its RECONSTRUCTION sites (`NonemptyStructure.lean:5221`, `SeqInteriorSeparators.lean:3675`) rebuild `RecSeqEntry.map` from a located window carrying only `WellBracketed`. So `OpenerAdj` must be a STORED field on `EmitScansInFlowRecEntry`, threaded by its producer `emit_scans_in_flow_rec_entry` (the MAP value-arm is FREE — it uses the FLAT map producer `emitPairList_scans_block_nonempty`, already `OpenerAdj`-carrying — only the SEQ value-arm threads the recursive body, via `emitList_scans_recseqbody`). See [[ref-severed-edge-blocks-orthogonal-projection]] (Reflection 403): the severed edge that defeats NAVIGATION (R335) also defeats PROJECTION of an orthogonal field, forcing it to be threaded.

### Reflection 403 — a severed-edge constructor blocks PROJECTING an orthogonal field, forcing it to be a STORED carrier threaded through every producer

Scoping an ATOMIC orthogonal-field `F` threading across a cluster of mutually-recursive predicates that includes a SEVERED-EDGE constructor (stores only a WEAK summary of its interior, deliberately dropping the recursion — `RecSeqEntry.map` stores only `WellBracketed interior`). The lesson: the severed edge BLOCKS deriving `F` by PROJECTION (`F` is not a consequence of the weak summary), AND you cannot add `F` to the constructor (its RECONSTRUCTION sites rebuild it from a located window carrying only the weak summary, so they have no `F` to pass). Therefore `F` is a STORED field on the FLAT producer's predicate, threaded through EVERY producer in the cluster, never a projection of the recursive deliverable — and the "atomic" step that LOOKS like 3 predicates is really 5 (the map body's `F` pulls in the KEY block; the `RecEntry → flat` coercion pulls in the recursive-entry predicate + its body assembler). **The discovery method:** before scoping, FIND the severed-edge constructor, CHECK `F` is derivable from what it STORES (usually no — `F` is orthogonal to the stored balance/typing), then ENUMERATE its RECONSTRUCTION (builder) sites — grep the `Ctor _ _ _` BUILDERS fed a located window, not just the `| Ctor … =>` cases — and if any reconstruction site lacks `F`, the constructor cannot carry it, confirming `F` threads the producer. A projection-shaped plan over a severed edge is a dead end. Sharpens [[ref-stored-vs-projected-severs-recursion-edge]] / [[ref-severed-edge-bounds-navigator-domain]] (the severed edge ALSO bounds what can be projected); pre-staging step is the producer-composition variant of [[ref-prestage-consumer-boundary-facts]]; the move [[ref-coerce-to-weaker-reuse-wrapper]] forbids here (the datum is gone, you cannot coerce the projection into existence). Demo: `Tests/Reflections/SeveredEdgeBlocksProjection.lean` — `Rec.severed` stores only `WeakOk interior`; `Rec.toNonempty` PROJECTS the weak field (POSITIVE), `rec_severed_not_adj` exhibits a `severed`-built entry failing the orthogonal `Adj` (NEGATIVE — no projection exists), `adj_wrap_if_stored` shows the composition closes once `F` is SUPPLIED (the threading the producer must do).

R403 ([[ref-severed-edge-blocks-orthogonal-projection]]) ruled the orthogonal `OpenerAdj` field non-projectable off `RecSeqBody` (the severed `RecSeqEntry.map` edge drops the map-body recursion, so a `WellBracketed` interior can violate opener-adjacency) ⇒ it must be a STORED field threaded through every producer. The natural worry: does the same severed edge also block the BOUNDARY side-inputs the consumer wrap (`OpenerAdj_wrap_seq`) needs about the recursive body — the head content-start and tail not-opener? R404's answer: **NO**. Those boundary facts read the deliverable's OWN stored fields — the per-entry head (`h_head : ContentStartTok`, stored on both `RecSeqBody` constructors) and the per-entry `EntryUnit` (via `RecSeqEntry.toEntryUnit`) — plus the recursion-append SHAPE, never the severed map-interior. So `RecSeqBody.lastNonOpener` is a `getLast?`-routed structural recursion off `lastNonOpener_of_entryUnit`, and `RecSeqBody.openerAdjHead` is a one-`cases` read of `h_head`. **The rule:** when an orthogonal INTERIOR field `F` is non-projectable off a severed-edge recursive deliverable (R403), test its consumer's BOUNDARY side-inputs SEPARATELY — they project iff they read only the deliverable's stored per-entry invariants + constructor shape (head/tail facts almost always do), even though `F` (an all-INTERIOR-positions field) does not. This is why the producer pre-staging is always possible: the severed edge severs the INTERIOR recursion, not the BODY boundary; the boundary projects, only the field threads. The constructive complement of [[ref-severed-edge-blocks-orthogonal-projection]] and the recursive-deliverable variant of [[ref-prestage-consumer-boundary-facts]] (R401/R402 pre-staged the FLAT body predicate's boundary fields; R404 projects them off the RECURSIVE deliverable). ### Reflection 405 — an orthogonal field unprojectable from a recursive deliverable is CO-PRODUCED through the deliverable's OWN assembler, glued by the deliverable's own seam

R403 ([[ref-severed-edge-blocks-orthogonal-projection]]) proved `OpenerAdj` cannot be PROJECTED off `RecSeqBody` (the severed `RecSeqEntry.map` edge) ⇒ it must be a STORED carrier threaded through every producer; R404 showed its consumer-wrap BOUNDARY side-inputs (head/tail) still project. ONE induction co-produces both `D` and `F`: the leaf supplies `F`'s base (`OpenerAdj_singleton`/`_nil`), the cons step the seam, the per-item tail the seam needs off each entry's stored `EntryUnit` (`lastNonOpener_of_entryUnit`, never the severed interior). The value-arm that WRAPS the body (`OpenerAdj_wrap_seq`) then takes `F` from `A`'s new output and its head/tail from R404 — but only for NON-EMPTY bodies; the empty-body arm (`seqEmpty`) has no `RecSeqBody`, so `F`+head+tail thread as VACUOUS-friendly `∀`-shaped fields through the producer's intermediate existential (provable for `[]` by `OpenerAdj_nil`+`simp`, for `w::ws` by `A`+R404). The reusable rule: **unprojectable orthogonal field ⇒ co-produce it as an output conjunct of the deliverable's assembler, glued by the deliverable's own seam; its consumer-wrap boundary inputs project (R404), its empty-arm instances go vacuous.** Demo: `Tests/Reflections/SeveredEdgeBlocksProjection.lean` — `coproduce_adj` (+ `adj_append` seam, `tail_append_right` tail-bridge) CO-PRODUCES `Adj` of a flattened body by folding per-item `Adj` with the seam (POSITIVE), where `rec_severed_not_adj` proves projection impossible (R403 NEGATIVE).

Step (c) planned to "carry `OpenerAdj` up to a global `GlobalFlowSeqOpenerAdj tokens` fact," and the global producer `globalFlowSeqOpenerAdj_of_structure` was ALREADY landed — so the obvious move was to call it INSIDE the structure consumers (where the body `OpenerAdj` and the boundary facts are both in scope). ### Reflection 412 — a fixed consumer slot's WEAK guard decides whether an existing NAVIGATOR can be reused; a path-blind gate conjunct masks the routing tag

[[ref-producer-stops-at-severed-edge]] (R338) established that a severed edge makes a NAVIGATOR non-total, so you PRODUCE the deliverable fresh (stop at the edge as a leaf) and the navigator's domain restriction `SeqPathAllSeq` survives only as the CONSUMER's routing tag. R412 is the INTEGRATION-TIME dual: a SECOND consumer arrives — the fixed slot `h_seq_rec` that `flowSubrangesOk_of_window_producers` demands — whose guard OMITS the routing tag entirely. **The question "can my existing navigator-producer be REUSED for this slot?" is decided by the slot's GUARD SHAPE, not by whether the navigator produces the deliverable.** The navigator serves the slot ONLY IF the slot's weak guard IMPLIES the navigator's routing tag. Decide it with a MINIMAL PAIR satisfying the slot's weak guard ([[ref-minimal-pair-extracts-the-gate]]): if the routing tag SEPARATES the pair, the weak guard does not imply it, so the navigator is non-total on the slot — forcing the stop-at-edge PRODUCER route a SECOND time, now at the assembler boundary rather than the root. **THE TRAP:** the slot's guard often already CONTAINS a path-BLIND PROJECTION of the routing tag (`SeqEnclosed`, the top-of-stack seq mark = the head of `SeqPathAllSeq`), which makes it tempting to think the tag is covered. It is not — the projection SEPARATES NOTHING on the pair (it reads only the immediate enclosing frame, blind to a severed frame deeper down), so probe the WHOLE-stack predicate, not its head projection ([[ref-aggregate-collapses-structured-separates]]). The reusable read: **before reusing a domain-restricted producer for a new consumer slot, read the slot's guard; if it omits the producer's routing tag, probe a minimal pair (weak-guard-passing) for whether the tag is non-vacuous there — watch for the path-blind projection that masks the real separator.** Demo: `Tests/Reflections/ProducerStopsAtSeveredEdge.lean` R412 section — `routingTag_not_implied_by_slot` exhibits the box-path window `[true,false,true]` passing `consumerGuard` + path-blind `enclosedTop` but FAILING `pathAllSeq` (NEGATIVE — the navigator can't serve the slot); `discriminator_is_whole_path` shows `enclosedTop` agrees on the pair while `pathAllSeq` disagrees (POSITIVE — the whole-path tag is the discriminator).

### Reflection 414 — the arm a false guard suppressed is already built in the deliverable's classify; restore it with a `by_cases`, not new infra

R413 named the (R2) residual as a feared REDESIGN: `recseqentry_window_dispatch` RELIES on a false guard to EXCLUDE the empty-bracket case (R392's unsoundness), so migrating onto the re-scoped guard must "redesign the dispatch to HANDLE empty brackets" — which reads as owed handling machinery. R414 inverts the count. **A deliverable type and its CLASSIFY (the head-shape unifier mapping a window to one located constructor) are built ONCE, COMPLETE — a constructor per real shape, plus a classify disjunct + dispatch per constructor — BEFORE any producer guard is chosen. So the case a producer's false guard excludes almost always ALREADY HAS a constructor, a classify arm, and a dispatch; the guard was SUPPRESSING an existing arm, not filling a gap.** The redesign is therefore not "author a handler" but "stop suppressing it": a `by_cases` on the degenerate-case discriminator, routing the TRUE branch to the existing classify arm and keeping the FALSE branch on the old path. Two free alignments make it cheap: **(i)** the `by_cases` discriminator IS the premise the re-scoped guard is keyed on — the re-scope narrowed the guard by ADDING the non-degeneracy condition (`tokens[k+1] ≠ close`), so the FALSE branch hands the re-scoped guard its own premise for free (guard ∧ case-split share one boundary, [[ref-window-absolute-gate-subset-restriction]]); **(ii)** the restored arm's only non-trivial input is sourced from a FIELD the SIBLING arms already consume (here the successor from `FlowBodyContent.bodySucc`, exactly as the scalar arm). The reusable rule: **a producer guard found to UNSOUNDLY exclude a real case does NOT imply new handling machinery — SEARCH the deliverable's classify/constructor family for an arm matching that shape (grep the constructor, the disjunction, the dispatch); if present, the migration is a `by_cases` routing to it, and you probe-route the degenerate disjunct through the EXISTING classify on a real witness to confirm before budgeting a redesign.** This is the DUAL of [[ref-threaded-guard-prunes-case-tree]] (there a STRONGER guard SOUNDLY made constructors UNREACHABLE, so structural moves < constructors; here a guard UNSOUNDLY pruned a REAL constructor's arm, and restoring it brings the moves back IN LINE with the constructors), a grammar-level cousin of [[ref-deferred-structural-already-proven-by-sibling]] ("the residual you fear is already built", here an arm in the unifier rather than a sibling whole-structure lemma), and it discharges the "redesign" residual [[ref-redirect-audit-full-guard]] named; new memory [[ref-restored-arm-already-in-classify]]. Demo: `Tests/Reflections/RestoredArmAlreadyInClassify.lean` — `producer_routes_empty_via_bycases` routes the empty case to the EXISTING `Entry.emptyE` via `by_cases headEmpty` (POSITIVE — no new arm authored); `deepOld_excludes_empty` / `deepNew_admits_empty` are the false-guard / re-scoped-guard pair on the same window, and `guard_skips_empty_head` / `guard_fires_nonempty_head` show the discriminator coincides with the re-scoped guard's opener keying (the free alignment).

### Reflection 415 — a de-risked guard-re-scope migration costs ONE clone-with-one-line per consumer; restoring the suppressed arm and supplying the guard's new debt are the SAME case-split

R414 forecast the (R2) migration as a `by_cases`, not new infra; R415 IMPLEMENTED it and confirms the COST STRUCTURE of a de-risked guard re-scope. When a guard is re-scoped from "DERIVES fact X internally" to "takes X as a PREMISE" (because X was the very thing the old field unsoundly over-asserted), X does not vanish — it RELOCATES from a derived `have` inside each consumer to a supplied hypothesis on that consumer's signature ([[ref-guarded-universal-fold-relocates-guard]]: G is the producer's GIFT and the consumer's DEBT). **The migration is then mechanically a CLONE of each consumer with exactly ONE line changed — the `have hX := <old guard>.field …` becomes a new hypothesis `hX` — plus the recursion's descend/advance calls swapped to the re-scoped twins. Nothing else moves; the additive-parallel clone ([[ref-additive-parallel-type-over-shared-edit]]) leaves the old guard and its consumers intact, so the increment lands green and verified-but-unconsumed with no risk to the existing chain.** The sharp confirmation: the case-split that RESTORES the arm the false guard suppressed ([[ref-restored-arm-already-in-classify]]) and the supply point for the re-scoped guard's NEW premise are ONE AND THE SAME `by_cases`. Re-scoping the guard added the non-degeneracy condition (`tokens[k+1] ≠ close`) to its opener field; the suppressed arm is precisely the degenerate case (`tokens[k+1] = close`); so `by_cases tokens[k+1] = close` splits them at once — the TRUE branch is the restored arm (routed through the existing classify), the FALSE branch hands the cloned oracle its `≠ close` premise verbatim. Two obligations (restore the arm; pay the guard's debt) discharged by one structural move, because the re-scope and the suppression share their boundary by construction. The reusable rule: **once a guard re-scope is de-risked, do NOT budget per-consumer redesign — budget one clone-per-consumer-with-one-line, and look for the single case-split that simultaneously routes the restored arm AND supplies the guard's relocated debt; if the re-scope's added premise is the negation of the suppressed arm's discriminator, that case-split already exists for free.** Demo: `Tests/Reflections/DeriskedMigrationOneClonePerConsumer.lean`. New memory [[ref-derisked-migration-one-clone-per-consumer]].

### Reflection 416 — a guard re-scope that GATES a field splits its consumers by premise-availability; the consumer that needs the field UNGATED re-sources it from a sibling boundary-fact at the NARROWED window

R415 priced a de-risked guard re-scope at one clone-with-one-line per consumer (the field the old guard DERIVED becomes a SUPPLIED premise). R416 IMPLEMENTED the CONSUMER half and finds the cost model is NON-uniform once the re-scope GATES a field — adds a premise `P` to field `F`. Partition `F`'s consumers by whether `P` is AVAILABLE where they consume `F`:

* a **P-available consumer** has `P` derivable at the call site, so the clone is R415's one line (supply `P`). The recursion's ADVANCE edge is this case: `flowBodyContentDeepSeq_advance`'s new premise `tokens[m+1] ≠ .key` is FREE — the step already holds `isFlowContentStart tokens[m+1]` from the content guard it produced, and a content head is never a key ([[ref-guarded-universal-fold-relocates-guard]]: `P` is the producer's gift and the consumer's debt, paid from a fact in hand).
* a **P-unavailable consumer** must PRODUCE a downstream structure whose mirror field is UNGATED (`FlowBodyContent.feContentStart` has no `≠ .key` premise), so it needs `F`'s conclusion WITHOUT `P` — and `P` is exactly what `F` would conclude. It CANNOT route through the re-scoped guard at all: the gated field holds VACUOUSLY (premise unmet) precisely where the ungated field is FALSE. It must RE-SOURCE `F` from a SIBLING provider that proves the conclusion UNCONDITIONALLY.

The re-source trick (the reusable part): when the sibling is a BOUNDARY-keyed carrier fact — fires only at a window's LAST position, conclusion about the token just PAST the window — instantiate it at the NARROWED window ending at `k+1` to cover interior position `k`. Narrowing the upper bound re-frames `k` as that sub-window's boundary, and the "token past the sub-window" is the parent's interior `tokens[k+1]`. So a boundary-only provider covers every interior position for free ([[ref-window-absolute-gate-subset-restriction]]: the carrier's body is window-absolute, restricting to any seq-typed sub-window), and narrowing is NECESSARY — the boundary fact at the FULL window end is the WRONG instance (its premise is about the window's actual last position, not the interior separator). Here `seqWindow_flowBodyContent_seq` re-sources the interior content from the separator carrier's `noTrailingSepFact` at `[lo, k+1)`; the guard's `feContentStart` was a redundant second source, and with it gated, the carrier carries the load. The reusable rule: **when implementing a gated guard re-scope, do NOT budget R415's flat one-line-per-consumer — first PARTITION the consumers by premise-availability; each P-unavailable consumer costs a re-source (often a narrowing relay off an existing boundary-keyed carrier fact), not a one-liner.** The reverse-direction dual of [[ref-coerce-to-weaker-reuse-wrapper]] (there the producer is STRONGER ⇒ write the strong→weak coercion and reuse the wrapper; here the re-scoped producer is WEAKER at the consume boundary ⇒ no coercion, re-source the dropped field). [[ref-gated-field-resourced-via-narrow]].

**LANDED (R417 — step (d)-seq-rec (R3) SMALLEST-FIRST: the global separator-adjacency `def` + window-restriction + re-chosen satisfiability probe; build green, frontier 4, verified-but-unconsumed):** The (R3) per-window producer's first brick — the SOURCE of `FlowBodyContentDeepSeq`'s third field `feContentStart` — mirrors R395's opener trio for the `.flowEntry` trigger (`SeqInteriorSeparators.lean`, right after the `…WindowOpenerAdj_of_emit` block). **(1)** `GlobalFlowSeqSepAdj` (def): `∀ k, k+1 < size → tokens[k] = .flowEntry → tokens[k+1] ≠ .key → isFlowContentStart tokens[k+1]` — `GlobalFlowSeqOpenerAdj` with `.flowSequenceStart ↦ .flowEntry`, `.flowSequenceEnd ↦ .key`; the `≠ .key` gate excludes the MAP-internal `,` (successor is a key), leaving exactly the SEQ-context separators. **(2)** `flowSeqSepAdj_window_of_global` (CONSUME-side restriction): the verbatim 2-line subset-narrowing clone of `flowSeqOpenerAdj_window_of_global` — the all-depth window field over any `[lo, hi)` with `hi ≤ size`. **(3)** `globalFlowSeqSepAdj_fires` (satisfiability probe): the [[ref-probe-provider-satisfiable-before-assembler]] anchor, RE-CHOSEN — the opener probe's witness `[{a:[b]}]` has NO `.flowEntry` (no commas), so it could not be reused; the new witness `["a","b"]` fires the body at the `.flowEntry` `k=3` (successor `tokens[4] = .scalar "b"`, `≠ .key`, content). The def and restriction cloned for FREE; only the probe was real work.

### Reflection 417 — mirroring a gated global-adjacency predicate to a SIBLING trigger token: the DEF and the WINDOW-RESTRICTION clone for FREE, but the SATISFIABILITY PROBE does NOT clone — re-choose its witness for the NEW gate's non-vacuity axis

The (R3) seq-rec field producer needs a NEW global fact (`GlobalFlowSeqSepAdj`, trigger `.flowEntry`) paralleling the existing `GlobalFlowSeqOpenerAdj` (trigger `.flowSequenceStart`). The mirror is THREE bricks, and only the third is real work. **The `def` clones for free** — a pure token swap of trigger + excluded successor, zero proof content. **The window-restriction clones for free** — the SAME subset-narrowing lemma; it is gate-AGNOSTIC (only widens the domain bound), so it transports unchanged ([[ref-window-absolute-gate-subset-restriction]]). **The satisfiability PROBE does NOT clone** ([[ref-probe-provider-satisfiable-before-assembler]]). The sibling's witness was chosen for the SIBLING's trigger+gate and can be doubly wrong for the mirror: **(a) TRIGGER ABSENT** — the opener probe's cross-axis witness `[{a:[b]}]` has openers on both axes but ZERO `.flowEntry` separators (single-element seq, single-pair map ⇒ no commas), so the separator body fires VACUOUSLY (no firing position; certifies nothing — the probe's whole job, ruling out a vacuously-true provider, is defeated); **(b) GATE EXCLUDES** — even a separator-bearing witness can be the wrong AXIS, where the NEW gate excludes it (a flow-MAP `,` has successor `.key`, exactly what `≠ .key` excludes). The fix: re-choose a witness that contains the new trigger AND satisfies the new gate (here a multi-element SEQ `["a","b"]`), so the body fires NON-vacuously. The probe's witness is fixed by the new gate's EXCLUSION SEMANTICS — precisely the part that genuinely differs between siblings ([[ref-minimal-pair-extracts-the-gate]]: the gate IS the discriminator) — which is why it is the lone non-mechanical brick. The reusable rule: **in a sibling-mirror round, do NOT price the whole mirror as free because the def and restriction are; budget the satisfiability probe as a FRESH derivation whose witness must be re-chosen for the new gate.** Contrast [[ref-conjunctive-consumer-gates-on-orthogonal-axis]]: there ONE axis-uniform intermediate fires on BOTH axes (certified by a cross-axis probe); here the mirror'd gate can be axis-EXCLUSIVE, flipping which axis the predicate is non-vacuous on, so the sibling's cross-axis witness is the WRONG instance. Demo: `Tests/Reflections/MirroredGateReprobeWitness.lean`. New memory [[ref-mirrored-gate-reprobe-witness]].

**LANDED (R418 — step (d)-seq-rec (R3) the `GlobalFlowSeqSepAdj` PRODUCE-side joint `globalFlowSeqSepAdj_of_structure`, mirror of R396's `globalFlowSeqOpenerAdj_of_structure`; build green, frontier 4, verified-but-unconsumed):** The (R3) producer's second brick — the consumer joint that reduces the GLOBAL separator contract `GlobalFlowSeqSepAdj tokens` to the structure lemma's boundary facts plus ONE body separator field over `[2, size-2)` (`SeqInteriorSeparators.lean`, right after `globalFlowSeqSepAdj_fires`). ### Reflection 418 — a gated-global-adjacency PRODUCER mirror clones its `k`-split SKELETON, but the PRE-CLOSE boundary cell does NOT: its discharge is TYPED by (gate-excludes-close?) × (trigger-balance-changer?), two axes the trigger token alone does not fix

R417 found that mirroring a gated global-adjacency predicate to a sibling trigger clones the def + window-restriction for free, but the satisfiability PROBE does not (the CONSUME-side part that's gate-determined). R418 authors the produce-side joint and finds the DUAL: **the PRODUCER's five-way `k`-split skeleton clones, but the PRE-CLOSE boundary cell (`k+1 = size-2`) does NOT — its discharge strategy is selected by TWO axes the trigger token alone does not determine.** At the pre-close the successor IS the enclosing close (not a content-start), so the conclusion is FALSE and the cell must refute a premise; WHICH premise, and how, is set by: **(A) does the GATE exclude the close?** If the gate token equals the close, the boundary gate premise is self-contradictory — one `absurd h_close hne`, no structural fact (the seq opener, R396). **(B) is the TRIGGER a balance-changer?** If the gate admits the close, the gate premise survives and you must refute the TRIGGER premise instead; a balance-POSITIVE trigger (an opener, delta `+1`) is refuted by the Dyck FLOOR — a pre-close opener forces prefix balance `−1`, contradicting `balance ≥ 0` (the map opener, R410); a balance-NEUTRAL trigger (delta `0`) moves no balance, so the floor argument is UNAVAILABLE. Three cells result: gate-excludes-close ⇒ free `absurd`; gate-admits-close + balance-positive ⇒ Dyck floor; gate-admits-close + balance-neutral ⇒ **a NEW emitter-level no-trailing-X structural fact** (`tokens[size-3] ≠ trigger`) that neither opener sibling carried. The seq SEPARATOR (R418) is that third corner: gate `≠ .key` admits the seq close, `.flowEntry` is balance-neutral, so both opener discharges fail and the pre-close `.flowEntry` is excluded ONLY by "the emitter writes no trailing separator." The reusable rule: **do NOT price a producer-mirror by its `k`-split skeleton (which clones) — the pre-close boundary cell is a fresh derivation, and BEFORE writing it classify it by (A) gate-vs-close and (B) trigger-balance; if it lands in the gate-admits + balance-neutral corner, you owe a no-trailing-X structural input neither sibling needed.** This is the PRODUCE-side sibling of [[ref-mirrored-gate-reprobe-witness]] (in a gated-adjacency mirror, TWO things don't clone — the satisfiability PROBE and the pre-close BOUNDARY DISCHARGE — both because they are fixed by the gate's exclusion semantics, the genuinely-differing part of the mirror); it sharpens [[ref-boundary-residual-end-dual]] (the no-trailing-X route is FORCED exactly in the third corner, NOT needed in the first two) and generalizes [[ref-near-leaf-mirror-sheds-machinery]] (its seq↔map opener flip is the corner-1↔corner-2 transition; the separator is the third corner). Demo: `Tests/Reflections/BoundaryDischargeGateTriggerTyped.lean` — `prod_of_skeleton` (the cloning split; the pre-close cell is the abstract `h_boundary` argument), `boundary_cell1_gate_excludes`/`boundary_cell2_dyck_floor`/`boundary_cell3_no_trailing` (the three discharges), and `boundary_cell3_false_without_no_trailing` exhibiting a trailing-separator witness where corner 3's obligation is FALSE without the structural fact (load-bearing, not decorative). ### Reflection 419 — a producer-mirror's ONE non-cloning boundary corner is the CONSUME side's carrier END-DUAL: search the carrier before pricing it a fresh derivation

R418 classified a gated producer-mirror's pre-close discharge by (gate-excludes-close?) × (trigger-balance-changer?) and found the seq separator lands in the third corner (gate admits the close, trigger balance-neutral), owing "a genuinely new emitter-level no-trailing-X structural fact" — and HEDGED its sourcing ("from the `noTrailingSepFact` carrier OR a fresh structure field"). "New input neither SIBLING carried" (R418) is new relative to the OPENER siblings, but already PAID relative to the WHOLE proof, because the produce and consume sides SHARE the END-relative boundary fact.** The load-bearing premise is `isContent(close) = false`: the END-DUAL refutation works precisely because the boundary successor is the non-content close; on a content-successor witness the carrier holds yet the pre-close IS a separator (so the discharge would not run). ### Reflection 422 — a relocated obligation's SOURCE field is leaf-UNCONDITIONAL vs recursive-GATE-COLLAPSED: the leaf head bridges to any gate for free, but the recursive carrier (projected to the SIBLING'S gate) is lossy for the mirror's gate, so the mirror threads a NEW field there

R421 found that mirroring the `OpenerAdj` wrap/seam layer to `SepAdj` RELOCATES the content-start obligation to the `.flowEntry` SEAM, where `SepAdj_seam` demands the successor block's content-start head. R422 SOURCES that obligation and finds the source has TWO forms by POSITION, only one of which mirrors freely. **Leaf — unconditional ∃-head, bridges for free:** the per-value block (`EmitScansInFlowBlock`) stores its head content-start UNCONDITIONALLY (`∃ h, ContentStartTok (block.head h)`); a bridge intro's-and-DISCARDS any gate premise, so it yields `≠ G → content` for EVERY `G` — `sepAdj_head_of_block_contentStart` is the opener bridge `openerAdj_head_of_block_contentStart` with the gate token swapped to `≠ .key`, the SAME proof. **Recursive carrier — gate-COLLAPSED head, lossy for the sibling gate:** the list body (`EmitListScansInFlowBlock`) does NOT keep the ∃-head; its threaded head field (`Block:189`) was already PROJECTED to the FIRST consumer's gate `≠ .flowSequenceEnd` (the IGNORED `_h_head_rest`). Deriving the mirror's `≠ .key → content` from `≠ .flowSequenceEnd → content` needs `(≠ .key → ≠ .flowSequenceEnd)` ≡ `(= .flowSequenceEnd → = .key)`, FALSE for distinct excluded tokens — so the gate-collapsed head CANNOT source the relocated obligation; the carrier owes a NEW `≠ .key`-gated field. The lossiness is STRUCTURAL, not inconvenient: `(P → C)` yields `(Q → C)` only if `Q → P`, and `Q = (≠ .key)`, `P = (≠ .flowSequenceEnd)` are incomparable; the ∃-head keeps `C` raw (yields both), the gate-projected head keeps only `P → C`. **The reusable rule: when mirroring a gated-adjacency field to a sibling gate, audit each relocated sub-obligation's SOURCE by POSITION — UNCONDITIONAL/∃ sources (leaves) bridge to any gate (mirror = sibling bridge, gate token swapped), but GATE-PROJECTED sources (recursive carriers, already collapsed to the SIBLING'S gate when first threaded) are lossy for your gate ⇒ budget a NEW gate-shaped field on that carrier, do NOT coerce.** So R421's relocation is NOT free at the bridge layer — it ADDS a field on the recursive carrier, even though the leaf bridge is a pure clone. This sharpens [[ref-trigger-coincidence-relocates-obligation]] (R421 moves the obligation to the seam; this prices the seam's SOURCE), is the failure-mode dual of [[ref-coerce-to-weaker-reuse-wrapper]] (there a STRONGER producer coerces strong→weak to reuse a wrapper; here the recursive form is weak along the SIBLING'S axis, so weak→your-gate is impossible — thread, don't coerce), positionally sharpens [[ref-incomplete-projection-still-factors]] (the projection is COMPLETE for the sibling gate, EMPTY for the mirror's gate), and adds a twist to [[ref-reconstruct-in-place-over-relocate]] (the IGNORED `_h_head_rest` resurfaces, but un-ignoring it is INSUFFICIENT — it is gate-wrong). Demo: `Tests/Reflections/SourceGateCollapseBlocksMirror.lean` — `headC`/`bridge`/`bridge_gateA`/`bridge_gateB` (the leaf unconditional head bridging to TWO gates, one parametric proof) vs `gateB_from_gateA_fails` (the gate-projected `gateA_head` does NOT yield `gateB_head`, refuted by `[seqEnd]` where `gateA_head` holds VACUOUSLY yet `gateB_head` is FALSE) + the positive `gateA_and_gateB_of_headC`. New memory [[ref-source-gate-collapse-blocks-sibling-mirror]].

**LANDED (R423 — step (d)-seq-rec (R3) input (a) continued, the seam-nonemptiness PREP atom: `block_ne_nil_of_chainGrew`; build green, frontier 4, verified-but-unconsumed):** The field-(i) `lastNonSep` threading must construct `lastNonSep (block₁ ++ [feTok] ++ block_rest)` at the seq-/pair-body cons seam via `lastNonSep_append_right (block₁ ++ [feTok]) block_rest hb h_lns_rest`, whose `hb : block_rest ≠ []` is a REAL premise — R421 restricted the tail bridge to `rest ≠ []` because the seam token `feTok = .flowEntry` IS the separator, so an empty tail makes the WHOLE block end in `.flowEntry` and falsifies the field. `block_rest` is the recursion's per-step delta, and the carrier `EmitListScansInFlowBlock` does NOT expose its nonemptiness — and CANNOT, since it serves the empty input too (`emitList []`, empty block), so a `block ≠ []` carrier field would be UNSOUND. Instead `block_ne_nil_of_chainGrew` (`Block.lean`, between `emitList_scans_block_empty` and `…_nonempty`) DERIVES it from the recursion's PROGRESS WITNESS: the recursive chain `ScanChainGrew (· ≠ .placeholder) s₃ (n+1) s_end` (⇒ filtered count grows by `≥ n+1`, `ScanChainGrew_filtered_grows`) composed with the delta equation `s_end.filtered = s₃.filtered ++ block_rest` forces `block_rest.length ≥ n+1 ≥ 1`. ### Reflection 423 — derive a recursion-seam side-condition from the PROGRESS WITNESS, not a new carrier field: a nonemptiness/measure fact on the per-step delta is certified for free by the strict growth that drives the recursion (and a carrier field would be unsound — the carrier is shared with the degenerate case)

Threading the field-(i) `lastNonSep` separator-tail field hit a side-obligation the carrier could not supply: constructing it at the seq-body cons seam `block₁ ++ [feTok] ++ block_rest` needs `block_rest ≠ []` (R421 fenced the tail bridge to `rest ≠ []` — the seam token `.flowEntry` IS the separator, so an empty tail falsifies the field). `block_rest` is the recursion's per-step delta. Two options, only one sound. **(1) Thread a `block ≠ []` carrier field — UNSOUND:** `EmitListScansInFlowBlock` serves both empty (`emitList []`, empty block) and nonempty inputs, so `block ≠ []` cannot be an unconditional conjunct; it holds only at the recursive seam. **(2) Derive it from the PROGRESS WITNESS — free and sound:** the recursion advances by strict filtered-token growth, so at the seam the recursive chain `ScanChainGrew (· ≠ .placeholder) s₃ (n+1) s_end` is already bound; `ScanChainGrew_filtered_grows` gives `(s_end.filter).size ≥ (s₃.filter).size + (n+1)`, and composing with the delta equation `s_end.filter.toList = s₃.filter.toList ++ block_rest` forces `block_rest.length ≥ n+1 ≥ 1`. The growth that DRIVES the recursion is itself a nonemptiness certificate for the per-step delta. **Position-match:** the side-condition arises only at the nonempty/recursive seam, which is exactly where the progress witness lives — obligation and certificate co-locate, so no field need carry the fact across the degenerate case. **The lesson:** before threading a NEW carrier field for a seam-construction side-condition, classify it — a CONTENT/GATE obligation (head content-start gated on a sibling token, enclosure mark, typed shape) is not derivable from progress, thread it (the R422 failure mode, [[ref-source-gate-collapse-blocks-sibling-mirror]]); a NONEMPTINESS/POSITIVITY/MEASURE side-condition on the per-step delta IS derivable from the strict growth/measure-decrease already threaded for advancement or termination, derive it. R422 and R423 are a complementary pair. This is the don't-thread-a-new-field sibling of [[ref-non-restriction-residual-root-seed]] (there: seed the ROOT from infra rather than thread a stronger local invariant; here: derive a per-step side-condition from the progress witness), and in spirit a use of [[ref-reduction-by-import]] (an existing verified fact — `ScanChainGrew_filtered_grows` — discharges the residual). Demo: `Tests/Reflections/ProgressWitnessCertifiesDelta.lean` — `Grew`/`grew_ge` (the strict-growth chain + length lower bound) + `delta_ne_nil_of_grew` (POSITIVE: derive `delta ≠ []` from a `≥ 1`-step `Grew`, no field) vs `cannot_thread_unconditional` (NEGATIVE: the would-be carrier field `∀ run, delta run ≠ []` is FALSE on the zero-step degenerate run). New memory [[ref-progress-witness-certifies-delta]].

Three obstruction modes for sibling-token mirrors now: R421 relocation / R422 gate-collapse / R424 invariant-neutrality.

### Reflection 424 — an invariant-NEUTRAL sibling token needs an extra hypothesis to mirror an invariant-derived edge-token lemma: the separator is invisible to bracket-balance (delta 0), so the lemma that is FREE for the opener (delta +1, visible) is NOT free for the separator

Field (i)'s threading was mechanical except for one coercion (`emitScansInFlowBlock_of_flowRecEntry`), which needed `lastNonSep`-from-`EntryUnit` and revealed a non-obvious asymmetry. `EntryUnit e` is a bracket-BALANCE invariant (`pbalance e = 0 ∧ ∀ i, 0<i → i<len → pbalance (e.take i) ≥ 1`). `lastNonOpener_of_entryUnit` derives `last ≠ .flowSequenceStart` from it ALONE: the opener's `flowBracketDelta = +1` is VISIBLE to the invariant — a lone opener `[op]` has `pbalance = +1 ≠ 0` (not a unit), and for length `≥ 2` an opener-last forces the `(len-1)`-prefix to balance `-1 < 0`. Both contradictions, ALL lengths covered. I expected `lastNonSep` to be a verbatim token-swap. It is NOT: `.flowEntry`'s `flowBracketDelta = 0` is NEUTRAL — a lone separator `[sep]` has `pbalance = 0` and no proper nonempty prefix, so `EntryUnit [sep]` HOLDS and the invariant cannot exclude it. For length `≥ 2` the prefix-`≥ 1` condition still forces `pbalance e = pbalance (take (len-1)) + 0 ≥ 1 ≠ 0`, but the singleton degenerate case needs an INDEPENDENT hypothesis: the content-start head (head = last, and a `ContentStartTok` scalar/`[`/`{` is never `.flowEntry`). So `lastNonSep_of_entryUnit_contentHead` takes `EntryUnit` PLUS the `∃`-content-head where the opener lemma took `EntryUnit` alone. **The reusable rule: before mirroring an invariant-derived edge-token lemma to a sibling token Y, compute Y's contribution to the invariant's MEASURE (its delta-table entry). VISIBLE (nonzero) ⇒ the invariant excludes a lone-Y at every length, the mirror is a pure clone; NEUTRAL (zero) ⇒ the invariant admits the degenerate singleton `[Y]`, so budget an extra hypothesis (here the head) that excludes that boundary, the bulk (length ≥ 2) still riding the invariant.** The neutrality is the token's algebraic signature, checkable BEFORE writing the mirror — not discovered mid-proof. This is a THIRD distinct obstruction for sibling-token mirrors, complementing [[ref-source-gate-collapse-blocks-sibling-mirror]] (R422 — a threaded field already PROJECTED to the sibling's gate, lossy) and [[ref-trigger-coincidence-relocates-obligation]] (R421 — the obligation RELOCATES to the coinciding token); related to [[ref-easy-edge-guard-fails-hard-edge]] (an argument sound on one configuration fails a degenerate one). The threading itself rode [[ref-progress-witness-certifies-delta]] (R423) at the seams. Demo: `Tests/Reflections/InvariantNeutralSiblingNeedsHead.lean` — `delta` (opener `+1` VISIBLE, sep `0` NEUTRAL), `Unit`; POSITIVE `unit_excludes_lone_opener` (opener-singleton not a unit) vs NEGATIVE `unit_admits_lone_sep` + `not_lastNonSep_from_unit` (sep-singleton IS a unit, so `last ≠ sep` doesn't follow from `Unit` alone) + rescue `head_content_rules_out_lone_sep`. New memory [[ref-invariant-neutral-sibling-needs-head]].

### Reflection 425 — the gate token of a shared GATED edge field IS the discriminating sibling's head: discharge bifurcates (vacuous where the gate token = head, substantive elsewhere)

Field (ii) is a SINGLE field shape `∀ h0, block[0] ≠ .key → isFlowContentStart block[0]` threaded through TWO sibling list-body axes — `EmitListScansInFlowBlock` (SEQ) and `EmitPairListScansInFlowBlock` (MAP) — yet the discharge is OPPOSITE on each. **SEQ:** a seq entry's block head is a value's content-start head (`block₁`'s ∃-head), so `isFlowContentStart block[0]` is genuinely TRUE and the `≠ .key` gate is irrelevant, DISCARDED (`intro h0 _`); built by `sepAdjHead_append3` (the gate-discarding twin of `headContentStart_append3`). **MAP:** a map entry's block is constructed as `⟨pos, .key, pos⟩ :: …` (the leading colon-key marker), so `block[0] = .key` and `isFlowContentStart block[0]` is FALSE — the field survives ONLY because the gate premise `block[0] ≠ .key` is FALSE, holding VACUOUSLY. So the gate token `.key` IS the map entry's head: it gates out exactly the axis where the conclusion fails, which is WHY the field is `≠ .key`-gated and not an unconditional content-start head (unconditional would be FALSE for the map). **The reusable rule: when threading a gated edge field `x ≠ K → P x` through a sibling family, the gate token K is read off the DISCRIMINATING sibling's constructor — the axis whose edge token K makes `P K` FALSE. Classify each sibling's edge token: head = K ⇒ VACUOUS discharge (the gate exists FOR this sibling — refute the premise from the literal head); head ≠ K and P-true ⇒ SUBSTANTIVE discharge (prove P, discard the gate); head ≠ K and P-FALSE ⇒ the gate UNDERGATES (the field is false for the un-gated falsifier — K is wrong, widen the gate or split per axis). If NO sibling has head = K, the gate is dead weight.** This is the MULTI-AXIS dual of [[ref-guarded-universal-fold-relocates-guard]] (a guard G is the producer's GIFT — narrower domain, where P fails is gated out; here the gated-out region is one entire SIBLING AXIS, named by the gate token = that axis's head). Complements [[ref-invariant-neutral-sibling-needs-head]] (R424 also bifurcated a single field's discharge by the head token, but by ADDING a content-head hypothesis where the invariant was blind; R425 by REFUTING the gate). Distinct from [[ref-threaded-guard-prunes-case-tree]] (a guard making a constructor UNREACHABLE — pruning; here the gate makes the field VACUOUSLY TRUE at a reachable constructor — satisfaction). Demo: `Tests/Reflections/GateTokenIsSiblingHead.lean` — `content`/`key`/`opener` tokens, `seqEntry` (head content) + `mapEntry` (head key); POSITIVE `seq_field_holds` (substantive, gate discarded) + `map_field_holds_vacuously` (gate premise false); NEGATIVE `wrong_gate_undergates` (gating on `≠ opener` instead of `≠ key` leaves the field FALSE for `[key]`). New memory [[ref-gate-token-is-sibling-head]].

### Reflection 426 — a carrier field on a MULTI-PRODUCER predicate is gated by the producer whose source is a STRUCTURE-DISCARDING inductive deliverable (project-from-inductive fails; thread-separate-from-grammar-producer succeeds)

Field (iii) `SepAdj block` added to `EmitScansInFlowBlock` exposed a structural constraint the blueprint's "thread through the block predicates" framing missed: **`EmitScansInFlowBlock` has TWO producers, and a carrier field obliges BOTH to supply it.** (a) The GRAMMAR induction `emit_scans_block_combined` supplies `SepAdj` via `SepAdj_wrap_seq`/`_wrap_map` from the scanned body's `SepAdj` — easy. (b) The nested-locator COERCION `emitScansInFlowBlock_of_flowRecEntry` forwards from `EmitScansInFlowRecEntry`, whose body is the inductive deliverable `RecSeqEntry` — and **`RecSeqEntry.map` BOTTOMS OUT at `WellBracketed interior`** (it deliberately discards the map interior's recursive structure for navigability). A `RecSeqEntry.toSepAdj` projection is **FALSE**: `.map` admits `SepAdj`-violating interiors like `{,,}` = `op :: ([fe, fe] ++ [cl])` (`[fe, fe]` is `WellBracketed` — both delta-`0` — yet the first `.flowEntry`'s successor is `.flowEntry`, neither `.key` nor a content start); `WellTyped` (a bracket-typing fold) places no `.flowEntry`→`.key` constraint, so it does not rescue it. **The reusable rule: a carrier field added to a predicate with multiple producers is gated by the producer whose SOURCE is a structure-DISCARDING inductive — that producer CANNOT project the field. Do NOT strengthen the bottoming inductive (it bottoms out on purpose); thread the field as a SEPARATE carrier field of the STRONG predicate (`EmitScansInFlowRecEntry`), supplied by ITS grammar producer (`emit_scans_in_flow_rec_entry`, which retains the scan structure and PROVES the field — the map interior's `SepAdj` is vacuous, separators followed by `.key`, provable from the scanned `EmitPairListScansInFlowBlock`); the coercion then FORWARDS the field, never `inductive.toField`.** De-risk: before adding a carrier field, grep ALL producers (`: Pred` / `→ Pred` conclusions); a coercion `StrongPred → Pred` whose source carries a structure-discarding inductive needs the field threaded through the strong predicate too. This is the PRODUCER-side dual of [[ref-source-gate-collapse-blocks-sibling-mirror]] (R422: a gate-COLLAPSED source can't supply a SIBLING gate ⇒ thread a new field; here a structure-DISCARDING source can't supply a STRUCTURAL field ⇒ thread through the grammar producer), the failure-mode dual of [[ref-coerce-to-weaker-reuse-wrapper]] (there strong→weak coerces to REUSE a wrapper; here the inductive is weak along the field's axis ⇒ thread, don't project), and sharpens [[ref-additive-parallel-type-over-shared-edit]] with WHICH producer gates the field. Demo: `Tests/Reflections/FieldOnMultiproducerPredicate.lean` — `SepOk`/`balanced`/`Deliv` (toys of `SepAdj`/`WellBracketed`/`RecSeqEntry`); NEGATIVE `deliv_toSepOk_fails` (`Deliv.toSepOk` FALSE — `wrap [sep, sep]` is `balanced` yet violates `SepOk`) + POSITIVE `sepOk_of_scanned_wrap` (the grammar producer that scanned the interior proves `SepOk` directly). New memory [[ref-field-on-multiproducer-predicate]].

### Reflection 428 — the contradiction branch supplies its own boundary fact

The separator emit-wrapper's last owed input was the pre-close no-trailing boundary `tokens[size-3] ≠ .flowEntry`. The natural first move — source a free-standing boundary-balance fact to feed R419's carrier — DEAD-ENDS: **the boundary balance `flowBracketBalance tokens 2 (size-3) = 0` is FALSE in general** (a nested-collection last element makes the pre-close a closing bracket, balance `+1`), so R419's unconditional `h_bal` hypothesis is unsatisfiable. The fix is the reflection: **to discharge a "token at boundary `p` is not `T`" residual BY CONTRADICTION, do NOT source an unconditional helper fact about `p` — derive the helper FROM the negated-goal assumption itself. Assume the token IS `T`; that assumption pins a structural delta (here: a `.flowEntry` is balance-neutral, delta `0`) that makes the helper hold LOCALLY in that branch (the prefix balance collapses to the known outer balance), and the helper then drives the contradiction.** The boundary balance is not a free-standing fact; it is a CONSEQUENCE of the very separator assumption being refuted — so a FALSE unconditional lemma becomes a TRUE conditional derivation. ### Reflection 432 — source a multi-field provider's later field from an earlier field's output

The flat `windowFacts` provider produces `FlowBodyWindow ∧ FlowBodyContentDeepSeq ∧ SeqEnclosed`. The fields of a conjunctive provider form a DEPENDENCY DAG, not independent parallel productions — order them so each field can consume its predecessors. Sharpens [[ref-floor-encodes-nonemptiness]] (the double-duty primitive is the floor) and [[ref-conjunct-of-projection-is-free-field]] (a sibling-derivable field is "free" in the residual sense); contrast [[ref-additive-field-cost-by-keying]] (per-field cost assumes INDEPENDENT fields — the dependency edge makes a field's marginal cost zero). ### Reflection 433 — endpoint+balance bracket guards admit cross-matched false windows

The queued plan was to "discharge the three `windowFacts` primitives from whole-stream well-bracketedness", treating `h_win_dyck` (the per-window Dyck floor) as a restriction of a global fact. ### Reflection 434 — a refutation-driven guard-strengthening threads contravariantly: producer-first

R433 forced ADDING a guard (the Dyck floor) to the `h_seq_rec`/`windowFacts` universal. That universal flows across a PRODUCER → CONSUMER boundary, and the added guard costs OPPOSITELY at the two ends, by the contravariance of `→`. **On the PRODUCER (which CONCLUDES the universal from its own `windowFacts`-style hypothesis), adding the guard to the conclusion is FREE: it RECEIVES the new premise on its conclusion side and passes it straight to its hypothesis (which also gains the guard) — pure threading, no new obligation. On the CONSUMER (which HYPOTHESIZES the universal and instantiates it), adding the guard makes the hypothesis WEAKER, so at every instantiation it must now SUPPLY the guard — the real work.** So floor the PRODUCER first (free, and it pins the guard's exact shape), then pay for the CONSUMER. R434 floored `seqRec_of_carrier_and_windowFacts_seq` for free; the consumer `flowSubrangesOk_of_window_producers` floor (via `seqLocator_of_window_recseqbody`, where each instantiation should project the floor from the located window's `FlowBodyWindow.dyck`) is the next brick. This builds on [[ref-bracket-guards-admit-cross-matched-window]] (the refutation that forced the guard) and is a contravariance-cost companion to [[ref-guarded-universal-fold-relocates-guard]] (a guard is the producer's GIFT and the consumer's DEBT — here applied to a guard ADDED after the fact). ### Reflection 436 — a self-propagating guard's descent lemma is usually already built; scope the consumer re-proof by finding it

R435's redirect adds the Dyck floor as a guard at the DEFINITION (`FlowSubrangesOk.seq`/`.map`), forcing a re-proof of the parser CONSUMER `flow_parser_ok_of_structure` to supply the floor at all 8 nested `.seq`/`.map` descend sites. **The reusable finding: before re-proving a consumer to supply an added guard, SCOPE it by finding the guard's DESCENT/RESTRICTION lemma — a SELF-PROPAGATING guard (an outer instance manufactures each inner instance under structural descent) usually ALREADY has it built, often twice, for two sibling consumers that each needed the guard's structure; the redirect's cost is then THREADING + EXPOSING the guard, not DERIVING it.** The floor's descent was built twice: `flowBracketBalance_matching_close` (the parser locator) yields the matching close `j` plus the depth-`1` interior invariant `balance lo i ≥ 1` over `(k, j]` (its fifth conjunct); `flowBracketBalance_interior_dyck` (built to feed `WellTyped_subrange`) re-bases that depth-`1` floor to the inner depth-`0` floor `balance (k+1) p ≥ 0`. `flowBracketBalance_inner_floor` composes the two in four lines: an outer window's floor plus a depth-`0` opener at `k` manufactures `j` and the inner window's OWN floor — no new combinatorics. **The EXPOSE caveat** (why not reconstruct-in-place at the handed-in witness, [[ref-reconstruct-in-place-over-relocate]]): the descent-output fields (`SeqBodyProps.bracket_seq` etc.) publish only `balance (k+1) j = 0`, which does NOT pin `j` as the first-return — a cross-matched inner `j` balances too (the R433/R435 cross-matched ambiguity recurs one level down). So the consumer cannot reconstruct the inner floor at the field's `j`; the PRODUCER (which knows the genuine structure) must EXPOSE the floor as a new conjunct on each bracket-matching output field, and the consumer reads it off. This sharpens [[ref-reconstruct-in-place-over-relocate]] (the field underdetermines the witness ⇒ EXPOSE on the field, the opposite resolution), is a cleaner-reuse instance of [[ref-reduction-by-import]] / [[ref-coerce-to-weaker-reuse-wrapper]], and contrasts [[ref-window-absolute-gate-subset-restriction]] (there the descend edge is ONE monotonicity lemma because the gate is subset-restriction; here the floor RE-BASES at each opener, so the descend needs the matching-close locator).
