### Reflection 437 — a shared-structure field refinement's ripple is bounded by constructor TOPOLOGY, not count: a delegation tree collapses it to the root; vacuous leaves absorb it

R436 concluded the Dyck floor must be EXPOSED as a new conjunct on `SeqBodyProps`'s bracket fields (the field underdetermines the first-return witness, so only the producer can supply it). Exposing a guard on a SHARED STRUCTURE field is exactly the move [[ref-additive-parallel-type-over-shared-edit]] warns against — a structural edit *nominally* forces every constructor to supply the new conjunct. **The reusable finding: that "every constructor" fear is CONDITIONAL on the constructors being INDEPENDENT. When the structure's constructors form a DELEGATION TREE rooted at ONE assembler, the field-edit ripple collapses to the root — the delegators are TRANSPARENT (each just calls the root, so it recompiles against the refined field with no edit) and any vacuous leaf is ABSORBENT (`False.elim : C` for every `C`, so an added conjunct changes nothing). The true field-edit cost is then ONE root producer + the field definition + a trailing `_` at each CONSUMER that doesn't yet use the guard.** `SeqBodyProps` has five constructors; adding the floor touched ZERO of four: three delegate into `seqBodyProps_assemble` (the root, which produces the bracket field's value via `seq_bracket_{seq,map}_conjunct`), and `seqBodyProps_empty` is the vacuous `lo = hi` leaf. A SECOND, orthogonal axis: the floor ORIGINATES at the shared primitive the field-value reads (the typed locator). Enriching that primitive ripples to ALL its consumers — but only as bind-ignore noise (`_` or a one-line projection), because the new output is ADDITIVE and nobody who didn't ask for it is disturbed beyond one `_`. So a refinement on a shared structure has two cost axes, BOTH cheap when the topology is right: the field-edit collapses to the assembler root (delegation + vacuity), and the origin-enrichment of the shared primitive is additive bind-ignore. This SHARPENS/QUALIFIES [[ref-additive-parallel-type-over-shared-edit]] (the "ripples to every constructor" cost model is for INDEPENDENT constructors; a delegation tree is the exception — and the parallel-type advice is most valuable precisely when the constructors are independent), and is a structural companion to [[ref-self-propagating-guard-descent-already-built]] (R436 — WHERE the guard comes from) and [[ref-fold-consumer-chain-to-producer-contract]] (the assembler-as-single-root pattern). Demo: `Tests/Reflections/DelegationTreeCollapsesFieldRipple.lean` — a `Box` field carrying the extra `Floor` conjunct, with a root `assemble`, two delegators (`delegate1`/`delegate2`, transparent), and a vacuous leaf (`empty`, `False.elim`) all typechecking against the refined field with no floor-specific code; plus `siblingConsumer` paying one `_` for the enriched shared `locate`. New memory [[ref-delegation-tree-collapses-field-ripple]].

### Reflection 441 — docking a producer by currying an ALREADY-PROVEN composition brick discharges the producer's CONCLUSION de-risk for free (import the proof), but RELOCATES the unsatisfiability risk onto every residual HYPOTHESIS the dock threads — so probe each threaded primitive for truth

### Reflection 442 — when a sorry needs a STRONGER hypothesis than its host lemma threads, RELOCATE the sorry to the consumer that natively has the strength; don't strengthen the host's predicate (it ripples to every co-consumer)

The R441 next step's audit found the seq `FlowSubrangesOk := sorry` sitting inside a host (`scanFiltered_emitSeq_nonempty_structure`) keyed on the WEAK `EmitScansInFlowBlock`, while the seq root carrier behind the sorry needs the STRONGER `EmitScansInFlowRecEntry`, with only a strong→weak coercion available — the wrong direction to manufacture the strong predicate at the sorry. **Two ways to close a predicate-STRENGTH gap at a sorry. Read the underscores before reaching for a signature change: they map exactly which consumers a relocation spares. Here `h_pnok`/`ParseNodeFlowSeqOk` (derived from the sorry'd `FlowSubrangesOk`) was `_h_pnok` at all four `SeqInteriorSeparators` destructures and used only by `parseStream_emitSequence` (which has `Grammable` → RecEntry); moving the conjunct out left the structure lemma Block-only + seq-side sorry-free, and the seq sorry now sits at the caller where `emit_scans_in_flow_rec_entry` supplies the root carrier's RecEntry directly. ### Reflection 444 — a queued "trivial parametric generalization, no proof restructuring" of a RECURSIVE producer can hide a DESCEND-edge interface obstruction: the new bound re-establishes free at the monotone (advance) edge but is UNPROVABLE at descend, where the IH adapter exposes only the width-decrease, not the containment the bound needs; a LEAF (no edges) generalizes freely, so split the brick

The R443 Next step called the carrier-span generalization "a pure generalization with a confirmed cheap core … a one-parameter swap with the narrow bound widened, no proof restructuring," resting on the de-risk that `SeqInteriorSeparators_narrow` restricts the carrier from ANY super-window. But that de-risk is about the LEAF narrow, not the RECURSION. **A parametric bound a recursion must MAINTAIN as an invariant re-establishes for free only at edges whose adapter EXPOSES the structural relation it needs.** The carrier bound `lo0 ≤ lo ∧ hi ≤ hi0` is free at ADVANCE (`(lo,hi)→(m+1,hi)`: `lo0 ≤ lo ≤ m < m+1` by `omega`) but STUCK at DESCEND (`(lo,hi)→[lo',hi')` via the dispatch's `h_ih`, whose type surfaces only `hi'-lo' < hi-lo`): from width-decrease alone `lo0 ≤ lo'` has a countermodel. The containment that would discharge it (`lo ≤ lo' ∧ hi' ≤ hi`) is TRUE — the seq-bracket oracle descends to `[lo+1, j) ⊆ [lo, hi)` and holds both — but HIDDEN behind the callback's weaker summary, so the obstruction is an INTERFACE gap, not a mathematical one. The tell that this was missed: the "trivial" claim implicitly checked only the ADVANCE (easy) edge, which MASKS the descend (hard) edge — [[ref-easy-edge-guard-fails-hard-edge]] read at the generalization's recursion edges. **The discipline: before generalizing a recursive producer, check EACH recursion edge's adapter interface for the relation the new bound needs.** A LEAF consumer has no edges, so it always generalizes freely — split the brick and land the leaf now (additive `_general` + signature-preserving wrapper; the original becomes the root-span instance, [[ref-additive-parallel-type-over-shared-edit]]). Two routes clear the stuck edge: ROUTE A strengthen the adapter to EXPOSE the containment (cheap proof — two `omega`s the oracle already holds — but the `h_ih` callback shape ripples through the descent plumbing: oracle, dispatch, `seqChild_safeBodyUnit`, their providers); ROUTE B re-architect so the bound's consumer sits OUTSIDE the recursion (inline the single dispatch step on the co-construction's OUTER width-IH — whose width-decrease shape already matches `h_ih` — consuming the window-local carrier ONLY at the current window, so the descend goes through `h_ih` and the edge that needed containment is dissolved). ROUTE B is also how the carrier↔recursion circularity [[ref-stale-residual-framing-co-construction]] named actually dissolves. The leaf's freedom is [[ref-window-absolute-gate-subset-restriction]] (window-absolute body ⇒ bounds enter only via domain monotonicity).

### Reflection 445 — clearing a recursive producer's DESCEND-edge obstruction (R444's ROUTE A) by EXPOSING the hidden relation through a forwarded IH/callback interface has an ASYMMETRIC cost: O(chain length) signature edits but only O(consuming sinks) proof edits — the relation is proved at the sink, typed-through the forwarders, and consumed at the provider by composing it with the captured invariant

R444 named the obstruction and the two routes; R445 executes ROUTE A, and the execution taught the cost STRUCTURE of an interface exposure. Adding `lo ≤ lo' → hi' ≤ hi →` to the shared `RecSeqBody`-producing IH rippled through NINE lemmas — but the genuine proof content was TWO `omega`s. **The ripple's SIZE (signatures touched) is not its DIFFICULTY (proofs written).** The two containment premises were ADDED to nine `h_ih` types, PROVED at only the two sites the IH is genuinely CALLED (the bracket oracles' internal `h_ih (lo+1) j …`, where the descend `[lo,hi)→[lo+1,j)` makes both premises trivial), and FORWARDED VERBATIM everywhere else (every intermediate node — `seqChild_safeBodyUnit`, the dispatches, `seqDescent_provider_of_*`, the embedded IHs of `h_enc`/`h_widthEnc` — passes `h_ih` by name, carrying the premises in the `∀`-type and proving nothing). So the relation is **proved at the sink, typed-through the forwarders, and consumed at the PROVIDER**: the recursion adapter combines the CAPTURED outer invariant `lo0 ≤ lo ∧ hi ≤ hi0` with the now-exposed local containment by `Nat.le_trans` to re-establish the maintained bound at the descend child. Both recursion edges collapse to one-liners — descend = one transitivity (UNPROVABLE before the exposure, R444's countermodel), advance = one `omega` (the easy edge, no exposure needed). **The discipline: when weighing exposure (ROUTE A) against re-architecture (ROUTE B), measure the ripple by COUNTING GENUINE CALL SITES (the consuming sinks), not the forwarders.** Here the count was two, so ROUTE A was cheap despite touching nine signatures. The deliverable — `seqWindowRecSeqBody_general` / `_seq_general`, the carrier-span generalization now riding the recursion, with the root-span lemmas as thin instances ([[ref-additive-parallel-type-over-shared-edit]]) — completes the local-carrier producer R444 split off, and tightens `seqRoot_carrier_of_widthEnc`'s `h_widthEnc` interface (now containment-carrying) for the co-construction [[ref-stale-residual-framing-co-construction]] named. Sharpens [[ref-guarded-universal-fold-relocates-guard]] (proved-where vs consumed-where across a forwarded universal). New memory [[ref-interface-exposure-asymmetric-ripple]].

### Reflection 446 — generalizing a producer from a fixed (root) span to an arbitrary window is exactly ONE swap of the BASE-CASE assembler: a producer that descends into sub-windows it does not own threads a descent route that is already window-parametric, so the only root-specific ingredient is the FLAT base supplier + span literals; lift those to arguments and the root version is recovered as a `rfl`-level literal instance

The R445 Next step queued the co-construction's part (a) as "a window-local analog of `seqRoot_carrier_of_widthEnc`." Before authoring a fresh window-local proof, R446 re-read `seqRoot_carrier_of_widthEnc` and found nearly all of it was ALREADY window-parametric. **A producer that descends into sub-windows it does not own threads a descent route whose lemmas all take the window bounds as arguments — only its BASE CASE bakes in the root span and the flat, recursion-free base supplier.** `seqRoot_carrier_of_widthEnc` drove `desc` through `seqRoot_seqInteriorSeparators` (literal `[2,size-2)` + `seqRoot_safeBodyUnit`); the chain it threads (`seqEnclosingOpener_of_gate` → `h_widthEnc` → `seqEnclosed_succ_of_located_opener` → `seqDescent_provider_of_located`) reads no literal. So the generalization isolated to ONE swap: replace the root assembler with the window-parametric `seqInteriorSeparators_of_safebody_and_descent`, LIFT the window `SafeBodyUnit` as a hypothesis, re-base `h_widthEnc`'s bounds — and the proof body is otherwise term-for-term, the root version recovered as the `lo:=2`, `hi:=size-2` instance fed the flat base (a `rfl`-level delegation, [[ref-additive-parallel-type-over-shared-edit]]). **The discipline: when generalizing a producer from a fixed span to an arbitrary window, measure the work by what the BASE CASE bakes in — span literals and the flat base supplier — and lift exactly those; do not re-prove the descent.** This is the consume-side dual of [[ref-root-seed-recursive-producer-swap]] (there: swap the recursive body INTO an existing flat-fact slice, keeping the slice; here: swap the flat base OUT of an existing window-parametric descent, keeping the descent). The measure that makes the next round's joint induction sound — every IH callee strictly narrower than `[lo,hi)`, even at the self-instantiation where the descent's enclosing window equals the whole window — was de-risked by `#guard` (`SeqLocalCarrierWidthProbe`, [[ref-probe-deferred-universal-before-producing]] / [[ref-minimal-pair-extracts-the-gate]]) before committing. New memory [[ref-root-to-window-base-assembler-swap]].

### Reflection 447 — a producer reused to break a circularity that routes through a SPINE-walking navigator inherits the spine's WHOLE-PATH invariant as a gate; that gate constrains the ANCESTOR stack, while the consumer's guard asserts only the window's OWN enclosing frame (vacuous over ancestors) — so the gate is NOT a projection of the guard and must be THREADED through the consuming recursion, seeded vacuously at the root

The R446 Next step queued the joint induction's first sub-task as "find/build the per-nested-value emission-flat `SafeBodyUnit` producer" for the within-window `h_safe`, ASSUMING (implicitly) it would be obtainable at each window from the joint-induction guard. R447 found the producer ALREADY exists (`nestedSeq_safeBodyUnit_of_locator`, R387) — but it routes through the forward locator, which walks an all-seq bracket SPINE, so it inherits `h_path : SeqPathAllSeq tokens (lo-1)`. **The guard the recursion carries asserts only the window's OWN enclosing frame; the spine navigator's gate constrains the whole ANCESTOR path — different stack regions, so the gate cannot be derived from the guard.** Concretely `SeqEnclosed tokens lo = (btFold (take lo)).bind (·.head?) = some true` reads the head (the window's own `[`, always `true` for a seq window — VACUOUS over ancestors `p = btFold (take (lo-1))`), while `SeqPathAllSeq tokens (lo-1) = allSeq p` reads all of `p`. The MINIMAL PAIR ([[ref-minimal-pair-extracts-the-gate]]) proving non-derivability: a seq under a map (`[{a:[b]}]`'s `[b]`) and a genuine all-seq window share the OWN frame (`SeqEnclosed`) yet differ on the gate — the map leaves a `false` deeper in `p` (`SeqPathAllSeqGateProbe`, `#guard`). **The discipline: when the producer you reuse to break a circularity routes through a navigator that walks a TYPED SPINE, it inherits the spine's WHOLE-PATH invariant; your consumer's guard typically pins only the window's OWN frame — so thread the gate through the recursion via a descend edge (push the own frame onto the ancestor stack), seeded at the root by the invariant's vacuous (empty) case even though the root itself FAILS the gate.** The root is the dispatch exception — `SeqPathAllSeq tokens 1` fails (empty stack), so the root sources `h_safe` flat from `seqRoot_safeBodyUnit` ([[ref-root-seed-discriminator-not-from-gate]]) while every nested window the recursion descends into satisfies the gate (the seq recursion only descends `[`→`[`, never meeting a `false`). R447 lands the root-vs-nested dispatch `seqWindow_safeBodyUnit` naming the `h_safe` interface ([[ref-consumer-joint-before-producer]] / [[ref-parametric-assembler-extraction]]); the threaded `SeqPathAllSeq` descend edge (the btFold-push preservation) is the next residual. Sharpens [[ref-minimal-pair-extracts-the-gate]] and complements [[ref-window-absolute-gate-subset-restriction]] (there the gate's body is window-absolute and re-bases on domain bounds; here the gate is a whole-path invariant threaded by a descend push). New memory [[ref-top-frame-guard-vs-spine-gate]].

### Reflection 448 — a UNIVERSAL producer over a domain predicate D cannot be completed by a NAVIGATOR whose reachable domain is a STRICT SUBSET of D; the gap is a structurally-SEVERED sub-domain (the navigator's recursive structure stores only a FLAT witness at its foreign-type constructor, dead-ending the spine), reachable only by a SIBLING navigator — which is therefore on the producer's CRITICAL PATH, not a downstream concern

R447 surfaced that the seq joint induction's per-window `h_safe` must be THREADED (the locator's `SeqPathAllSeq` gate is not derivable from the guard); R448 set out to thread it, found both threading edges already proven (R337), and on executing the joint induction hit a deeper, structural obstruction. **The seq ROOT CARRIER `SeqInteriorSeparators tokens 2 (size-2)` is a UNIVERSAL over a domain predicate** — `∀ a b, … → SeqTypedInterior tokens a b → bodySuccFact ∧ noTrailingSepFact` — and `SeqTypedInterior` pins only the TOP bracket frame `[` (path-blind), so its domain INCLUDES map-nested seqs (`[{a:[b]}]`'s `[b]`). The all-seq locator that sources `h_safe` reaches only `SeqPathAllSeq` (whole path `[`) windows. **So the producer's domain is strictly wider than the navigator's reach**, and the gap is not a patchable edge case: the seq `RecSeqBody` spine the locator walks SEVERS at `RecSeqEntry.map` (which stores only `WellBracketed interior`, not the recursive `RecMapBody` — [[ref-stored-vs-projected-severs-recursion-edge]]), so map-nested seqs are structurally unreachable from the seq side ([[ref-severed-edge-bounds-navigator-domain]]). They live behind the SIBLING structure `RecMapBody`/`RecMapPair` (value field re-enters `RecSeqEntry`), reachable only by a MAP-PATH locator (the map mirror). **The discipline: before sourcing a universal producer's per-element witness from a reused navigator, compare the navigator's reachable-domain gate against the producer's domain D; if D is wider, the missed elements are a severed sub-domain needing the SIBLING navigator — check the recursive structure's foreign-type constructor for whether it stores the recursive or only the flat witness.** The consequence re-scopes the seq endgame: the map mirror is on the seq root carrier's CRITICAL PATH (not just the map half of `FlowSubrangesOk`), and R447's 2-way `h_safe` dispatch `seqWindow_safeBodyUnit` is necessary but insufficient (a 3rd map-path arm owed). Builds on [[ref-top-frame-guard-vs-spine-gate]] (R447); corrects [[ref-stale-residual-framing-co-construction]] (the seq root carrier is not the LAST seq-only residual). New memory [[ref-carrier-domain-wider-than-navigator-reach]].

### Reflection 449 — a SEVERED recursive edge does not cost ONE sibling navigator; it costs a navigator PER nesting level. When a deliverable stores a FLAT witness at its foreign-type constructor, EACH navigator crosses that foreign boundary at most ONCE (descending into the structure the producer built AT that boundary), so a target nested behind k foreign boundaries needs k crossings and is unreachable for k ≥ 2. A PATH-BLIND producer domain admits unbounded nesting depth — so the gap cannot be closed by adding ONE sibling navigator; the deliverable itself must store a RECURSIVE witness at the foreign constructor (mutual recursion to any depth)

R448 found the seq root carrier needs the MAP MIRROR (a sibling navigator) on its critical path, because the seq spine severs at `RecSeqEntry.map`. R449 probed the map mirror's single-step shape and found the sibling navigator is necessary but NOT sufficient — the severance RECURSES. **The move decision is sound and cheap** (`map_move_trichotomy`: DESCEND-KEY / DESCEND-VALUE / ADVANCE by pure length arithmetic on the stored `block_k`/`block_v`, the map analog of R350's seq `move_trichotomy` — no balance front end), and below the key/value descent the map navigator hands off to the EXISTING seq `RecSeqEntry`/`RecSeqBody` machinery (`RecMapPair` stores both key and value as `RecSeqEntry`s). **But `RecSeqEntry.map` stores only `WellBracketed interior` — no recursive `RecMapBody` — so the MAP navigator dead-ends at a NESTED map precisely as the seq navigator dead-ends at a map.** `#guard`-probed (`MapPathLocatorMoveProbe`): `[{a:[b]}]`/`[{a:[b,c]}]` (map-depth 1) are REACHABLE (target seq is the map value, a `RecSeqEntry.seq`); `[{a:{x:[b]}}]` (map-depth 2) is a SECOND severance, UNREACHABLE — yet all three are in the carrier's path-blind domain `SeqTypedInterior`. **The discipline: when a severed recursive edge forces a sibling navigator, check whether the foreign boundary RECURS — if the deliverable stores a flat witness at the foreign constructor and the producer's domain is path-blind (admits the foreign frame at any depth), ONE sibling crosses only the first boundary; closing the whole domain needs the deliverable to store a RECURSIVE witness at the foreign constructor, turning the navigators into a MUTUAL recursion that descends any depth.** The consequence sharpens R448's re-scope: the route is a SEPARATE map navigator over `RecMapBody` (the key/value split has no seq analog), but full coverage of `SeqTypedInterior` requires the FULLY-RECURSIVE map interior (`RecSeqEntry.map` storing `RecMapBody`, the doc's deferred refinement) — not merely the map mirror over today's depth-1 deliverable. Sharpens [[ref-carrier-domain-wider-than-navigator-reach]] (R448: the gap is one severed sub-domain → here the severance is a LADDER, one severance per nesting level) and [[ref-severed-edge-bounds-navigator-domain]]; the move arithmetic mirrors [[ref-width-recursion-combinator-before-grammar-step]] (R365). New memory [[ref-severance-recurses-by-nesting-depth]].

### Reflection 450 — an ADDITIVE recursive field is trivial at the TYPE level, but its PRODUCER can force a MUTUAL recursion the existing acyclic producer-CITATION DAG forbids; before pricing "additive field = cheap", trace the field's producer citation graph — the recursive ASSEMBLER is a hypothesis-parametrized LEAF, so supplying the field makes each construction site discharge its hypotheses from sibling producers, and if one sibling ALREADY cites the producer you are editing, the field closes a citation cycle (#1 ↔ #2) requiring a `mutual` block; the type edit is a DECOY, the cost is the producer mutual recursion

R449 concluded the bounded-cost fix for a path-blind LADDER of severances is to store a RECURSIVE witness at the foreign constructor, landed ADDITIVELY, and its route note read "additive field likely wins — the producer already builds the `RecMapBody` at one level; the gap is only that `RecSeqEntry.map` discards it." R450 reads the producers and finds the second clause is the trap. **The TYPE field is one line** (`RecSeqEntry.map` adds `h_rec : RecMapBody interior`, keeps `h_wb`), and the recursive assembler `emitPairList_scans_recmapbody` ALREADY exists, delivering a full `RecMapBody` (a superset of the flat pair producer). **But the assembler is a hypothesis-parametrized LEAF** — it inducts on `pairs` and takes the per-key/per-value recursive deliverables as HYPOTHESES, citing no producer. **To SUPPLY the field, both `RecSeqEntry.map` construction sites must CALL the assembler and DISCHARGE its hypotheses from the sibling producers** — the per-key one from the saved-key producer #2, the per-value one from the value producer #1. So #1 must cite #2; but #2 already cites #1 (its `.seq` value bodies are fed by the value producer). **#1 → #2 (new) + #2 → #1 (existing) is a citation CYCLE Lean forbids outside a `mutual` block** — so #1 and #2 must become a `mutual theorem` block (structural on the `emit`/`YamlValue` tree), exactly where the mutual-block gotchas live; the assembler #3 stays a leaf. **Two facts make the cost hidden and mislead:** (a) the DATA types already mutually reference each other (`RecSeqEntry` ↔ `RecMapBody`), so "the recursion already exists" is TRUE — but at the type level, not the producer level; (b) the assembler already exists as a proven leaf. Neither is the cost; the cost lives in the PRODUCERS' termination structure. **The contrast that proves the point:** the value producer's `.seq` arm feeds the recursive seq-body producer from its OWN induction hypothesis — no sibling, no back-edge — so the seq recursion rode the single self-recursion for FREE; the map recursion cannot, because the map body needs the SAVED-KEY deliverable (a different scan path, not the value IH) for its keys, and that sibling cites back. **The discipline: when the fix for a path-blind severance is "store a recursive witness additively", do a PRODUCER-SIDE probe BEFORE the type change — find the recursive assembler (confirm it is a parametrized leaf), find each construction site (grep the constructor), and check the citation DIRECTION among the siblings that discharge its hypotheses; a back-edge means the field forces a `mutual` recursion, so price the field by that refactor, not the one-line type edit.** Sharpens [[ref-severance-recurses-by-nesting-depth]] (R449: the fix is the additive recursive field → here that field's PRODUCER is the real cost) and qualifies [[ref-additive-parallel-type-over-shared-edit]] (additive-over-structural keeps CONSUMERS untouched, but the additive field's PRODUCER can still force a mutual recursion); extends [[ref-stored-vs-projected-severs-recursion-edge]] from one producer's recursion graph to the CITATION graph across producers. New memory [[ref-additive-field-forces-producer-mutual-recursion]].

### Reflection 451 — when two mutually-CITING producers recurse on the SAME inductive, the citation cycle (Reflection 450) does NOT need a `mutual theorem` block; prove the CONJUNCTION of their deliverables by ONE induction and the shared IH carries BOTH at every sub-value, so each arm reads its component off the IH (`.1`/`.2`) instead of citing the sibling. A mutual-THEOREM block is forced ONLY when the two recurse on DIFFERENT data; same-data ⇒ conjunction-motive single induction, strictly simpler — the mutual recursion stays in the DATA, the PRODUCER collapses to one ordinary theorem

R450 priced the additive-field fix as restructuring the value producer #1 and the saved-key producer #2 into a `mutual theorem` block. R451 executed R450's own first sub-task — "de-risk the `mutual theorem` shape FIRST" — and found the block is UNNECESSARY. **The key observation R450 missed: #1 (`emit_scans_in_flow_rec_entry`) and #2 (`emit_scans_in_flow_saved_key_rec_entry`) BOTH prove their result by `induction hg` on the SAME `Grammable v inFlow`** (structurally recursive on `YamlValue`; its `sequence`/`mapping` constructors carry the sub-value `Grammable` proofs under `∀ i : Fin _.size`). **A `mutual theorem` block is forced only when two producers recurse on DIFFERENT data.** When they share the recursion, the cycle resolves to ONE theorem proving the CONJUNCTION of the two deliverables — `Grammable v inFlow → EmitScansInFlowRecEntry v ∧ EmitScansInFlowSavedKeyRecEntry v` — by a single `induction hg`; the shared induction hypothesis then carries BOTH deliverables at every sub-value, so each arm reads off the component it needs rather than citing the sibling: **#2's seq arm's #2→#1 edge (`:3233`) becomes `(ih i).1`; #1's map arm reads the saved-key keys for assembler #3 from `(ihk i).2` and the value values from `(ihv i).1`.** The original #1/#2 become thin `.1`/`.2` projections, so their signatures — and ALL consumers — stay unchanged. **The mutual recursion never needed to live in the PRODUCERS:** it already lives, and stays, in the DATA (`RecSeqEntry` ↔ `RecMapBody`, a mutual INDUCTIVE); the producer is ONE ordinary theorem by one `induction`, dodging every Reflection-234 `mutual`-THEOREM gotcha (`induction`-inside-`mutual`, cross-call termination, `Or`-nesting). **The de-risk is DECISIVE because it ran on the ACTUAL `Grammable` recursor with the ACTUAL `∀ i : Fin _.size` array nesting** (the part R450's binary-tree toy did NOT exercise): a lightweight mirror — mutual INDUCTIVE `EValue`↔`ESkey` for the two deliverables' shapes (cross-edges in the constructors) + `grammable_gives_both` by one `induction hg` — compiles, so the real (voluminous) merge is now mechanical (pair the existing per-arm bodies as `⟨value-arm, saved-key-arm⟩`, swap each sibling-call for the matching IH projection). **The discipline: before pricing a producer citation cycle as a `mutual theorem` refactor, check whether the two producers recurse on the SAME inductive (the tell: both `induction` on the same hypothesis); if so, the conjunction-motive single induction is the cheaper resolution.** A GOTCHA the probe hit on its FIRST build: a doc comment `/-- -/` cannot attach to the `mutual` keyword even for a mutual INDUCTIVE (not just a theorem) — use plain `/- -/` (Reflection 234, confirmed for the inductive case). Corrects [[ref-additive-field-forces-producer-mutual-recursion]] (R450's "mutual theorem block" cost) and generalises [[ref-recursive-producer-mirrors-flat-over-shared-induction]] (one IH now serves TWO deliverables, not one); the unchanged-consumer property mirrors [[ref-additive-parallel-type-over-shared-edit]] lifted from the type to the producer. New memory [[ref-conjunction-motive-breaks-producer-cycle]].

### Reflection 452 — EXECUTING a conjunction-motive producer merge (Reflection 451) is a MECHANICAL ZIP whose semantic edit count = the number of per-child WITNESS-CONSUMPTION sites across both bodies (own-IH uses + sibling cross-citations), NOT the body size; each site becomes one `(ih …).i` projection and everything else transports VERBATIM under the two conjunct bullets, so a 760-line merge costs exactly 2 edits — before committing, COUNT the witness sites, not the lines

R451 de-risked the conjunction-motive merge on a TOY (no body bulk); R452 EXECUTED it on the REAL producers — #1 `emit_scans_in_flow_rec_entry` (value, ~300 lines) + #2 `emit_scans_in_flow_saved_key_rec_entry` (saved-key, ~430 lines) → one `emit_scans_in_flow_rec_entry_both (v) (hg : Grammable v inFlow) : EmitScansInFlowRecEntry v ∧ EmitScansInFlowSavedKeyRecEntry v` by a single `induction hg`. **The execution revealed the COST LAW the de-risk could not show: the merge is a ZIP of the two `induction` arms, and its edit count equals the number of per-child DELIVERABLE-WITNESS consumption sites — not the body size.** Wrap each arm in `refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩`, drop the value body under the first conjunct bullet and the saved-key body under the second, and transport BOTH bodies VERBATIM (a constant indentation shift, done by SCRIPT — the content is inert payload). The ONLY content edits: **(a)** every place a body consumes a per-child witness becomes the matching conjunction-IH projection — #1's OWN-IH use `ih ⟨i,_⟩` (now typed as a *pair* by the changed motive) and #2's by-name SIBLING citation `emit_scans_in_flow_rec_entry _ (h ⟨i,_⟩)` (`:3233`, the lone #2→#1 cross-edge) BOTH collapse to the SAME `(ih ⟨i,_⟩).1`; **(b)** a per-arm binder UNION (promote #2's underscored `_ih` → `ih`, now consumed by the merged `sequence` arm). **Why 760 lines cost 2 edits:** only the two `sequence` arms consume a per-child witness. The `mapping` arms feed off FLAT black-box wrappers (`emit_scans_in_flow_block`/`_saved_key_block`) and build `RecSeqEntry.map`, which stores only `WellBracketed` (the SEVERANCE — no recursive child witness, [[ref-stored-vs-projected-severs-recursion-edge]]); the `scalar` arms are leaves. Both are INERT w.r.t. the IH ⇒ ZERO edits, pure verbatim transport. The merge introduces NO new proof obligation (the conjunction IH already delivers at every sub-value exactly what each site consumed), so it is FRONTIER-NEUTRAL and the de-risk→execute gap is ~zero. **The discipline: before committing to a conjunction-motive merge, COUNT the per-child witness-consumption sites (grep the sibling producer's NAME in the other's body + the own-IH uses) — that count is the true edit count and the whole risk surface; body volume is a red herring. Do the re-indentation by SCRIPT (a constant prefix shift preserves nested bullet structure).** Re-expose the two originals as thin `.1`/`.2` projections so signatures — and all consumers — stay unchanged ([[ref-additive-parallel-type-over-shared-edit]] at the producer level: the combined theorem is the new joint carrier, the two projections the old interfaces). Sharpens [[ref-conjunction-motive-breaks-producer-cycle]] (R451 found the merge possible without a mutual block; R452 prices its execution); the inert `mapping`-arm severance is the very field the NEXT step restores. New memory [[ref-conjunction-merge-cost-is-citation-edges]]; demo `Tests/Reflections/ConjunctionMergeCostIsCitationEdges.lean`.

### Reflection 453 — additivity reasoning that holds for a shared inductive's CONSUMERS (a `cases`/`match` arm ignores a new field) FAILS for its CONSTRUCTORS (every builder must supply it); before adding a REQUIRED field to carry a deferred refinement, enumerate every CONSTRUCTION site and classify each by ROLE/STRENGTH — a deliverable built in TWO roles at different strengths cannot take a required field on the SHARED constructor (the weak-role builder has nothing to fill it), so split off a SEPARATE constructor for the strong role, NOT a field on the shared one

R452's queued step was "(2) ADD the field `h_rec : RecMapBody interior` to `RecSeqEntry.map` — additive, all consumers ignore it." R453 read the actual construction sites BEFORE editing and found the additivity claim is a category error. **A `cases`/`match` arm ignores a new field, so CONSUMERS are untouched — but every BUILDER of the constructor must SUPPLY the field, and that is where two-role deliverables break.** Enumerating the four `RecSeqEntry.map` construction sites and classifying each by ROLE: **(a) PRODUCER role** — `emit_scans_in_flow_rec_entry_both`'s two mapping bullets HAVE a `RecMapBody` (from the assembler `emitPairList_scans_recmapbody`), can fill it; **(b) SEQ-NAVIGATOR role** — `recseqentry_map_window` (`NonemptyStructure.lean:5455`) / `recseqentry_map_dispatch` (`:5829`), the seq locate driver's NEAR-LEAF — the R335/R449 severance where the seq path stops descending — synthesize `RecSeqEntry.map` from RAW BALANCE (`flowBracketBalance` / `WellBracketed interior`), have NO `RecMapBody`, cannot recover one (it needs the key/value structure the balance-only locate never computed), and feed the live `recseqentry_classify` chain so cannot be deleted. **A required field is uninhabitable by role (b)** — and unlike a consumer, the builder cannot ignore it. **The test that exposes it: for the field's type `F interior`, ask whether the weak role's fact `W interior` DETERMINES `F`; here `∃ interior, WellBracketed interior ∧ ¬ RecMapBody interior` (a balance-only nested mapping has no forced key/value structure), so there is no total `W → F` and the required field cannot be built by the weak role.** (The newer `nestedSeq_recseqentry_locate_*` family at `:5087`/`:5101` COULD thread the field from its `cases h_e` on an incoming `RecSeqBody`; the navigator near-leaf cannot — the cleavage is between builders that consume an existing typed witness and builders that synthesize from coarse data.) **The resolution — a SEPARATE constructor `RecSeqEntry.mapRec`** carrying `h_rec : RecMapBody interior`: the seq navigator keeps building the FLAT `map` (unchanged, keeps severing), the producer builds `mapRec`, the map navigator descends only `mapRec`; each ~13 `RecSeqEntry` matcher gains one verbatim `mapRec` arm (reads the balance fact, ignores `h_rec`). **This is the additive-parallel refinement done RIGHT — the principle [[ref-additive-parallel-type-over-shared-edit]] means a new CONSTRUCTOR whose strong field only the strong role fills, NOT a new FIELD on the shared constructor** (which is exactly the "structural edit to the shared/polymorphic type" it forbids; the prior plan MIS-cited it as justification for the field). **A second, independent risk surfaced the same round:** the strong field comes from a DIFFERENT scan than the flat facts — the producer's map arm reads `OpenerAdj`/`SepAdj`/tail off the flat `EmitPairListScansInFlowBlock` scan (22 conjuncts), but `emitPairList_scans_recmapbody`'s output (`:2194-2214`, 19 conjuncts) carries `RecMapBody` and DROPS those, so it is NOT a superset; wiring needs either a determinism reconciliation (`ScanChain_deterministic` wants EQUAL step counts, so the two existential `n`s must be proven equal first) OR (cleaner) strengthening the assembler to a single-scan SUPERSET carrying every flat conjunct PLUS `RecMapBody`, mirroring how the seq side's `emitList_scans_recseqbody` supersets `emitList_scans_safebody`. The two-roles-at-different-strengths trap is the construction-site dual of [[ref-coerce-to-weaker-reuse-wrapper]] (there ONE producer / two consumers → coerce strong→weak; here ONE consumer-shape / two PRODUCERS → split the constructor); the "name the case the abstraction can't represent and check it arises" move is [[ref-derisk-consumer-blindspot-vs-contract]] applied to a constructor field; the severance the seq navigator stops at is [[ref-stored-vs-projected-severs-recursion-edge]]. New memory [[ref-two-role-deliverable-blocks-shared-field]]; demo `Tests/Reflections/TwoRoleDeliverableBlocksSharedField.lean` (axiom-free).

### Reflection 454 — adding a constructor whose FIELD TYPE lives in a downstream, originally NON-`mutual` group of the same recursive family silently FORCES the two groups to MERGE into one `mutual` block (the field closes a dependency cycle); the additive-constructor cost (one verbatim arm per matcher) holds as predicted, but the MERGE is the hidden cost — price it, and it is SAFE iff the moved declarations reference nothing defined BETWEEN the merge target and their old site (and moving a declaration strictly EARLIER never breaks use-ordering)

R453 resolved the blocked shared-field plan with a SEPARATE `RecSeqEntry.mapRec` constructor, priced as "add a constructor + one verbatim arm per matcher (~13)." R454 EXECUTED it; the 13-arm prediction held EXACTLY (each arm a verbatim mirror reading `h_wb`, ignoring `h_rec`; green on the first full build — no matcher missed, no term-mode recursion broken). **The under-priced cost: the new constructor's field type `RecMapBody` lived in a DOWNSTREAM, originally-NON-`mutual` group.** `RecMapBody`/`RecMapPair` sat ~1500 lines after `RecSeqEntry`'s group, depending on `RecSeqEntry` ONE-DIRECTIONALLY (`RecMapBody → RecMapPair → RecSeqEntry`) — so the original design correctly used no `mutual` block. Adding `RecSeqEntry.mapRec : … → RecMapBody interior → …` adds the back-edge `RecSeqEntry → RecMapBody`, turning the one-directional dependency into a genuine CYCLE `RecSeqEntry → RecMapBody → RecMapPair → RecSeqEntry`. **A cycle must be co-declared, so the additive constructor silently FORCED a four-inductive mutual-group MERGE** (`RecSeqBody`/`RecSeqEntry`/`RecMapPair`/`RecMapBody` into one block; the obsolete "no mutual needed" header rewritten). **The merge is SAFE by an ordering argument, checkable before editing:** moving the downstream INDUCTIVE DECLARATIONS up is sound iff they reference nothing defined BETWEEN the target block and their old site — here `RecMapPair`/`RecMapBody`'s declarations reference only `RecSeqEntry` + token constructors (their PROJECTION theorems, which DO use intervening lemmas, stay at the old site; only the bare `inductive` declarations move), and moving a declaration strictly EARLIER can NEVER break use-ordering (every consumer sat after the old position, hence still after the new, earlier one). The structural recursions on the moved inductive survived the merge (recursing on ONE inductive of a mutual family is exactly what the joint recursor supports). **The discipline: when adding a constructor whose field type `F` is a recursive type whose group (transitively) references the type you are EXTENDING, the new field closes a cycle and the groups MUST merge into one `mutual` block — diagnose this BEFORE editing (does `F`'s group reference your type?), price the merge, and verify safety via the no-references-in-between + earlier-declaration-ordering checks.** Sharpens [[ref-two-role-deliverable-blocks-shared-field]] (R453 priced the separate constructor but not the mutual-group MERGE its field type forces) and [[ref-additive-parallel-type-over-shared-edit]] (an additive CONSTRUCTOR can have a non-additive STRUCTURAL consequence — pulling a downstream group into the block — even while leaving every consumer untouched); the severance the flat `.map` preserves is [[ref-stored-vs-projected-severs-recursion-edge]] / [[ref-severance-recurses-by-nesting-depth]]. New memory [[ref-constructor-field-forces-mutual-group-merge]]; demo `Tests/Reflections/ConstructorFieldForcesMutualGroupMerge.lean` (axiom-FREE).

### Reflection 455 — which members of a recursive deliverable's PROJECTION FAMILY are derivable from the type splits by READ LOCUS: BOUNDARY reads (last-token facts) survive a constructor's recursion-severance and project off the type; INTERIOR reads (every-seat adjacency) do NOT — the severed constructor stores only a balance predicate that admits an interior counterexample, so those facts stay SCAN-THREADED. Probe whether the interior projection is even a THEOREM (find the severed-constructor counterexample) before trying to derive it.

Stepping into STEP D step 2 (strengthen the assembler so the map arms can read both the flat facts AND `RecMapBody` from one scan), the appealing shortcut was to COLLAPSE the whole cascade: the assembler already produces `RecMapBody body`, so DERIVE all four body facts the map wrap needs (`OpenerAdj`, `SepAdj`, last≠`[`, last≠`,`) from `RecMapBody` via projection methods — the way `RecSeqBody.lastNonOpener`/`.openerAdjHead` are derived (`NonemptyStructure.lean:876`/`:915`, used at `:3025`). **R455 found this works for HALF the family and is provably IMPOSSIBLE for the other half, and the split is exactly boundary-vs-interior.** The BOUNDARY facts — last token ≠ `[` / ≠ `,` — ARE derivable from `RecMapBody`: the last token is the final pair's value-block end (a scalar / `]` / `}`), a datum fixed by the constructor SHAPE and read off the value entry's balance-based `EntryUnit` (`lastNonOpener_of_entryUnit`), so it holds for ANY value entry — flat `.map` included, because the last token is structure-blind at the boundary. Those four landed this round (`RecMapBody.getLast?_not_opener`/`.lastNonOpener` + the `getLast?_not_sep`/`lastNonSep` twins, mirrors of the `RecSeqBody` quartet; build green, frontier-neutral, axiom-clean `[propext, Quot.sound]`). The INTERIOR facts — `OpenerAdj`/`SepAdj`, which inspect EVERY interior `[`/`,` seat — are NOT derivable: `RecSeqEntry`'s flat `map` constructor (the R453/R454 severance) stores only `h_wb : WellBracketed interior`, and **`WellBracketed` does not imply `OpenerAdj`** — a balanced block can still seat a `[` next to a non-content token, so a flat-`map` entry (hence `RecMapBody`) cannot yield interior adjacency. The would-be `RecSeqEntry.openerAdj`/`RecMapBody.openerAdj` is FALSE on the flat-`map` case; the demo `severed_admits_bad_interior` manufactures the counterexample (`wrapFlat [bad] trivial` is a legal entry whose interior IS the forbidden token). **So `OpenerAdj`/`SepAdj` of the body MUST stay SCAN-THREADED** (proven by the actual emit, where the tokens really are well-formed) — there is no derive-from-the-type shortcut, and the assembler-strengthening cascade is unavoidable for those two. **The reusable law: a deliverable's projection family splits by READ LOCUS — boundary reads survive any interior severance ([[ref-stored-vs-projected-severs-recursion-edge]]: the stored-vs-projected edge that severs the recursion also bounds which projections are recoverable); interior reads are owed to whatever proof DID see the interior.** The de-risk move that saved a doomed deep mutual induction: PROBE whether `RecSeqEntry.openerAdj` is even a theorem ([[ref-probe-deferred-universal-before-producing]]) — the flat-`map` counterexample answers no in one line, so don't chase it. Sharpens [[ref-complete-projection-family-for-new-member]] (completing a new member's family means completing the BOUNDARY half off the type; the interior half is a separate scan-threaded obligation). New memory [[ref-severed-constructor-boundary-projects-interior-doesnt]]; demo `Tests/Reflections/SeveredConstructorBoundaryProjectsInteriorDoesnt.lean` (axiom-clean `[propext]`).

### Reflection 456 — strengthening a predicate whose INTERMEDIATE existential SEVERED a fact set is a verbatim MIRROR-TRANSPORT from the sibling arm that did NOT sever: the proof content pre-exists in the mirror, so the cost is re-exposing the dropped binders + the same wrap lemmas, not new derivation; the wrapped output fact splits into a BOUNDARY half (free off the deliverable's projection, R455) and an INTERIOR half (re-threaded from the scan)

The proof content pre-existed; the cost was re-exposing the dropped binder + the same wrap lemmas. **The split is R455's:** the BOUNDARY inputs (head/tail/lns) come FREE off `RecSeqBody.openerAdjHead`/`.lastNonOpener`/`.lastNonSep` — boundary projections off the recursive witness the intermediate already carries; the INTERIOR inputs (`OpenerAdj`/`SepAdj`) are RE-THREADED (recseqbody already proves them; the arm had merely dropped them — un-drop, don't re-run the scan). The scalar arm is `*_singleton`; the mapping arm un-bundles the flat `h_pair_scan` (`_h_body_tail` → `h_body_tail, h_body_oa, h_body_lns, _h_body_keyhead, h_body_sa`) which already carried all four, and wraps via the `_wrap_map` family (no head fact — the `{` opener is inert). **The consumer side stayed additive:** the assembler's two key destructures (`:2284`/`:2452`) absorbed the four new conjuncts behind their catch-all `h_ke` — only the CONSTRUCTING `RecMapPair.mk` forced un-bundling `h_ke` back to `RecSeqEntry` (the [[ref-conjunct-of-projection-is-free-field]] / additive-consumer pattern, dual to the constructor cost). ### Reflection 457 — a projection method you proved for a deliverable (for a DOWNSTREAM consumer) is a FORWARD REFERENCE at an UPSTREAM producer that BUILDS the deliverable: the producer cannot call its own downstream projection, so rebuild the needed boundary fact from the LOCAL constituents the producer already has — the SAME constituents the projection itself is built from — and the two routes coincide

Executing step 2b (strengthen the assembler `emitPairList_scans_recmapbody` to carry body `OpenerAdj`/`SepAdj`), two things showed up. **First, the R456 cascade ordering paid off exactly as designed:** the per-pair `OpenerAdj_map_single`/`SepAdj_map_single` glue needs the KEY's `OpenerAdj`/`SepAdj`/tail (now supplied by the R456-strengthened key predicate, read off the renamed `h_oa_k`/`h_sa_k`/`h_tail_k`/`h_lns_k`) AND the VALUE's `OpenerAdj`/`SepAdj` (un-bundled from `EmitScansInFlowRecEntry`'s `_h_cs_v` catch-all into `h_oa_v`/`h_sa_v`); the base case is one `_map_single` per side, the cons case glues per-pair via `OpenerAdj_seam`/`SepAdj_seam` to the recursive tail's `OpenerAdj`/`SepAdj` (now in the IH). So strengthening the key predicate FIRST (R456) was the genuine unlock — the assembler transport was mechanical once both halves were available. **Second, the FORWARD-REFERENCE trap:** the seam needs each entry's TAIL-not-opener fact, and R455 had just landed `RecMapBody.lastNonOpener` — exactly this boundary fact off the deliverable. The natural move `(RecMapBody.single _ … h_pair …).lastNonOpener` FAILED: `RecMapBody.lastNonOpener` is declared ~1400 lines DOWNSTREAM of the assembler (R455 placed it near the future map NAVIGATOR, a consumer that lives later in the file), so at the assembler it is an unknown identifier. **A producer that BUILDS a deliverable sits UPSTREAM of the projections proved for that deliverable's downstream consumers; it cannot call them.** The fix: rebuild the boundary fact from the LOCAL constituents the producer already has — the entry ends in its VALUE block (`entry = front ++ block_v`), so the entry's tail-not-opener is `lastNonOpener_append_right _ block_v h_bv_ne (lastNonOpener_of_entryUnit block_v h_ve.toEntryUnit)` (and tail-not-sep the `lastNonSep` twin off the value's content-start head `_h_cs_v`). These are EXACTLY the constituents `RecMapBody.lastNonOpener` itself recurses to (the last pair's value block); producer and projection share the same underlying derivation, only the entry point differs by declaration site. `h_bv_ne : block_v ≠ []` came inline from `cases h_ve <;> simp` (since `RecSeqEntry.ne_nil` is ALSO downstream). Build green (707 jobs), frontier-neutral (exactly 4). **The reusable law: a deliverable's projection is usable only AT-OR-AFTER its declaration; an upstream producer rebuilds the boundary fact from the constituents (the projection's own ingredients), losing nothing.** This sharpens [[ref-severed-constructor-boundary-projects-interior-doesnt]] (boundary facts are constituent-derivable, so a producer can always rebuild them rather than wait for the projection) and is the use-site dual of [[ref-constructor-field-forces-mutual-group-merge]]'s declaration-ordering safety argument (there: moving a declaration EARLIER never breaks ordering; here: a declaration cannot be USED before its site). New memory [[ref-downstream-projection-unavailable-rebuild-from-constituents]]; demo `Tests/Reflections/DownstreamProjectionRebuildFromConstituents.lean` (axiom-clean `[propext]`).

### Reflection 458 — a downstream projection unreachable at an upstream producer has TWO remedies (rebuild-from-constituents vs move-the-projection-up); the SELECTOR is the GRAIN at which the producer holds the deliverable — CONSTITUENTS IN HAND → rebuild, OPAQUE WHOLE → move; plus a recursive constructor that cannot represent the degenerate (empty) case forces an emptiness DISPATCH behind a builder function

Executing STEP D steps 2c+3 — wire both map arms of `emit_scans_in_flow_rec_entry_both` to build `RecSeqEntry.mapRec` — surfaced the **selection criterion** between R457's two remedies for an unreachable downstream projection. R457 (the assembler `emitPairList_scans_recmapbody`) REBUILT the body tail facts from constituents because it HELD them (the value block `block_v` decomposed in scope). The two map arms, by contrast, receive the body as a single opaque hypothesis `RecMapBody bodyBlock` returned from the assembler sub-call — they hold NO constituents, only the whole. **At an opaque-whole site you cannot rebuild without `cases`-ing the deliverable open and re-deriving the projection inline (which IS the projection); with TWO such sites, the dependency-correct fix is to MOVE the projection up.** So step 2c moved `RecMapBody.lastNonOpener`/`.lastNonSep` (+ the `RecSeqEntry.ne_nil`/`head_contentStart` helpers they read off the value entry) up to just after `RecMapBody.toWellBracketed` — safe by the earlier-declaration ordering check ([[ref-constructor-field-forces-mutual-group-merge]]) since they reference only constructors + upstream helpers — and step 3 reads the wrapped block's tail facts off `RecMapBody.lastNonOpener h_body_rec`/`.lastNonSep h_body_rec` directly. **The selector: rebuild where the constituents are decomposed-in-hand; move where the deliverable is bundled-opaque. The grain at which the producer holds the deliverable picks the remedy.** Second finding — the **DEGENERATE-CASE DISPATCH**: `RecSeqEntry.mapRec` carries `RecMapBody interior`, but `RecMapBody` has NO empty constructor (`single`/`cons` are both non-empty), so an empty map `{}` (`bodyBlock = []`) cannot inhabit `.mapRec` — it falls back to the flat `.map` (which needs only `WellBracketed []`). The producer dispatches on emptiness inside the nested existential and packages BOTH constructors behind ONE builder function `(∀ fms fme, h_open → h_close → RecSeqEntry (fms :: (bodyBlock ++ [fme])))`, so the outer wrap code applies it constructor-blind — the same `h_entry_builder` shape the seq arms already use for `.seqEmpty`/`.seq`. Both arms (value `:~3543`, saved-key `:~3807`) now build `.mapRec` for non-empty pairs via the recursive assembler (its `h_all_k`/`h_all_v` discharged from the renamed IHs `(ihk i).2`/`(ihv i).1`) and `.map` for empty `{}`. Build green (708 jobs), frontier exactly 4. Sharpens [[ref-downstream-projection-unavailable-rebuild-from-constituents]] by naming the move-vs-rebuild selector; relates to [[ref-additive-parallel-type-over-shared-edit]] (the recursive `.mapRec` is the additive constructor the degenerate case cannot inhabit). New memory [[ref-opaque-whole-moves-projection-constituents-rebuild]]; demo `Tests/Reflections/OpaqueWholeMovesProjectionConstituentsRebuild.lean` (axiom-clean `[propext]`).

(3) Both map arms of `emit_scans_in_flow_rec_entry_both` now build `RecSeqEntry.mapRec` (non-empty, carrying `RecMapBody interior` from `emitPairList_scans_recmapbody`) / `RecSeqEntry.map` (empty `{}`), via a nested-existential builder (`h_entry_builder`); body tail facts read off `RecMapBody.lastNonOpener`/`.lastNonSep`. `mapRec` is now INHABITED on the emit feed. ### Reflection 459 — a flat-severance constructor TOKEN-INDISTINGUISHABLE from its recursive sibling blocks `cases`-recovery of the recursion: any hypothesis strong enough to recover the body is EQUIVALENT to the conclusion, so the recursion must be THREADED from the producer (which holds it at build time), not RECOVERED by the descent — the seq/map descent asymmetry, resolved by bridging into the severance-FREE recursive type

The R458 Next step planned step 4 as "mirror `RecSeqEntry.seq_interior`" — a plain `cases`-projection `RecSeqEntry (.flowMappingStart-headed) → RecMapBody interior ∨ interior = []` — and front-loaded a PROBE of "THE OPEN BRANCH" (non-empty flat `.map`). **PROBING it ([[ref-probe-deferred-universal-before-producing]]) showed the planned projection CANNOT work the way `seq_interior` does, for a structural reason that re-scopes the descent.** `seq_interior` is debt-free because `RecSeqEntry` has **no flat seq severance** — every nested flow-SEQUENCE entry is `.seqEmpty` or `.seq` (which STORES its `RecSeqBody`), so `cases` digs the body straight out. The map side is asymmetric: alongside recursive `.mapRec` (stores `RecMapBody interior`) there is flat `.map` (stores only `WellBracketed interior`), built by the seq-navigator near-leaf `recseqentry_map_window` (`:~5764`, which severs by design). **Crucially `.map interior` and `.mapRec interior` are TOKEN-INDISTINGUISHABLE — same index `op :: (interior ++ [cl])`, same tokens — so no `cases` on a bare `RecSeqEntry` can tell them apart; and flat `.map` admits interiors that are `WellBracketed` but NOT a `RecMapBody`, so `RecMapBody interior` is a fact about `interior` the type genuinely does not determine.** Hence ANY hypothesis strong enough to conclude `RecMapBody interior ∨ interior = []` is EQUIVALENT to that conclusion (decidable emptiness collapses both directions) — there is no "weaker but sufficient" discriminator, the way `seq_interior`'s `.flowSequenceStart` head was strictly weaker than its conclusion. **So the recursion cannot be RECOVERED by the descent; it must be THREADED from the PRODUCER, which holds `h_rec` (non-empty) / emptiness (`{}`) at build time.** That body is the descent's DEBT ([[ref-root-seed-discriminator-not-from-gate]]) — but unlike a position discriminator, the debt here is the conclusion itself, which is precisely why a bare-`RecSeqEntry` consumer (the navigator, holding an opaque entry off `RecSeqBody`/`RecMapPair`) cannot supply it. **The clean resolution is to bridge into the SEVERANCE-FREE recursive type `RecMapEntry`** (whose own `RecMapEntry.map_interior` descent IS debt-free, exactly because `RecMapEntry` has only `mapEmpty`/`map`-with-`RecMapBody`, no flat constructor): R459 lands `RecSeqEntry.toRecMapEntry` (`:~3998`) — given the located map entry and the producer's body debt, it reads the closer off `h`, rules out the non-map heads by `h_op`, dispatches the emptiness disjunct to `RecMapEntry.mapEmpty`/`.map`, and the EXISTING `recmapbody_window_of_located_entry` (`:~7264`) descends from there. The bridge SUBSUMES the planned `mapRec_interior` (composing with `map_interior` recovers the disjunction) and plugs the producer's `.mapRec` output straight into the map navigator's existing descent. **The discipline: before planning a recursive DESCENT as a `cases`-projection, check the deliverable type for a flat severance TOKEN-INDISTINGUISHABLE from the recursive constructor; if one exists AND the flat constructor admits payloads the recursive one excludes, the descent cannot recover the recursion — thread it from the producer and bridge into the severance-free sibling type whose descent IS clean.** Sharpens [[ref-probe-deferred-universal-before-producing]] (the probed-open branch turns out unrecoverable, not merely vacuous) and [[ref-root-seed-discriminator-not-from-gate]] (here the discriminator equals the conclusion, so it is producer-threaded by necessity, not choice); relates to [[ref-additive-parallel-type-over-shared-edit]] (`RecMapEntry` is the severance-free parallel type the bridge targets) and [[ref-stored-vs-projected-severs-recursion-edge]] (the flat `.map` is the projected-not-stored edge). New memory [[ref-token-indistinguishable-severance-threads-recursion-from-producer]]; demo `Tests/Reflections/TokenIndistinguishableSeveranceThreadsRecursionFromProducer.lean` (axiom-clean `[propext]`).

**LANDED (R459 — STEP D step 4):** `RecSeqEntry.toRecMapEntry` (`NonemptyStructure.lean:~3998`, just after `RecMapEntry.toWellBracketed`): a map-headed `RecSeqEntry (op :: (interior ++ [cl]))` + the producer's body debt `h_body : RecMapBody interior ∨ interior = []` → `RecMapEntry e`. The `cases h` reads the closer `cl.val = .flowMappingEnd` off whichever map constructor built `e` and rules out `scalar`/`seqEmpty`/`seq` by `h_op`; `h_body`'s disjunct selects `RecMapEntry.mapEmpty` (empty `{}`) vs `.map` (non-empty, fed the producer's `h_rec`). It is the producer→navigator bridge that the PROBE showed the planned `cases`-projection `mapRec_interior` could not be (token-indistinguishable flat `.map`/`.mapRec` ⇒ recursion is producer-threaded, not descent-recovered) — composing with `RecMapEntry.map_interior` recovers the planned `RecMapBody interior ∨ interior = []`, and `recmapbody_window_of_located_entry` descends from the bridged `RecMapEntry`. ### Reflection 460 — bridging a token-indistinguishable severance to a severance-free sibling type cleans the LOCATED TOP entry only; the severance RE-SURFACES one level deeper, at every `RecMapPair`'s bare-`RecSeqEntry` value/key field — so the recursive map navigator STILL faces the undischargeable flat-`.map` `cases` at every map-value-that-is-itself-a-map, and the recursion is producer-threaded debt at EVERY level, not once

The R459 Next step planned STEP D step 5 as "wire the recursive map navigator so it descends the severance-free `RecMapEntry`/`RecMapBody` end-to-end, never casing a bare `RecSeqEntry` at a map boundary", and front-loaded a PROBE to "trace WHERE a map-value-that-is-itself-a-map is reached — confirm it arrives as a `RecMapBody`/`RecMapEntry` and NOT as a bare `RecSeqEntry`". **PROBING it ([[ref-probe-deferred-universal-before-producing]] / [[ref-minimal-pair-extracts-the-gate]]) shows the severance-freedom of `RecMapEntry`/`RecMapBody` is SHALLOW — it holds at the entry / body / pair-LIST spine, but its pairs reuse the bare severance-prone entry type for their sub-values, so the severance recurses.** `RecMapBody` is a list of `RecMapPair`s; `RecMapPair.mk` (`NonemptyStructure.lean:510`) stores the value `h_ve : RecSeqEntry block_v` (and the key `h_ke : RecSeqEntry block_k`) as a **bare `RecSeqEntry`** — exactly the type with the flat `.map` / recursive `.mapRec` token-indistinguishability R459 isolated. So tracing the `MapPathLocatorMoveProbe` M3 `[{a:{x:[b]}}]` DESCEND-VALUE-into-a-map step: it reaches the inner map as the bare `h_ve : RecSeqEntry block_v`, and recursing into its inner `RecMapBody` re-hits the undischargeable flat-`.map` `cases`. **So `toRecMapEntry` cleaning the LOCATED top entry does not eliminate the severance — it relocates it one level deeper, to every nested map value/key, where it bites again.** A navigator descending `RecMapBody` therefore CANNOT recurse into nested-map values from the deliverable alone: the per-value recursive body is the producer's debt at *every* level, and the deliverable does not carry it at its pair-value fields (they are bare `RecSeqEntry`). **The fix is NOT more bridging at the top: it is a PARALLEL deep-map family whose `RecMapPair` value/key FIELDS carry the recursion (a severance-free `RecMapEntry`-like entry, no flat constructor), built by the producer applying `toRecMapEntry` at EVERY map value/key — so the navigator only ever descends severance-free types and never `cases`es a bare value/key `RecSeqEntry`.** Per [[ref-additive-parallel-type-over-shared-edit]] this is a NEW additive parallel family, not a structural edit to the shared `RecMapPair` (whose bare-`RecSeqEntry` fields are load-bearing for the flat projections elsewhere). **The discipline: before planning a recursive navigator over a severance-free bridge target, PROBE whether the target is severance-free ALL THE WAY DOWN — the bridge target's severance-freedom is shallow (entry level only) iff its sub-structure reuses the bare entry type for sub-values; if shallow, the severance recurses and must be producer-threaded through a parallel deep family whose sub-value field carries it.** Sharpens [[ref-token-indistinguishable-severance-threads-recursion-from-producer]] (the bridge relocates the severance one level deeper, it does not remove it); relates to [[ref-additive-parallel-type-over-shared-edit]] (the parallel deep family) and [[ref-stored-vs-projected-severs-recursion-edge]] (the pair value/key field PROJECTS the entry, severing the recursion edge — the projected-not-stored edge re-appears at the sub-value). New memory [[ref-severance-recurses-through-pair-value]]; demo `Tests/Reflections/SeveranceRecursesThroughPairValue.lean` (axiom-clean `[propext]`).

The PROBE traced the `MapPathLocatorMoveProbe` M3 DESCEND-VALUE-into-a-map step to the bare `RecMapPair.mk` value field `h_ve : RecSeqEntry block_v` — confirming a bare-`RecSeqEntry` `cases` IS unavoidable at every nested-map value boundary, so the R459 bridge cleans only the located top entry and the severance recurses. ### Reflection 461 — the severance-free deep family that resolves a RECURSIVE token-indistinguishable severance must mirror the FULL MUTUAL GROUP of the recursion (both the seq AND the map axes), not just the one axis where the severance was first seen — because the navigator recursion is MUTUAL (a map value can be a seq, a seq entry can be a map, to any depth) — and its FIRST brick is the deep→flat PROJECTION (author it before the navigator)

The R460 Next step queued STEP D step 6 as a SHAPE PROBE: decide whether the deep-map family is **(a)** a NEW four-inductive mutual group, or **(b)** a thinner family reusing the map-only `RecMapEntry` for the pair value/key, then author the deep→flat projection FIRST and probe the producer can build it. **PROBING it ([[ref-probe-deferred-universal-before-producing]] / [[ref-recursive-deliverable-project-to-flat-first]]) settles all three sub-decisions and lands the projection core-Lean.** **(a) over (b):** a map pair's value can be a SCALAR (or a SEQ), not only a map, so the value field must be a *universal* severance-free entry — the map-only `RecMapEntry` (`mapEmpty`/`map` only) cannot type it; a `RecMapPair`-of-`RecMapEntry` (shape (b)) cannot represent a scalar- or seq-valued pair the emit feed produces freely. So the deep family needs its OWN universal entry type. **The decisive sharpening of the next-step's map-only framing — the recursion is MUTUAL.** `RecSeqBody.single`/`.cons` store their entries as **bare `RecSeqEntry`** exactly as `RecMapPair.mk` stores its value, so a seq-of-map (`RecSeqBody` whose head entry is a map — the M3 `[{a:{x:[b]}}]` ancestor path `[`→`{`→`{`→`[`) re-hits the flat-`.map` token-indistinguishability through the SEQ spine, not just the map one. So the deep family's SEQ bodies must be deep too: **ONE four-inductive mutual group covering BOTH axes** (`RecSeqBodyDeep`/`RecEntryDeep`/`RecMapPairDeep`/`RecMapBodyDeep`, names TBD), mirroring `RecSeqBody`/`RecSeqEntry`/`RecMapPair`/`RecMapBody` MINUS the flat `.map` constructor — NOT a map-only family bolted onto the flat `RecSeqBody` (which would leave the cross-axis seq-of-map nesting still severed). **The FIRST brick is the deep→flat PROJECTION** ([[ref-recursive-deliverable-project-to-flat-first]]): a mutual theorem block `*.toFlat` taking the deep `map` to flat `.mapRec` (RECURSION PRESERVED — flat consumers reading `mapRec`'s body still fire), the deep `mapEmpty` to flat `.map []` (the producer's degenerate-`{}` dispatch, R458 — the flat empty `.map` is reached only where the no-`nil` `RecMapBody` structurally cannot represent the empty body). ### Reflection 462 — AUTHORING the deep four-inductive mutual group in the main lib: the parallel-family port SHEDS the flat field ORTHOGONAL to the family's purpose (`WellBracketed`) and RE-MATERIALIZES it on projection — keeping the deep family a minimal recursion carrier and lightening the future producer's contract

The R461 SHAPE PROBE decided shape (a) (a four-inductive mutual group covering both axes) and landed the deep→flat projection core-Lean; STEP D step 7 AUTHORS it in the main lib (`NonemptyStructure.lean`, after `RecMapBody.toWellBracketed` `:2143`): the parallel group `RecSeqBodyDeep`/`RecEntryDeep`/`RecMapPairDeep`/`RecMapBodyDeep` (verbatim mirror of the merged group `:481-528` MINUS the flat `.map` severance), the mutual projection `*.toFlat`, and two consumer-firing corollaries. **The one design decision the toy front-loaded as "budget the extra `WellBracketed` field per constructor" — resolved by SHEDDING it.** The flat `RecSeqEntry.seq`/`.mapRec` store `h_wb : WellBracketed interior` because the flat family's SEVERED constructor (the flat `.map`, recursion-cut) has no recursive body to derive `WellBracketed` from, so it MUST store it, and the recursive `seq`/`mapRec` inherit the stored-field convention to mirror. The deep family REPLACES the severed constructor with a recursion-carrier (there is no deep flat `.map`; every map entry carries its `RecMapBodyDeep` or is `mapEmpty`), so `WellBracketed` is now REDUNDANT — re-derivable from the body the family carries, via the EXISTING `RecSeqBody.toWellBracketed`/`RecMapBody.toWellBracketed` applied to the *projected* body. So the deep `seq`/`mapRec` carry NO `WellBracketed` field, and the projection's `seq`/`mapRec` arms SUPPLY it as `RecSeqBody.toWellBracketed (RecSeqBodyDeep.toFlat h_rec)` / `RecMapBody.toWellBracketed (RecMapBodyDeep.toFlat h_rec)` (the `mapEmpty` leaf supplies `WellBracketed_nil`) — calling `*.toFlat` of the body twice (body + extractor), which compiles fine under structural recursion (the demo validates the double-call). **The payoff is twofold:** (1) the deep family stays a MINIMAL recursion carrier — it stores only what the recursion needs (the body + the non-derivable head/opener fields `h_ne`/`h_head`/`h_op`/`h_kt`, which are KEPT verbatim), not the orthogonal balance invariant; (2) the future producer is LIGHTER — it threads only the recursion, never `WellBracketed`, which materializes only at the flat-projection boundary. The two corollaries `RecSeqBodyDeep.toSafeBody`/`RecMapBodyDeep.toSafeBody` confirm the projected flat consumers (`RecSeqBody.toSafeBody` `:563`, `RecMapBody.toSafeBody` `:2106`) still fire on both axes. **The reusable discipline: when PORTING a verified-but-unconsumed parallel family to the main lib (the toy validated the shape), SHED any flat-type field that is ORTHOGONAL to the parallel family's purpose and re-derivable from the field the family DOES carry — re-materialize it on projection via the existing flat extractor applied to the projected body; the field to shed is exactly the one the flat severed constructor needed BECAUSE it lacked a recursive body, and the recursion-carrier makes redundant.** Sharpens [[ref-deep-family-mirrors-full-mutual-group]] (which fixed the family SHAPE) with the field-level porting refinement, via [[ref-recursive-deliverable-project-to-flat-first]] (the projection re-materializes the shed field — its first job) and [[ref-additive-parallel-type-over-shared-edit]] (a minimal additive carrier; the flat type's stored field is untouched). ### Reflection 464 — a flat→strengthened producer MIRROR is a pure TEXT-SWAP iff the flat proof reads each per-item fact from the predicate's STANDALONE CONJUNCT, not from a PROJECTION off the per-item inductive; the minimal/severance-free strengthened family SHEDS those projections, so each `hentry.toX` read forces a REROUTE to the standalone conjunct — and the mirror's cost is QUANTIFIED before writing it as (text swaps) + (one reroute per projection read)

STEP D step 8's deep producer is built bottom-up by mirroring the flat body producers ([[ref-recursive-producer-mirrors-flat-over-shared-induction]]). R463 landed the deep per-entry PREDICATES + coercions; this brick lands the FIRST body producer, the deep SEQ-body assembler — and surfaces the rule for *when a mirror is truly verbatim*. The deep four-inductive family is MINIMAL ([[ref-deep-family-mirrors-full-mutual-group]]): it SHEDS the orthogonal `WellBracketed`/`EntrySafe`/`EntryUnit` projections ([[ref-parallel-family-sheds-orthogonal-field]]), so `RecEntryDeep` carries ONLY `.toFlat` — there is no `RecEntryDeep.toEntryUnit`. Whether the flat proof's mirror is a pure text-swap therefore turns on HOW it read each per-item fact: **(a) from the per-item predicate's STANDALONE conjunct** (the predicate carries `… ∧ EntryUnit block ∧ RecSeqEntry block ∧ …`; the proof binds the `EntryUnit` conjunct as a named hyp and uses it) ⇒ the deep predicate carries that SAME standalone conjunct verbatim, so the mirror is a pure swap (`EmitScansInFlowRecEntry`→`…Deep`, `RecSeqBody`→`RecSeqBodyDeep`, leaf constructors), ZERO reroutes; **(b) via a PROJECTION off the entry** (`hentry.toEntryUnit`, where `hentry : RecSeqEntry block`) ⇒ the deep mirror gives `hentry : RecEntryDeep block`, and `RecEntryDeep.toEntryUnit` DOES NOT EXIST — so each such read must be REROUTED to the predicate's standalone conjunct (which the predicate keeps precisely because the deep family cannot reproject it). **The payoff is a cost that is QUANTIFIED before the mirror is written:** count the `.toX`-projection reads in the flat proof; the mirror is (the global text swaps) + (one reroute per projection read), no new helper. The seq-body assembler `emitList_scans_recseqbody` (`:1673`) reads `EntryUnit`/`ContentStartTok` from the STANDALONE conjuncts `h_eu₁`/`h_cs₁` (it binds them positionally and never projects off the entry) ⇒ case (a), a clean two-swap mirror; the map-body assembler `emitPairList_scans_recmapbody` (`:~2829`) reads `h_ve.toEntryUnit` twice (value side; the key side reads no projections) ⇒ case (b), predicted cost 4 swaps + exactly 2 reroutes to the value predicate's standalone `EntryUnit` conjunct (`_h_eu_v`, today bound-but-unused). **The reusable discipline: before mirroring a flat producer to a strengthened (minimal) parallel family, grep the flat proof for `.toX` projection reads off the per-item inductive — each is a reroute to the predicate's standalone `X` conjunct, the only non-verbatim site; a proof that reads all per-item facts from standalone conjuncts mirrors by pure text-swap.** Sharpens [[ref-recursive-producer-mirrors-flat-over-shared-induction]] (the *when-is-it-verbatim* predictor) via [[ref-parallel-family-sheds-orthogonal-field]] (the shed projections are exactly the non-verbatim sites) and [[ref-stored-vs-projected-severs-recursion-edge]] (stored-vs-projected decides the proof's READ shape, here, not only the recursion edge). New memory [[ref-mirror-reads-conjunct-not-projection]]; demo `Tests/Reflections/MirrorReadsConjunctNotProjection.lean` (`#check_failure` witnessing the absent `DEntry.toExtra`).

### Reflection 465 — the pre-write mirror-cost count (Reflection 464) held OFF-BY-ZERO on the harder MAP-body brick; and a corollary on composite items: in a key++value pair the projection reads (hence the reroutes) concentrate on the END-most sub-block, because the consumer projects only BOUNDARY facts

R464 turned "is this big mirror clean or messy?" into a pre-write COUNT: grep the flat proof for `.toX` projection reads off the per-item inductive; the mirror is (global text swaps) + (one reroute per projection read). The seq-body brick (0 reroutes) was the easy confirmation. This brick TESTED the count against the harder map-body assembler — predicted 4 swaps + exactly 2 reroutes — and it held with ZERO surprises: the four swaps and the two `h_ve.toEntryUnit`→`_h_eu_v` reroutes were the entire delta, the proof type-checked first try, axioms identical to the flat producer. **The count is reliable enough to commit to before writing** — the mirror was generated mechanically (Python text-swap of the 532-line flat source + the 2 reroutes) rather than hand-transcribed, eliminating transcription error in a large proof. **The corollary** sharpens [[ref-mirror-reads-conjunct-not-projection]] for COMPOSITE per-item structures: a map item is a `key ++ value` pair carrying a standalone `EntryUnit` conjunct for EACH side, yet only the VALUE side rerouted. The reason is structural, not incidental: the consumer (the map-wrap's OpenerAdj/SepAdj seam) projects only BOUNDARY facts (last-token-not-opener/-not-sep), and a pair's boundary IS its value tail — so every projection read lands on the END-most sub-block, leaving the key side (interior, never the boundary) a pure conjunct read. So when predicting a composite mirror's cost, grep the END-most sub-structure first; the interior sub-blocks contribute swaps but not reroutes. This also previews the NEXT brick's harder shape: the recursion-CLOSING per-entry producer is NOT a pure swap, because the deep leaf constructors change ARITY ([[ref-mirror-constructor-arity-reads-storage]] — dropping the shed `WellBracketed`, restoring the flat-severed map recursion) and its 4 `RecMapBody.lastNon*` reads need coerce-to-weaker reroutes ([[ref-coerce-to-weaker-reuse-wrapper]]). ### Reflection 489 — a RESTRICTION producer cannot upgrade the guard: re-threading a window-parametric chain onto the boundary-true WEAKER twin stays in the weak family END-TO-END, even at descended windows where the strong guard genuinely holds. **The de-risk for step γ′, and its foundational `_seq` child-bracket primitive `flowBodyContentDeepSeq_child_bracket` landed.**

**The trap — and why a `_seq` twin, not a coercion back to the strong guard.** The enclosing child `[p, hiE)` IS a nested `[ … ]` window where the strong `FlowBodyContentDeep` genuinely HOLDS — so the tempting shortcut is "produce the strong child and feed the EXISTING strong recursion." This is FALSE in a restriction setting. The child producers work by RESTRICTION — narrowing the parent's universally-quantified guard fields to a sub-window domain — which is MONOTONE in the guard: it can only carry forward the fields the parent ACTUALLY HOLDS. The weaker `FlowBodyContentDeepSeq` parent does not carry the strong guard's `{`-opener / empty-`[]`-opener facts (its `openerContentStart` is gated to non-empty `.flowSequenceStart`), so the strong child is UNREACHABLE from a weak parent — its truth at the child comes from GLOBAL emitter structure the local restriction cannot see. The membrane is one-way: `FlowBodyContentDeep ⇒ FlowBodyContentDeepSeq` coerces (drop to the gated subset), but `FlowBodyContentDeepSeq ⇒ FlowBodyContentDeep` does not. So the re-thread must stay in the WEAK twin family end-to-end (weak parent → weak child → weak-keyed IH, exactly `seqWindowRecSeqBody_seq`'s `FlowBodyContentDeepSeq` recursion conjunct), and each child producer needs a `_seq` twin.

**The transferable rule.** When you re-thread a window-parametric producer chain onto a boundary-true WEAKER guard `P'` (to seed a recursion where the strong interior guard `P` is false), every RESTRICTION-shaped child producer must output `P'` children, not `P` — even at descended windows where `P` holds — because restriction is monotone in the guard and only propagates what the `P'` parent carries. The strong child's truth is irrelevant; what matters is derivability from the parent you hold. Build a `_seq` twin of each child producer; do not reach for a `P' ⇒ P` upgrade (it does not exist as a restriction). The `_seq` twin is usually STRICTLY SIMPLER at the head field: given the typed `.flowSequenceStart` opener directly (the gate already disambiguated `[` vs `{`), it sheds the strong sibling's `flowBracketDelta_eq_one_iff` `[`-vs-`{` split.

### Reflection 490 — a guard RE-SCOPE that demotes a guard-PROJECTED field to a UNIFIED residual can SIMPLIFY the downstream consumer, not complicate it: routing the unified residual through ONE invariant the consumer already holds SHEDS the strong twin's boundary-specific hypothesis. **Step γ′'s content child-bracket twin `flowBodyContent_child_bracket_seq` landed — the floor's reach over the close position drops `h_jclose` from the signature.**

The re-scoped guard's `feContentStart` is GATED by `tokens[k'+1] ≠ .key`, so the consumer cannot project the interior either — and `flowBodyContent_of_deepSeq` therefore UNIFIES both into a SINGLE `feContent` residual (interior AND boundary, `k' < hi`, carrying the `balance = 0` premise). This LOOKS like an added burden (an extra, unprojectable residual). But at THIS consumer — the child bracket `[k, j+1)` — the unified residual routes through ONE invariant the consumer ALREADY holds: the child-bracket FLOOR `h_floor1 : ∀ i, k+1 ≤ i → i ≤ j → flowBracketBalance tokens k i ≥ 1`, whose range REACHES the close position `j` (the pre-close index). The close hypothesis `h_jclose` is REDUNDANT here and DROPPED from the twin's signature.

**The transferable rule.** When a guard re-scope demotes a guard-PROJECTED field to a UNIFIED named residual (merging cases the strong form split), don't assume the consumer got harder. Inventory the invariants the consumer already holds; check whether ONE of them is strong enough to discharge the WHOLE unified residual — its reach must cover the boundary the strong split handled separately. If so, route the unified residual through that one invariant and DROP the boundary-specific hypothesis the strong twin consumed (the close / end marker). The re-scope SIMPLIFIES rather than complicates: routing through one invariant DECOUPLES the discharge from the per-case hypotheses (guard projection AND boundary marker) the split required. The tell that the floor reaches the boundary: the strong twin's interior projection was gated `< boundary` while the floor is `≤ boundary` (it covers the pre-close index `j` itself) — that one position of extra reach subsumes the boundary case.
