R519 predicted this would be FREE on the consumer side, and it was: `mapLocator_of_window_recmapbody` already binds `h_floor` (its `MapLocated`-output guard), so the six call sites just append it; the only other consumer, `mapLocated_of_recmapbody_outer`, takes the inner `∀ k` bodies (not the guarded wrappers) so its signature is untouched. The producer-slot texts are byte-identical across the three lemmas, so the strengthening was a single `replace_all` per slot.

**Step (2) — the projection re-key, and why the route choice is forced.** The collapse `mapProducers_of_mapRoot` needs, at each window `[lo, hi)`, the six `MapGrammarFacts tokens lo hi`. There are two carrier→facts routes: R515's `mapGrammarFacts_of_mapRoot` (keyed on the OPENER position `q`, gate reconstructed from `enclosingMark_false_of_opener`) and R518's `mapWindow_grammarFacts` (keyed on a `FlowBodyWindow tokens lo hi`). **The slot guard is the non-strict `lo ≤ hi`** — because the empty nested `{}` window `lo = hi` is a real window the producer must answer (vacuously). `FlowBodyWindow` carries `lo < hi` (strict), so the R518 route literally cannot fire there; the R515 route needs only `q + 1 ≤ hi`, never `lo < hi`, so it survives `lo = hi`. **The consumer's degenerate case forces the route.** The bridge is a single new lemma `mapGrammarFacts_window_of_root` that re-keys R515 from `q` to the window-start `lo` (set `q := lo - 1`, so `q + 1 = lo` by `Nat.sub_add_cancel` since `2 ≤ lo`), pulls the pre-opener prefix witness from `h_fold_total`, threads the producer's own opener/balance/floor, and DISCARDS the `.flowMappingEnd` closer (the marker-free carrier identifies the interior by enclosure, not the closer). The only new arithmetic over R515 is the one `Nat.sub_add_cancel` rewrite, carried through the balance argument, the floor argument, and the conclusion.

**The transferable rule.** When a per-window deliverable admits two equivalent projection routes that differ only in the window bound they demand (`lo < hi` vs `lo ≤ hi`), and the CONSUMER's slot guard is non-strict — admitting the degenerate window `lo = hi` it is obligated to answer — you MUST pick the route whose bound the consumer's guard supplies. The strict route cannot fire on the degenerate window the consumer carries; choose the projection route by the bound the consumer's guard forces, not by which lemma reads cleaner. This is the route-selection dual of [[ref-easy-edge-guard-fails-hard-edge]] (a guard sized to its easy edge cannot do its hard edge) and an instance of [[ref-derisk-consumer-blindspot-vs-contract]] (name the degenerate case the abstraction can't represent, before building).

### Reflection 521 — brick (2)'s pivot, `FlowBodyContentDeepMap`: the delegation asymmetry in the deliverable propagates to the guard, which sheds fields. **The map body content-navigation guard the map width-recursion `mapWindowRecMapBody_map_general` (the R415 analog) threads landed — and it is STRICTLY SIMPLER than its seq twin `FlowBodyContentDeepSeq`: two fields not three, one edge not two, because a map body DELEGATES nesting where a seq body INLINES it.**

**The hard design decision, resolved by reading the inductive.** Brick (2) was flagged as pivoting on a "hard design decision": the map body's separator-successor is a `.key` MARKER, not content, so the seq `FlowBodyContent`/`FlowBodyContentDeep` machinery (built around "separator → content") does not transfer. The resolution is to read the DELEGATION off the recursive deliverable. `RecSeqEntry` INLINES the seq item shapes (`scalar`/`seq`/`mapRec` constructors), so the seq recursion DESCENDS into every nested `[ … ]` itself; its guard `FlowBodyContentDeepSeq` therefore carries THREE fields (`headContentStart`, `openerContentStart`, `feContentStart`) and supports BOTH a descend and an advance edge — `openerContentStart` is exactly the fact the descend edge reads to seat a nested child's head. `RecMapBody → RecMapPair → RecSeqEntry` DELEGATES: the key/value blocks are `RecSeqEntry`s navigated by the seq-entry oracles (`recmapentry_pair_located`), and the map body itself only ADVANCES past depth-`0` `.flowEntry` separators by BALANCE — it never descends. So `FlowBodyContentDeepMap` SHEDS the opener field and the descend edge: TWO fields (`headKey`, `feKey`), ONE edge (`flowBodyContentDeepMap_advance`). The delegation asymmetry in the inductive (one navigator inlines, the other delegates) propagates verbatim to the threading guard.

**The dual-axis separator gate.** `FlowBodyContentDeepSeq.feContentStart` reads `tokens[k] = .flowEntry → tokens[k+1] ≠ .key → isFlowContentStart tokens[k+1]` — a seq `,` is followed by content, and the `≠ .key` premise EXCLUDES map-internal `,`s (which are followed by a key). `FlowBodyContentDeepMap.feKey` is the exact dual: `tokens[k] = .flowEntry → ¬ isFlowContentStart tokens[k+1] → tokens[k+1] = .key` — a map `,` is followed by a key, and the `¬ content` premise EXCLUDES seq-internal `,`s (which are followed by content). The discriminator is the OTHER axis's separator-successor in each case — `.key` for seq, content-start for map — so the two fields are exact mirrors modulo that swap. The gate value is read off `MapBodyProps.after_fe` (the balance-gated map grammar fact) the driver supplies at the advance, so the advance edge takes the child head `tokens[m+1] = .key` directly and the parent's `feKey` only restricts — strictly simpler than the seq advance, which must READ its child head from the parent's `feContentStart`.

**The transferable rule.** A deliverable whose recursion DELEGATES nesting to a sibling navigator needs a strictly simpler threading guard than one that INLINES nesting — fewer fields, fewer restriction edges. Read the delegation off the inductive (which constructors store a recursive sub-deliverable vs. which delegate to a sibling), and SHED the guard fields the delegated machinery owns. The corollary for dual-axis separators: mirror by swapping the discriminator to the OTHER axis's separator-successor; the structural fields are otherwise verbatim.

**The finding — threading form vs assemble form.** A per-window separator-successor fact has TWO shapes that do NOT interconvert:
- the **THREADING form** is *conditional* — `FlowBodyContentDeepMap.feKey`: a depth-`0` `,` whose successor is NOT content ⟹ the successor is a `.key`. This is the shape the recursion's *advance* edge re-establishes step-by-step; its `¬ content` premise is exactly what lets the advance fire without proving the content-exclusion, because the driver supplies the next head directly.

The threading form does NOT imply the assemble form: deriving the unconditional from the conditional would require proving the `¬ content` premise FOR FREE — the very content-exclusion the threading form assumed as a hypothesis. (The demo witnesses this with a `seqLike` stream where the threading form holds vacuously yet the assemble form is false.)

**Why this forces the seq/map carrier asymmetry.** The SEQ carrier `SeqInteriorSeparators` bundles TWO facts — `bodySuccFact` AND `noTrailingSepFact` — so the seq bridge `seqWindow_flowBodyContent_seq_general` self-sources its comma-successor fact (`feContent`: every depth-`0` `,` is followed by content) by instantiating `noTrailingSepFact` on the narrowed window `[lo, k+1)`. The MAP carrier `MapInteriorSeparators` bundles ONLY the six `MapGrammarFacts` — it has NO comma-successor fact — so the map's dual (`after_fe`: every depth-`0` `,` is followed by a `.key`) cannot be re-sourced from the carrier and is taken as a SUPPLIED hypothesis. This is the precise location of the asymmetry the R513 map-carrier block recorded ("the six map-grammar facts ride into the consumer as raw per-window producers"): M1 `headKey` comes from the deep guard on BOTH axes; only the comma-successor splits — internalized by the seq carrier, deferred by the map. The transferable rule: when porting a parallel bridge, audit which per-window facts the OTHER axis's carrier internalizes vs. defers; a fact's threading form (guarded, for the recursion) and its assemble form (unconditional, for the assembler) are distinct shapes and the carrier may carry one, the other, or neither.

### Reflection 523 — brick (2)'s skeleton locator, `mapPairSkeleton_locate`: a balance-invisible split point is GRAMMAR-located, and the "it precedes the boundary" proof BIFURCATES by head shape. **The map pair-boundary skeleton — the `∃ kv e, …` that `recmapentry_pair_located` (R282/R284) had to take SUPPLIED — is now PRODUCED from the per-window `MapBodyProps` R522 delivers, via `firstEntryBoundary` for the pair end `e` and the M4/M5 grammar dispatch for the value separator `kv`; the crux `kv < e` costs zero balance reasoning for a flat (scalar) key and one positivity step for a nested (bracket) key.**

**The two findings.**
- **Balance-invisibility blocks a balance LOCATOR, not the location.** A pair `.key K .value V` returns balance to `0` at the depth-`0` `.value` separator AND at every nested-entry end inside `K` and `V`, so the `.value` is *balance-invisible* (R282) — there is no balance-pure `kv` locator. But `kv` is read off the typed grammar instead: M1's `.key` head, M3's content-start at `lo+1`, dispatched by shape into M4 (scalar key ⟹ `kv = lo+2`) or M5 (bracket key ⟹ `kv = j+1`, the matching close). The pair end `e` is the SHARED half — the least depth-`0` marker via the axis-agnostic `firstEntryBoundary` — carrying `balance lo e = 0`, the marker disjunct, and the minimality clause verbatim. So the balance-invisibility that BLOCKS a balance locator does not block the location; it *routes* it through the grammar.
- **The crux `kv < e` (the value separator precedes the first boundary) has a proof cost that BIFURCATES by the key's head shape.** Both branches rule out a marker in `(lo, kv]`. For a FLAT (scalar) key the two interior positions (`lo+1` the scalar, `kv` the `.value`) are ruled out as markers by *token identity alone* — neither is a `.flowEntry`, neither is `hi` — with NO balance reasoning. For a NESTED (bracket) key the bracket interior `[lo+2, j]` is genuinely depth-positive, so it is ruled out by the M5 positivity invariant lifted through `lo` (`balance lo k = 1 + balance (lo+2) k ≥ 1 ≠ 0`) — one balance step the flat case never pays; the two endpoints (`lo+1` the opener, `kv = j+1` the value) again fall to token identity. This is exactly the no-interior-boundary fact `recmapentry_classify` flagged as un-derivable from a single balance invariant and took as supplied: now DERIVED, with the head's interior depth profile setting the proof cost (zero for a flat scalar key, one positivity lift for a bracketed key).

### Reflection 525 — brick (2)'s last skeleton input, bundled: the head dispatch that LOCATES the value separator also PINS its depth, for free. **The fact R524 had to isolate as `h_kv_depth : balance lo kv = 0` is discharged AT ITS SOURCE — `mapPairSkeleton_locate` now emits it in its output existential, free in each dispatch branch because the same case-split that PLACES `kv` walks over tokens whose bracket-deltas telescope to the depth.**

**The setup.** R524's `mapPairSubblocks_flowBodyWindow` consumed every input from the R523 skeleton EXCEPT one — `h_kv_depth : flowBracketBalance tokens lo kv = 0`, the value separator's depth-`0`-ness. R524 established this fact is *genuinely* outside `MapBodyProps`: the successor fields M6/M7/M8 take depth-`0`-ness of the value position as a GUARD precondition, not an assertion, so it cannot be bootstrapped from the grammar bundle. R524 left it "to the head dispatch." This reflection closes that: the head dispatch is exactly `mapPairSkeleton_locate`, and it already had the fact in hand.

**The finding — a located witness's depth is a FREE byproduct of the locator's own head dispatch.** A balance-invisible split point (R523) is located by case-splitting on the key's head shape; the very same dispatch determines the located position's depth, because the depth is just the telescoped sum of the bracket-deltas of the tokens the dispatch walked over from `lo`:
- **scalar key** `kv = lo+2`: the dispatch stepped over a `.key` (`flowBracketDelta = 0`) and a scalar (`= 0`), so `balance lo (lo+2) = balance lo lo + 0 + 0 = 0` — one composition.
- **bracket key** `kv = j+1` for the matching close `j`: the dispatch stepped over a `.key` (`0`), an opener (`+1`), the bracket interior (balanced, by the locator's OWN `h_inner_bal : balance (lo+2) j = 0`), and the matching close (`-1`), so `balance lo (j+1) = 0 + 1 + 0 + (-1) = 0`. ### Reflection 526 — brick (2)'s per-window ADVANCE step, `recmapbody_map_descend_tail`: a descend-tail's two obligations both discharge from ONE per-window separator-successor fact, and the seq/map twins differ only in provider and polarity. **The map driver's guard-descent past a depth-`0` pair-end separator landed as the map twin of `recseqbody_seq_descend_tail` (R511) — and reading the two edges side by side names the reusable shape: the suffix non-degeneracy and the deep-guard advance are a single dual-use of the located separator's successor token, supplied by `MapBodyProps.after_fe` on the map side where the seq side reads `FlowBodyContent.feContentStart`.**

### Reflection 540 — PROBING before producing reveals the map separator carrier `MapInteriorSeparators` is UNPROVABLE as defined: its `MapGrammarFacts` is BOUNDARY-FRAGILE where the seq carrier's facts are BOUNDARY-ROBUST. **A separator fact threaded through a SUBSET-RESTRICTION carrier (`∀ sub-window [a,b) ⊆ [lo,hi)`, gate `→` fact) must be BOUNDARY-ROBUST: its conclusion may CONSTRAIN the boundary token but must not REQUIRE a successor to lie STRICTLY INSIDE the window. The seq carrier `SeqInteriorSeparators` is CONSTRUCTIBLE (`seqRoot_seqInteriorSeparators`) because `bodySuccFact` (`k+1 = b ∨ ∃ following entry`) and `noTrailingSepFact` (asserts `isFlowContentStart tokens[k+1]`, a fact about the boundary token, not a strict-interior demand) both survive the window that ends one past a separator. The map carrier `MapInteriorSeparators` COPIED THE SHAPE but its `MapGrammarFacts` is fragile — conjuncts 1/2/3/5 conclude `k+1 < b ∧ …` / `k+2 < b ∧ …`, demanding the `.key`/`.value` marker's content sit STRICTLY inside. Because `flowBracketDelta .key = flowBracketDelta .value = 0`, a gated window can END right after a marker at balance 0, and there `k+1 < b` is `b < b` — FALSE. The carrier was only ever ASSUMED (`h_carrier`), never constructed, so the falsity never surfaced ([[ref-probe-deferred-universal-before-producing]]: a target you only PROJECT hides its own falsity). The whole map ASSEMBLE half (R538/R539's locate+close, building toward `mapRoot_mapInteriorSeparators`) was aimed at an unprovable target — caught BEFORE writing the provider.**

**The witness — verified against the real defs.** On the stream `{a: 1}` = `#[ {, .key, scalar a, .value, scalar 1, } ]` (positions 0..5) the mid-key-cut window `[1,2)` covering only the `.key` marker satisfies `MapTypedInterior toks 1 2` (balance 0; `btFold`-top after the prefix `[0,1)` = `{` is `some false`; floor ≥ 0) yet refutes `MapGrammarFacts toks 1 2`: conjunct 1 at `k=1` forces `1+1 < 2`. Since `[1,2) ⊆ [1,5)` and `[1,5)` is the genuine outer map body, `MapInteriorSeparators toks 1 5` is FALSE. Three `example`s — `MapTypedInterior toks 1 2`, `¬ MapGrammarFacts toks 1 2`, `¬ MapInteriorSeparators toks 1 5` — compiled clean against the imported defs (the scratch was a verification probe, not committed; its content is reproduced abstractly in the runnable companion).

**Why seq escaped and map did not.** The seq separator facts reference the boundary token *without requiring it strictly inside* (`noTrailingSepFact` is happy for `tokens[k+1]` to be the close at `b`), or offer a `k+1 = b` close disjunct (`bodySuccFact`). This is the converse-of-the-seq-asymmetry the seq carrier never had to confront ([[ref-converse-forward-invariant-asymmetry]]).

**Cost / artifact.** The runnable companion `Tests/Reflections/BoundaryRobustVsFragileFact.lean` isolates the principle abstractly with core-only tactics: `FragileFact` (`trig k → k+1 < b ∧ P (k+1)`) vs `RobustFact` (`trig k → k+1 = b ∨ P (k+1)`); the fragile fact is refuted at the cut window `[1,2)` while the robust one survives; `robustFact_rebase` (the abstract `bodySuccFact_rebase`, axioms `[propext, Quot.sound]`) is provable while the fragile-rebase is concretely refuted. Frontier sorry count holds at 4 — this turn lands a verified REDIRECT, not a forward brick: it prevents the wasted construction of `mapDescent_provider_of_located` / `mapEnclosingFacts_provider_of_located` against an unprovable carrier.

### Reflection 538 — the map root-carrier `desc` provider's LOCATE half, the `some false`/`{` dual of the seq locate: `flowBracketBalance_pos_of_mapTypedInterior` + `mapEnclosingOpener_of_gate` + `mapOpenerType_of_located_and_gate`. **An AXIS DUAL of a lemma chain over a single tag bit (seq `[` ↦ `true`, map `{` ↦ `false`) is near-FREE to build precisely when the chain's primitives do not branch on the bit. Two ways a primitive earns this: TYPE-AGNOSTIC — it reads only bit-blind facts (the backward balance scan locates the enclosing opener from balance alone, never inspecting which bracket), so the dual reuses it VERBATIM; or GENERIC in the bit — it takes the bit as a PARAMETER (the head-positivity lemma takes `hd : Bool`), so the dual instantiates the OTHER bit, a one-symbol swap with zero proof difference. The ONLY proof content of the whole dual lives at the ONE site where the bit is CONSUMED to pick a constructor — the opener-type dispatch — and there a decidable two-constructor split (`delta = 1`: the opener is `[` OR `{`) is resolved by the gate's head bit: one case discharges the typed conclusion, the OTHER is killed ABSURD. The MAP root carrier had only the two `def`s `MapTypedInterior` / `MapInteriorSeparators` and the R513–R520 foundation (gate reconstruction, carrier→facts, six-producer collapse) — **no descent machinery at all**. So the map `desc` provider is the second of the two root-carrier descent providers the frontier-status names as the genuine open math, and this reflection lands its first concrete brick: the LOCATE half.

### Reflection 535 — brick (2)'s locate piece (iii), the SEQ half of the cross-deliverable knot: `recbody_joint_oracle_seq_ih`, the joint-oracle → seq-only-IH adapter. **A width-recursion driver over a JOINT guard hands its per-window step an oracle that delivers BOTH deliverables at every narrower sub-window, keyed on the close marker — `(seqEnd → RecSeqBody) ∧ (mapEnd → RecMapBody)`. But the concrete first-entry dispatch you want to run consumes a SINGLE-AXIS induction hypothesis (a bare `RecSeqBody` from loose window facts plus a choosable enclosure predicate). Don't widen the oracle: write an ADAPTER that RECONSTRUCTS the joint guard for the sub-window from the dispatch's loose facts and PROJECTS the one side; the OFF-axis guard conditional is VACUOUS by marker exclusivity. Drawing the IH from the joint oracle instead of an axis-only carrier LIFTS the carrier's all-one-path domain restriction — the oracle is path-agnostic.**

**The setup.** `recbody_joint_navigator_driver_carrier` (R534) is now a closed function of just the two `locate`s (and the per-window M2). The seq first-entry dispatch `recseqentry_window_dispatch_seq` (R527) — the workhorse of `locate_seq` — and the map locate's single-entry sub-block producer `recseqentry_whole_window_seq` both consume an induction hypothesis `h_ih : ∀ lo' hi', hi'-lo' < hi-lo → lo ≤ lo' → hi' ≤ hi → FlowBodyWindow … → FlowBodyContentDeepSeq … → Q lo' → tokens[hi']!.val = .flowSequenceEnd → RecSeqBody …`, where `Q` is a predicate the dispatch lets the caller CHOOSE. But the driver's per-window step holds a JOINT `oracle : ∀ lo' hi', hi'-lo' < hi-lo → RecBodyJointGuard tokens lo0 hi0 lo' hi' → (seqEnd → RecSeqBody …) ∧ (mapEnd → RecMapBody …)`. The shapes don't unify: the oracle wants a folded joint guard and returns a marker-keyed pair; the dispatch wants loose facts and a bare body.

**The finding — adapt by guard reconstruction + one-side projection, the off-axis conditional vacuous.** The bridge is not to teach either side about the other. Choose the dispatch's `Q := SeqEnclosed tokens`, so its `h_ih` hands over `SeqEnclosed tokens lo'` — exactly the enclosure conjunct the joint guard's seq side needs. Then the adapter FOLDS the loose pieces back into `RecBodyJointGuard tokens lo0 hi0 lo' hi'`: the two outer bounds compose by `omega` (`lo0 ≤ lo ≤ lo'`, `hi' ≤ hi ≤ hi0` — the adapter takes the outer `lo0 ≤ lo`/`hi ≤ hi0`, the IH supplies `lo ≤ lo'`/`hi' ≤ hi`); the `FlowBodyWindow` is verbatim; the seq conditional is `fun _ => ⟨h_deep, h_encl⟩` because we are in the seq-close case; the disjunct is `Or.inl` the seq close; and the MAP conditional is VACUOUS — its premise `tokens[hi']!.val = .flowMappingEnd` contradicts the seq close, so marker exclusivity (`rw [h_seqEnd] at h_mapEnd; exact absurd h_mapEnd (by decide)`) discharges it with NO map fact in scope. Folding done, `(oracle lo' hi' h_span <folded guard>).1 h_seqEnd` is the `RecSeqBody` the IH owes.

**Why this is the SEQ half of the cross-deliverable knot.** A carrier-only seq producer, `seqWindowRecSeqBody_seq_general`, already delivers a window's `RecSeqBody` IH — but ONLY on the **all-seq PATH** domain (`SeqPathAllSeq`, every enclosing frame a `[`), because it sources nested deliverables from the seq carrier alone and a carrier cannot speak for a `{`-enclosed frame. Drawing the IH from the JOINT oracle instead lifts that restriction: the oracle delivers `RecSeqBody`/`RecMapBody` at EVERY narrower window regardless of enclosing-bracket type, so the dispatch threaded through this adapter is path-agnostic. The map deliverable the oracle also carries is not consumed by this adapter — it flows on to the dispatch's `{`-bracket branch (the nested-map entry), the symmetric map half still to be wired.

**What landed.** `theorem recbody_joint_oracle_seq_ih` (`SeqInteriorSeparators.lean`, immediately after `recbody_joint_navigator_driver_carrier`): takes the outer frame bounds and the joint `oracle`, produces the dispatch's exact seq-only `h_ih` shape with `Q := SeqEnclosed tokens` inlined. Pure guard folding over `RecBodyJointGuard` plus the oracle — no structure lemma, no `Classical.choice` — so it audits to the MINIMAL `[propext, Quot.sound]`, `sorryAx`-free (cleaner than R534's profile, which inherited `Classical.choice` from the assemblers). ONE adapter serves BOTH locates, since the seq locate's dispatch and the map locate's sub-block producer want the identical seq IH shape.

### Reflection 486 — a refinement surfaced as an explicit consume-side residual is FREE at the wiring site: when `seqEnclosingLocate_of_seqOpener_nested` is wired into R475, the surfaced `h_open : tokens[p]!.val = .flowSequenceStart` costs the caller NOTHING — the SAME gate that delivers `SeqTypedInterior` carries the enclosing-type MARK that reconstructs the `[`. **The POSITIVE closure of R481: "not derivable from the producer's NAMED premise" ≠ "owed by the caller."**

**Context.** R481 (`GenericDiscriminantUnderdeterminesOutput`) proved that the (α) assemble's `tokens[p]!.val = .flowSequenceStart` is PROVABLY NOT derivable from R475's slot premise `flowBracketDelta tokens[p]!.val = 1` — a `{` satisfies `delta = 1` yet has a map child — so it SURFACED the refinement as the assemble's explicit hypothesis `h_open`. R485 then shed the OTHER surfaced hypothesis (`h_p_depth`, the depth-`0` discriminator) by making the assemble depth-general. The only question left for the wiring: can the caller afford `h_open`? R486 answers: it costs nothing.

**The two discharges, both free.** (1) **The depth obligation** — R485's `_nested` assemble already shed `h_p_depth`; descending the seq recursion lands the enclosing opener `p` at depth `d := balance lo p ≥ 0`, and the assemble re-derived every depth-`0` read from the enclosing Dyck floor. There is NO depth-`0` fact for the wiring to supply. (2) **The typed-opener discriminator** — R475's `enclosingLocate` slot only offers the weaker `flowBracketDelta tokens[p]!.val = 1`, but `seqOpenerType_of_located_and_gate` RECONSTRUCTS the `[` from `delta = 1` + the gate's `btFold`-top marker `hgate.2.1` (`SeqTypedInterior`'s middle conjunct, `(btFold (some []) (take a)).bind head? = some true`) + the locator floor: a `{` would push `false` and the interior floor cannot pop it back, contradicting the `= some true` head. The delta `= 1` alone can't decide `[` vs `{`; the gate's enclosing-type mark is what disambiguates.

**The transferable rule.** A refinement surfaced as an explicit consume-side residual (R481, because the producer's NAMED slot premise is too weak to derive it) is often discharged FOR FREE at the wiring site from a CO-LOCATED invariant the consumer already carries — reconstruct in place, don't thread it through every caller. The discriminating question is not "does the producer's NAMED premise determine the refinement?" (R481: no) but "does SOME fact co-located at the wiring determine it?" (R486: yes — the gate mark). A residual is only truly OWED by the caller if NO co-located invariant pins it: two facts that each underdetermine the output (the test: each premise alone admits a witness with no output) can TOGETHER pin it. This is the POSITIVE complement of the head-blind/end-free gate findings — there a weak gate ADMITS spurious shapes; here a weak discriminator is RESOLVED by a richer co-located mark.

### Reflection 484 — a base-depth hypothesis costs exactly its EQUALITY reads to drop: once the depth-general primitive exists, grep where `h_p_depth : balance lo p = 0` is READ — floor reads (`≥ 0`) are free, only `rw [h_depth]` substitutions of the pinned `= 0` cost a re-derivation. **The CONSUME side of R483: the R478 close-within locator generalizes by a PURE SWAP (zero equality reads), landed as the `_nested` sibling.**

**Context.** R482 + R483 landed the depth-general close PRIMITIVE (the balance core `flowBracketBalance_matching_close_nested` and the typed locators `flowBracketBalance_matching_close_{seq,map}_nested`, all dropping `h_k_depth`). R484 does this and surfaces the reusable *scoping* lesson: how to count the cost of dropping a base-depth hypothesis before touching the proof.

**Floor reads vs equality reads.** Grep the hypothesis name in the proof body; every occurrence is one of two kinds. A **FLOOR read** is a fact derived from the Dyck floor `balance … ≥ 0` — monotone and frame-stable, so it never touches `h_p_depth` at all; it reads the *enclosing* floor `≥ 0`, true at every nesting depth. An **EQUALITY read** is an `rw [h_depth]` that substitutes the pinned baseline `= 0` — depth-BOUND, because at depth ≥ 1 the baseline is `d := balance lo p ≥ 0`, not `0`, so the rewrite is gone and the downstream `omega` must re-derive from `≥ 0`. So **cost(drop a base-depth hypothesis) = (the locator call → a pure SWAP to the depth-general twin) + (one re-derivation per `=0`-equality read)** — both countable by grep, no surprises in the body.

In the R478 close-within locator, `h_p_depth` funnelled to EXACTLY ONE read: the `flowBracketBalance_matching_close_seq` call. Every downstream fact — `a ≤ j`, `balance a j = 0`, `b ≤ j`, and the upper containment `j ≤ hi` (via R477 `seqLocatedClose_within_body`, which reads `hiE ≤ hi` off the enclosing `≥ 0`, not `= 0`) — is a FLOOR read. So the generalization is a pure swap: the proof body is byte-identical, only the hypothesis type (`= 0 ↦ 0 ≤ …`, here simply *dropped*) and the one call (`…_seq ↦ …_seq_nested`) change.

### Reflection 483 — the nested TYPED close locator is a FRAME, not a re-proof: a depth-≥1 opener sits over a base stack `s_k` whose bottom markers are inert, so the depth-0 typed argument frames by `s_k` and collapses to the IDENTICAL depth-0 conclusion. **The typed half of R482's depth-general close locator — and the frame is structurally SIMPLER than the depth-0 special case it generalizes.**

But the seq/map close locators are TWO layers: the balance core locates the close *position* `j`, and the TYPED layer (`matching_close_typed_{generic,core}`, then `flowBracketBalance_matching_close_{seq,map}`) pins the close *token type* (a `[` matches a `]`, never a `}`) via the `btFold` stack. R483 lifts the typed layer off depth 0.

**Re-base a scalar, FRAME a stack.** This is the conceptual payoff. The balance layer carries a scalar `Int` depth, which shifts uniformly under nesting — so R482 RE-BASED (re-derived against `balance lo k`, since the global Dyck floor `≥ 0` does not shift-transfer, becoming `≥ d`). The typed layer carries a `List Bool` STACK, and a nested opener sits over a base stack `s_k` (length `d = balance lo k`) whose bottom `d` markers — the enclosing openers — are INERT across the positive-depth span `[k, j]`. So the nested proof FRAMES the depth-0 one rather than re-deriving it: the base stack is a suffix the interior never reads. Opener push frames up (`btStep_frame`: `[] → [b]` becomes `s_k → b :: s_k`); the balanced `WellTyped` interior `[k+1, j)` (recovered via `WellTyped_infix_balanced`) folds from `b :: s_k` back to `b :: s_k` (`WellTyped_frame`); and `btStep_frame_inv` strips `s_k` off the close — collapsing the nested `btStep tokens[j]! (b :: s_k) = some s_k` to the IDENTICAL depth-0 `btStep tokens[j]! [b] = some []`. The depth-0 close-type readers (`btStep_pop_eq_{seqEnd,mapEnd}`) then apply verbatim. **The frame is CLEANER than the special case**: the depth-0 `matching_close_typed_generic` open-coded interior preservation as bottom-preservation (`btFold_getLast?_preserved` + a length-1 singleton argument); the nested proof replaces that with `WellTyped_frame` ("a balanced body returns to ANY prefix"), so the generalization is structurally simpler than the thing it generalizes — framing names the abstraction the special case did by hand.

**LANDED (R483 — verified-but-unconsumed, `WellBracketed.lean` part 5.5, after `WellTyped_subrange`):** four lemmas, all DROPPING `h_k_depth`.
- `matching_close_typed_generic_nested` — the genuine new proof (the framing argument above): base stack via `WellTyped_take_stack`, opener push via `btStep_frame`, interior `WellTyped` via `WellTyped_infix_balanced` then `WellTyped_frame`, close strip via `btStep_frame_inv`. Takes the RELATIVE interior floor `flowBracketBalance tokens (k+1) i ≥ 0` (exactly the balance core's output) in place of the absolute `≥ 1`.
- `matching_close_typed_core_nested` — the array-bridge specialization (`length`/`balance`/`value` bridges verbatim from the depth-0 `_core`, calling the nested generic).
- `flowBracketBalance_matching_close_{seq,map}_nested` — consumer-facing: locate `j` via `flowBracketBalance_matching_close_nested`, read the close type via `matching_close_typed_core_nested` + `btStep_pop_eq_{seqEnd,mapEnd}`. These are SIMPLER than their depth-0 originals — the relative interior floor is the balance core's own output, so NO `flowBracketBalance_interior_dyck` re-derivation.

Build green (full 729 jobs; Tests.Reflections 186), frontier exactly 4 (EmitterScannability `:315`/`:809`/`:848` + NonemptyStructure `:10641`). `#print axioms` of all four = `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` (no `sorryAx`). Demo `Tests/Reflections/NestedTypedLocatorIsAFrame.lean` (a `step`/`fold` stack machine; `step_frame`/`fold_frame` the framing engines; `fold_frame_self` the balanced-body-returns-to-any-prefix `WellTyped_frame` analogue; `nested_close_via_frame` the punchline that the nested close IS the depth-0 close framed by `s_k`; `nestedWord`/`inner_close_is_framed` a concrete depth-1 `[ { x } ]` witness). The principle lifted to `ref-nested-typed-locator-is-a-frame`, paired with `ref-located-encloser-is-nested-rebase-locator` (R482) as the two halves of the depth-general close locator.

**Next step.** With the depth-general close locator complete (balance R482 + typed R483), wire it back: **(i)** re-prove R478 `seqClose_of_located_and_enclosing_within` WITHOUT `h_p_depth`, calling `flowBracketBalance_matching_close_seq_nested`. **(ii)** DROP `h_p_depth` from the R481 assemble `seqEnclosingLocate_of_seqOpener_at_depth`, discharging `h_open` for free via `seqOpenerType_of_located_and_gate`, and finally WIRE the assemble into R475 (`seqWidthEnc_of_enclosingLocate_and_recIH`). Then (β) the carrier ↔ `SafeBodyUnit` half via `seqLocalCarrier_of_widthEnc`. In parallel (independent): the MAP-side per-window producer + the recursive deep NAVIGATOR (R467 brick (b)); wiring seq + map producers + the 6 facts into `flowSubrangesOk_of_window_producers` discharges BOTH `FlowSubrangesOk` sorries at once.

### Reflection 482 — the located INNERMOST encloser is at depth ≥ 1, so the close locator must be DEPTH-GENERAL: re-base the matching-close scan relative to the opener's own depth, don't re-restrict the consumer. **Wiring R481 into R475 hit a FALSE premise — `h_p_depth : balance lo p = 0` does not hold for deeply-nested gated windows; the depth-general balance core lands as the fix's first brick.**

**Context — wiring R481 surfaced a false premise.** R481's queued next step was to WIRE the (α) seq assemble `seqEnclosingLocate_of_seqOpener_at_depth` into `seqWidthEnc_of_enclosingLocate_and_recIH` (R475) by discharging its two surfaced discriminators from the seq recursion's consume context. Reading that context (`seqLocalCarrier_of_widthEnc`) found: it locates, at every gated window `[a, b)`, the **INNERMOST** enclosing opener `p` (`seqEnclosingOpener_of_gate`, which runs the backward scan to the immediate encloser) and asks `enclosingLocate`/`h_widthEnc` for `p`'s full bracket span `[p, hiE)`. The carrier `SeqInteriorSeparators tokens lo hi` quantifies over **all** gated sub-windows including DEEPLY-NESTED ones (e.g. the inner `[1]` interior of `[ [[1]], 2 ]` passes the window-absolute gate), and for such a window the innermost encloser `p` sits at **depth ≥ 1** in the body window. So R481's assemble premise `h_p_depth : flowBracketBalance tokens lo p = 0` — R478's sole depth sink, ultimately `flowBracketBalance_matching_close_seq`'s `h_k_depth` — is **not merely unprovable but actually FALSE**. This corrects R481's "the located `p` is a top-level `[` at depth `0`": the seq-type half is right (see below) but the depth-`0` half is wrong — the recursion descends into nested `[`, so the located encloser is nested, not top-level.

**Of the two discriminators, only `h_p_depth` is the gap.** The OTHER R481 discriminator `h_open : tokens[p]!.val = .flowSequenceStart` is **FREE** in the consume context: `seqOpenerType_of_located_and_gate` already derives it from the gate's enclosure mark (`btFold (take a) top = some true`, "the immediately enclosing bracket is a seq") plus the located-opener facts. So the seq-type refinement R481 surfaced is discharged for free; the depth-`0` refinement is the genuine residual — and it cannot be discharged because it is false.

**The reusable point — re-base the scan, don't re-restrict the consumer** ([[ref-located-encloser-is-nested-rebase-locator]]). The trio child-bracket constructors (R479/R480) are already depth-free, so the SOLE depth-`0` dependency in the assemble is the close LOCATION (R478 → `flowBracketBalance_matching_close_seq`). And the matching-close SCAN never reads the opener's absolute depth — every clause is a DIFFERENCE from the opener's own level `balance lo k` (the close is "first RETURN to that level", the interior floor is "never drops BACK to it"). So the depth-`0` locator generalizes to a nested opener purely by RE-BASING: substitute the return level `0 ↦ balance lo k` and the just-after-opener level `1 ↦ balance lo k + 1`, and state the located close + floor RELATIVE to the opener (`balance (k+1) j = 0`, `balance (k+1) i ≥ 0`). What does NOT shift-transfer is the GLOBAL Dyck floor `balance lo i ≥ 0` (under the shift it becomes `≥ d`), so the generalization RE-PROVES rather than reduces: the depth-`0` proof's recurse step used the global floor to bridge `≠ 0 ⟹ ≥ 1`; the nested proof switches that step to the threaded interior invariant `balance lo i ≥ balance lo k + 1`, leaving the global floor needed ONLY to pin the opener's own depth `d ≥ 0`. This is [[ref-scan-owns-the-depth-debt]] discharged: R480 located the depth debt in the scan; this pays it by generalizing the scan.

**LANDED (R482 — `flowBracketBalance_matching_close_nested`):** In `ParserGrammableBase.lean` (right after the depth-`0` `flowBracketBalance_matching_close`): `theorem flowBracketBalance_matching_close_nested (tokens) (lo k hi) (h_lo_k : lo ≤ k) (h_k_hi : k < hi) (h_hi_sz : hi ≤ tokens.size) (h_k_open : flowBracketDelta tokens[k]!.val = 1) (h_total : flowBracketBalance tokens lo hi = 0) (h_dyck : ∀ i, lo ≤ i → i ≤ hi → flowBracketBalance tokens lo i ≥ 0) : ∃ j, k < j ∧ j < hi ∧ flowBracketDelta tokens[j]!.val = -1 ∧ flowBracketBalance tokens (k+1) j = 0 ∧ (∀ i, k < i → i ≤ j → flowBracketBalance tokens (k+1) i ≥ 0)`. The `h_k_depth : balance lo k = 0` hypothesis of the depth-`0` version is **DROPPED**; the forward `find` fixpoint threads the interior invariant against `balance lo k` (not the literal `0`) and the output floor is re-based onto `k+1`. Proof is a mechanical generalization of the depth-`0` original: `h_d_ge : balance lo k ≥ 0` from the Dyck floor at `k`, the same one-step `step` recurrence, the same `find` induction with `0`/`1` replaced by `balance lo k`/`balance lo k + 1`, and a final `flowBracketBalance_compose` to re-base the absolute floor onto the opener. Full build green (728 jobs); frontier exactly 4 (EmitterScannability.lean:315/809/848 + NonemptyStructure.lean:10641), unchanged; sorry-free; `#print axioms` = `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, no `sorryAx`. Demo `Tests/Reflections/DepthGeneralMatchingClose.lean` (`matchesClose` states the close relation as differences from `B k`; `matchesClose_shift` proves it INVARIANT under a uniform shift `B' = B + c` — the formal content of "depth-relative, so depth-`0` re-bases to any depth"; `depth0_precondition_fails : Bnest 1 = 1 ≠ 0` the nested-opener obstruction; `nested_opener_has_matching_close : matchesClose Bnest 1 3` the close IS locatable at depth 1).

**Next step — re-base the TYPED close locators, then R478, then re-wire.** The balance core lands; the typed close finders are next. (i) Re-base `matching_close_typed_core` / `flowBracketBalance_matching_close_seq` (and the `_map` mirror) onto the nested balance core — the typed version's only depth-`0` use is `h_k_push : btStep tokens[k]! [] = some [b]` (push onto the EMPTY stack); for a nested opener the push is onto the enclosing stack `s_k` and the matching close pops back to `s_k`, so the generalization carries a base stack `s_k` instead of `[]` through `matching_close_typed_generic`. (ii) Re-prove R478 `seqClose_of_located_and_enclosing_within` WITHOUT `h_p_depth`, calling the nested typed locator. (iii) DROP `h_p_depth` from `seqEnclosingLocate_of_seqOpener_at_depth` (R481), discharging `h_open` for free via `seqOpenerType_of_located_and_gate`, and finally WIRE the assemble into R475. **Then (β)** the carrier ↔ `SafeBodyUnit` half via `seqLocalCarrier_of_widthEnc`. **In parallel (independent):** the MAP-side per-window producer + the recursive deep NAVIGATOR (R467 brick (b)); wiring seq + map producers + the 6 facts into `flowSubrangesOk_of_window_producers` discharges BOTH `FlowSubrangesOk` sorries at once.

### Reflection 481 — a GENERIC-discriminant premise underdetermines a TYPE-SPECIFIC output: the assemble must SURFACE the type-refinement as an explicit hypothesis, not derive it. **The (α) `enclosingLocate` ASSEMBLE for the seq child — the trio of "given close" constructors composed into the full residual, fed one located close.**

**Context — the assemble, and what writing it discovered.** With the "given close" trio complete (R479 content, R480 window, plus the all-depth deep sibling), the (α) residual is finally assembleable: from a located enclosing opener `p` of the typed interior `[a, b)` inside the body window `[lo, hi)`, deliver R475's `enclosingLocate` payload `lo ≤ p ∧ ∃ hiE, b ≤ hiE ∧ hiE ≤ tokens.size ∧ hiE ≤ hi ∧ FlowBodyWindow/Deep/Content tokens p hiE`, feeding ONE located close UNIFORMLY to all three constructors. Writing it surfaced a latent gap: `seqWidthEnc_of_enclosingLocate_and_recIH` (R475) hands the assemble the GENERIC located-opener premise `flowBracketDelta tokens[p]!.val = 1` — "`p` is *some* opener" — but `delta = 1` is satisfied by BOTH `.flowSequenceStart` (`[`) and `.flowMappingStart` (`{`), while the seq output `FlowBodyContent` encodes a `.flowSequenceEnd` close and R478's close locator needs `tokens[p]!.val = .flowSequenceStart` to guarantee the matching close is a `]`.

**The reusable point — surface the refinement, don't derive it** ([[ref-generic-discriminant-underdetermines-output]]). The type-specific refinement (`.flowSequenceStart`) is PROVABLY NOT derivable from the generic discriminant (`delta = 1`): a `{`-opener satisfies the premise yet has a MAP child, not a seq child — a spurious inhabitant the seq deliverable cannot represent. The honest move is to take the refinement as an EXPLICIT hypothesis of the assemble; that RETYPES the residual ([[ref-reduction-by-import]]) from "build `enclosingLocate`" to the strictly smaller "at the located `p`, discharge seq-opener-type + depth-0" — pure boundary facts, no further structure. The assemble's job is to SURFACE the irreducible refinement as a named consume-side residual, not invent a derivation that cannot exist. Same shape as the head-blind / end-free gate findings ([[ref-probe-provider-head-blind-gate]], [[ref-end-free-gate-underdetermines-close]]) but on the CONSUMER's SUPPLIED premise rather than the producer's precondition: a too-generic discriminant admits inhabitants the deliverable cannot inhabit. The irreducibility is purely about the INPUT premise being too generic — the same refinement IS recoverable once the OUTPUT already pins the type (the converse `SeqChild → isSeqOpener` is free).

**The two discriminators are the consume-side residual.** The assemble takes BOTH strengthenings as explicit hypotheses: `h_open : tokens[p]!.val = .flowSequenceStart` (the seq-opener type) and `h_p_depth : flowBracketBalance tokens lo p = 0` (R478's sole depth sink, [[ref-scan-owns-the-depth-debt]]). In the consume context the located `p` is a top-level `[` at depth `0` — the seq recursion only ever descends into nested `[` (the `{` branch is the near-leaf map oracle, no seq IH) — so both hold by construction; here they isolate EXACTLY what the `enclosingLocate` wiring must still supply.

**LANDED (R481 — `seqEnclosingLocate_of_seqOpener_at_depth`):** In `SeqInteriorSeparators.lean` (right after R478 `seqClose_of_located_and_enclosing_within`): `theorem seqEnclosingLocate_of_seqOpener_at_depth (tokens) (lo hi) (h_win : FlowBodyWindow tokens lo hi) (h_deep : FlowBodyContentDeep tokens lo hi) (a b p) (ha : lo ≤ a) (hab : a ≤ b) (hb : b ≤ hi) (hbal : flowBracketBalance tokens lo a ≠ 0) (hgate : SeqTypedInterior tokens a b) (hpa : p < a) (h_open : tokens[p]!.val = .flowSequenceStart) (h_body_bal : flowBracketBalance tokens (p+1) a = 0) (h_loc_floor : ∀ i, p+1 ≤ i → i ≤ a → flowBracketBalance tokens (p+1) i ≥ 0) (h_p_depth : flowBracketBalance tokens lo p = 0) : lo ≤ p ∧ ∃ hiE, b ≤ hiE ∧ hiE ≤ tokens.size ∧ hiE ≤ hi ∧ FlowBodyWindow tokens p hiE ∧ FlowBodyContentDeep tokens p hiE ∧ FlowBodyContent tokens p hiE`. The five moves: (1) `lo ≤ p` from R476 `seqLocatedOpener_within_body`; (2) locate the close `hiS` from R478 (re-exporting `balance (p+1) hiS = 0`, `tokens[hiS]! = .flowSequenceEnd`, the `(p+1)`-keyed floor `≥ 0`); (3) the CHILD-keyed floor `balance p i ≥ 1` on `[p+1, hiS]` by one `flowBracketBalance_compose` through the opener (`balance p (p+1) = 1`); (4) `hiS < hi` (so `hiE := hiS+1 ≤ hi`) from `balance lo hiS = balance lo p + balance p (p+1) + balance (p+1) hiS = 0 + 1 + 0 = 1 ≠ 0 = balance lo hi`; (5) the three depth-free constructors `flowBodyWindow_child_bracket_at` (R480) / `flowBodyContentDeep_child_bracket` / `flowBodyContent_child_bracket` (R479) at `k := p, j := hiS`. Full build green (727-class); frontier exactly 4 (EmitterScannability.lean:315/809/848 + NonemptyStructure.lean:10641); sorry-free; `#print axioms` = `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, IDENTICAL to the family (the `Classical.choice` inherited via R478/`WellTyped_subrange`), no `sorryAx`. Demo `Tests/Reflections/GenericDiscriminantUnderdeterminesOutput.lean` (`isOpener` the generic premise vs `isSeqOpener` the refinement; `seqChild_of_seqOpener` the constructor; `generic_opener_underdetermines` the negative `isOpener .mapOpen ∧ ¬ SeqChild .mapOpen`; `seqOpener_implies_opener`/`seqOpener_of_seqChild` the strictly-stronger + converse-recoverable directions).

**Next step — WIRE the assemble into R475 (discharge the two discriminators).** The remaining (α) work is to instantiate `seqWidthEnc_of_enclosingLocate_and_recIH` (R475) with `seqEnclosingLocate_of_seqOpener_at_depth`, discharging the two surfaced discriminators at the located `p` from the SEQ recursion's consume context: the located opener is a `[` (seq-typed, never `{`) at depth `0` (top-level in the body window). This bridges the GENERIC `delta = 1` premise R475 quantifies over to the SEQ-specific `.flowSequenceStart` + depth-`0` the assemble needs — the head-necessity / depth-`0` consume-context facts. **Then (β)** the carrier ↔ `SafeBodyUnit` half via `seqLocalCarrier_of_widthEnc`. **In parallel (independent):** the MAP-side per-window producer (the `{`-child analog of this seq assemble — the other inhabitant of the generic `delta = 1` premise) + the recursive deep NAVIGATOR (R467 brick (b)); wiring seq + map producers + the 6 facts into `flowSubrangesOk_of_window_producers` discharges BOTH `FlowSubrangesOk` sorries at once.

### Reflection 480 — the depth-`0` discriminator a child-window family member carries belongs to the LOCATING SCAN, not the member's content; take the located close as INPUT and EVERY constructor (window/deep/content) is DEPTH-AGNOSTIC. **The (α) window member, depth-free: the trio is now complete — one depth-needing locator + three depth-free "given close" constructors.**

**Context — the third "given close" member, and the depth caveat it dissolves.** R479 landed the (α.2) CONTENT half over `[p, hiE)`; the (α) `enclosingLocate` residual's last owed structure is the WINDOW member `FlowBodyWindow tokens p hiE` (`= FlowBodyWindow tokens k (j+1)`, `k := p`, `j := hiS`, `hiE := hiS+1`). The existing `flowBodyWindow_child_bracket` (R470) produces it — but it LOCATES the close `j` ITSELF via the forward scan `flowBracketBalance_matching_close`, and that scan is the SOLE reason it requires the depth-`0` discriminator `h_k_depth : balance lo k = 0` (the scan reads the matching close off the `lo`-keyed running balance returning to depth `0`, which coincides with the bracket's OWN close only when `k` starts at depth `0`). R475's `enclosingLocate` hypothesis does NOT carry `balance lo p = 0`, so threading it would push a depth obligation through the whole assemble — the [[ref-rebase-fact-from-enclosing-window]] caveat.

**The reusable point — the SCAN owns the depth debt** ([[ref-scan-owns-the-depth-debt]], a sharpening of [[ref-weak-family-member-projects-depth-free]]). R479 showed the PROJECTED content member is depth-free; this shows the directly-CONSTRUCTED window member is too — and reveals WHY: the depth-`0` premise was never a property of the window's CONTENT, only a precondition of the SCAN. Remove the scan — take the located close `j`, the closer delta, the interior balance `balance (k+1) j = 0`, and the CHILD-ORIGIN floor `balance k i ≥ 1` (keyed on `k`, never the outer `lo`) as INPUTS — and the construction of `FlowBodyWindow tokens k (j+1)` carries NO `balance lo k = 0`: `balanced` is the `flowBracketBalance_compose` chain `(+1)+0+(-1)=0` (which CANCELS the depth term), `dyck` reads `≥ 1` straight off the floor (no re-base through `balance lo k` — the only place the scan version touched depth), `wellTyped` transports by `WellTyped_subrange` over the balanced Dyck subrange `[k, j+1) ⊆ [lo, hi)`. Abstractly, with `childBal B k i = B i − B k` (`B = balance lo ·`), the depth offset is visible as the `− B k` term: the constructor cancels it (every fact is a `childBal`), the scan's return test `B (j+1) = 0` keeps it.

**The family splits, the depth obligation concentrates.** The trio `{flowBodyWindow_child_bracket_at, flowBodyContentDeep_child_bracket, flowBodyContent_child_bracket}` is now UNIFORM: three depth-free "given close" constructors, all keyed on the child origin `k`, plus exactly ONE depth-needing locator (R478's `seqClose_of_located_and_enclosing_within`, which carries `h_p_depth`). When the assemble feeds all three the SINGLE close R478 located, none re-pays the depth — the assemble owns `balance lo p = 0` exactly once, at the locator, supplied from the consume-context discriminator (SeqInteriorSeparators.lean:502).

**LANDED (R480 — `flowBodyWindow_child_bracket_at`):** In `NonemptyStructure.lean` (right after `flowBodyWindow_child_bracket`, `:~6959`): `theorem flowBodyWindow_child_bracket_at (tokens) (lo k j hi) (h_win : FlowBodyWindow tokens lo hi) (h_lo_k : lo ≤ k) (h_k_j : k < j) (h_j_hi : j + 1 ≤ hi) (h_k_open : flowBracketDelta tokens[k]!.val = 1) (h_jclose : flowBracketDelta tokens[j]!.val = -1) (h_inner : flowBracketBalance tokens (k+1) j = 0) (h_floor : ∀ i, k+1 ≤ i → i ≤ j → flowBracketBalance tokens k i ≥ 1) : FlowBodyWindow tokens k (j+1)`. Body mirrors `flowBodyWindow_child_bracket` MINUS the `flowBracketBalance_matching_close` scan: the same `single`/`flowBracketBalance_compose` derivations of `balanced`, the same endpoint+interior `dyck` split, the same `WellTyped_subrange` transport — but the `dyck` interior case reads `≥ 1` off `h_floor` directly instead of re-basing the scan's `lo`-keyed `hfloor` through `h_k_depth`, so NO `balance lo k = 0` appears. **Next step — the (α) ASSEMBLE (the trio is complete).** With all three "given close" constructors in hand, assemble `enclosingLocate`'s `lo ≤ p ∧ ∃ hiE, b ≤ hiE ∧ hiE ≤ tokens.size ∧ hiE ≤ hi ∧ FlowBodyWindow/Deep/Content tokens p hiE`: (1) call R478 `seqClose_of_located_and_enclosing_within` for `hiS` (carrying `balance (p+1) hiS = 0`, `tokens[hiS]!.val = .flowSequenceEnd`, the `(p+1)`-keyed floor `≥ 0`), supplying its `h_p_depth : balance lo p = 0` from the consume-context discriminator; (2) set `hiE := hiS + 1`; (3) bridge the `(p+1)`-keyed floor to the child-keyed `balance p i ≥ 1` by one `flowBracketBalance_compose` through the opener (`balance p (p+1) = 1`); (4) feed the three constructors at `k := p, j := hiS` (closer delta from the typed `.flowSequenceEnd`, interior balance and floor from R478); (5) combine with `lo ≤ p` (R476), `hiE ≤ hi` (R477), `b ≤ hiE` (`b ≤ hiS < hiS+1`), `hiE ≤ size`. ### Reflection 479 — the WEAK member of a child-window structure family is a PROJECTION of its strong sibling through the family's existing strong→weak projector (residuals VACUOUS against the window's own interior floor), and is DEPTH-AGNOSTIC because the floor is keyed on the CHILD origin — so the depth caveat lives ENTIRELY in the locating sibling. **The (α.2) content half: the third and final opener-inclusive child-bracket sibling.**

**Context — the (α.2) content structures over `[p, hiE)`.** With the close `hiE = hiS + 1` now locatable (R478) and the two containments in hand (R476/R477), the (α) `enclosingLocate` residual still owes the THREE content structures over the located enclosing frame `[p, hiE)`: `FlowBodyWindow tokens p hiE`, `FlowBodyContentDeep tokens p hiE`, `FlowBodyContent tokens p hiE`. ### Reflection 475 — a width-gated IH over an inner CONTAINED frame is dischargeable from the OUTER joint width IH for free, and the per-step ASSEMBLE that does it ISOLATES the locator while SIDESTEPPING the SafeBodyUnit ↔ carrier ↔ recursion circularity. **First brick of the body-width joint induction (R474's queued Next step).**

**Context — author the joint induction, smallest half first.** R474 made `h_widthEnc` satisfiable; its Next step was the body-width joint induction co-producing, per body window `[lo, hi)`, the pair `SeqInteriorSeparators tokens lo hi ∧ RecSeqBody ((take hi).drop lo)`. Reading the landed machinery shows that induction has TWO halves of very different difficulty. The carrier half (`seqLocalCarrier_of_widthEnc`) needs a `SafeBodyUnit` per window, and that is circular — the carrier needs `h_safe`, `h_safe` comes from `RecSeqBody.toSafeBodyUnit`, and `RecSeqBody` needs the carrier (`seqRoot_seqInteriorSeparators`'s doc, lines 1187–1196, records exactly this) — broken only by the width well-ordering, a multi-piece wiring. The OTHER half — discharging `h_widthEnc`'s inner recursion IH from the joint IH — touches none of that. Land it first.

**What `h_widthEnc`'s deliverable actually is.** Per gated window `[a, b)` with enclosing opener `p`, it is the ENCLOSING-WINDOW facts of a frame `[p, hiE)` (`FlowBodyWindow`/`FlowBodyContentDeep`/`FlowBodyContent`) PLUS a `RecSeqBody` IH for THAT frame's sub-windows, gated by the FRAME width `hi' - lo' < hiE - p`. The joint induction's own IH is gated by the BODY width `hi' - lo' < hi - lo`. **The two gates differ**, so the inner IH is not literally the outer IH.

**The bridge — frame containment (the one piece of real content, R473's `body_ih_covers_frame_ih`).** The locator delivers the frame INSIDE the body: `lo ≤ p` and `hiE ≤ hi`. All three obligations are pure `omega`. The containment is LOAD-BEARING: drop it and pick a frame WIDER than the body (`hiE - p > hi - lo`) and the inner gate no longer implies the outer.

**The reusable point.** When a producer-guarded deliverable carries its own width-gated recursion IH over an inner CONTAINED frame, that inner IH is dischargeable from an outer joint-induction IH for free. So write the per-step ASSEMBLE as a standalone lemma lifting the two residuals — `enclosingLocate` (the LOCATE residual, returns the contained frame + content facts + the two containments) and `recIH` (the joint width IH) — and discharge the inner IH by `recIH` under the three `omega` bridges. This proves the width arithmetic, isolates the LOCATOR as the single residual, and touches NO `SafeBodyUnit`/carrier — it is the half of the joint induction that sidesteps the circularity. ### Reflection 473 — a width-recursion producer that DROPS the BRANCH-GUARD selecting its own sub-case MIS-DIAGNOSES its recursion MEASURE. The dropped guard, restored, BOTH excludes the out-of-range instance AND keeps the natural (body-width) measure. **CORRECTS Reflection 472.**

**Context — R472's SMALLEST-FIRST sub-de-risk, run this turn.** R472's Next step queued the FRAME-WIDTH-KEYED joint induction, with a sub-de-risk to run first: confirm the frame base case `FlowBodyWindow ∧ FlowBodyContentDeep ∧ FlowBodyContent tokens 1 (size-1)` for the document bracket. Reading the actual structures to author it surfaced a CONTRADICTION that overturns R472's diagnosis.

**The finding — `FlowBodyWindow tokens 1 (size-1)` is UNINHABITABLE, and R472 read the WRONG branch.** `FlowBodyWindow` carries `lo_ge : 2 ≤ lo` and `hi_le : hi ≤ tokens.size - 2` — both EXCLUDE the document bracket `[1, size-1)`. So R472's proposed frame base case is ill-typed. Chasing why, the carrier dispatcher `seqInteriorSeparators_of_safebody_and_descent` (line 1167) CASE-SPLITS every gated sub-window `[a, b) ⊆ [lo, hi)` on `flowBracketBalance tokens lo a = 0`:
- the **`then` branch** (`balance lo a = 0`, a TOP-LEVEL window at depth `0`) is handled by `seqEnclosingFacts_provider_of_located` *directly from the flat root `SafeBodyUnit`* (`h_safe`), with `loS = lo, hiS = hi` — the whole body, NO descent, NO nested `FlowBodyWindow`. The code's own comment (line 333): "The `loS - 1 = 1` opener is the outer `[` — no descent is consulted." **This is exactly R472's `p = lo - 1` case.**
- the **`else` branch** (`balance lo a ≠ 0`, a STRICTLY NESTED window) is the ONLY branch `desc` / `h_widthEnc` handles.

So `h_widthEnc` never sees the `p = lo - 1` (document opener) case — R472 attributed a `then`-branch instance to the `else`-branch producer.

**Under the `else`-branch guard the BODY-width measure CLOSES — no re-keying.** When `balance lo a ≠ 0`, the located opener `p` (`flowBracketBalance_backward_open_locate`, giving `balance (p+1) a = 0`) CANNOT be `lo - 1`: if `p + 1 = lo` then `balance (p+1) a = balance lo a ≠ 0`, contradicting the locator. Hence `lo ≤ p`, the enclosing frame `[p, hiE) ⊆ [lo, hi)` is CONTAINED, width `hiE - p ≤ hi - lo` — NEVER `+2` — and the BODY-width IH (`< hi - lo`) covers the deliverable's frame IH (`< hiE - p ≤ hi - lo`) with NO gap. The `<` is strict, so even the equality case `p = lo, hiE = hi` (one nested bracket filling the whole body) is covered. R472's `+2` arithmetic was real but for the `then` branch only.

**The real bug — a DROPPED GUARD (`h_widthEnc` is the producer-guarded-quantifier trap).** `h_widthEnc`'s signature (line 2628) quantifies over `a b p` WITHOUT the `flowBracketBalance tokens lo a ≠ 0` hypothesis — even though `seqLocalCarrier_of_widthEnc` binds it (`_hbal`, line 2642) and has it in scope at the call site (line 2647 simply does not pass it). As stated, `h_widthEnc` must hold for the `p = lo - 1` instance, which demands the uninhabitable `FlowBodyWindow tokens 1 hiE`: undischargeable yet type-checks ([[ref-producer-guarded-quantifier]]). The fix is to THREAD the guard into `h_widthEnc` (and pass `_hbal`), keeping BODY-width keying — [[ref-guarded-universal-fold-relocates-guard]] / [[ref-reconstruct-in-place-over-relocate]] applied to a producer contract: the consumer already establishes the guard; relocate it into the producer's hypotheses. New memory [[ref-dropped-branch-guard-mis-measures-recursion]] (corrects [[ref-enclosing-frame-rekeys-width-recursion]]; sharpens [[ref-probe-deferred-universal-before-producing]] — probe WHICH branch the producer serves before measuring).

### Reflection 472 — the recursion MEASURE is the de-risk: a width strong-induction whose per-window obligation references the ENCLOSING FRAME (one bracket-level OUT, wider by exactly 2) CANNOT be keyed on the inner BODY width — the IH `< bodyWidth` never reaches the frame obligation at `bodyWidth + 2`. RE-KEY on the ENCLOSING-FRAME width (the outermost frame is the base, every descent goes strictly INWARD)

> **⚠ L4YAML INSTANCE CORRECTED — see Reflection 473 above ([[ref-dropped-branch-guard-mis-measures-recursion]]).** The `p = lo - 1` enclosing-frame case diagnosed below is the carrier dispatcher's **`then` branch** (top-level windows, `balance lo a = 0`), handled directly from the flat root `SafeBodyUnit` — NOT the `desc`/`h_widthEnc` branch this co-construction measures. That branch (`balance lo a ≠ 0`) has `lo ≤ p`, so the frame `[p, hiE) ⊆ [lo, hi)` is CONTAINED (width `≤ hi - lo`, never `+2`) and **BODY-width keying closes with no gap**. The real defect was a DROPPED branch-guard in `h_widthEnc`'s signature, not the measure; do NOT re-key on frame width. The general lesson below still holds for a producer that GENUINELY references the enclosing frame, but does not apply to the L4YAML `h_widthEnc` instance. The frame base case it queued (`FlowBodyWindow tokens 1 (size-1)`) is moreover UNINHABITABLE (`FlowBodyWindow.lo_ge : 2 ≤ lo`).

**Context — R471's SMALLEST-FIRST de-risk, run this turn.** R471's Next step queued the joint width strong-induction discharging `h_widthEnc`'s last owed half (the width-recursion IH), as a `Nat.strongRecOn` on the BODY width `hi - lo` co-producing, per seq body window `[lo, hi)`, the PAIR `SeqInteriorSeparators tokens lo hi ∧ RecSeqBody ((take hi).drop lo)` — and queued one question to settle FIRST: does the child window `[p, hiE) = [p, j+1)` the R470/R471 siblings produce satisfy the IH's width guard `hiE - p < hi - lo`? This turn read the consumer chain end-to-end (`seqLocalCarrier_of_widthEnc`'s `h_widthEnc` → `seqEnclosingOpener_of_gate` → `seqDescent_provider_of_located` → `seqChild_safeBodyUnit`) and `seqWindowRecSeqBody_general`'s `G`. **The answer is NO — and the failure is structural, deciding the recursion's MEASURE, not a fixable off-by-one.**

**The arithmetic (confirmed by balance, not intuition).** The carrier `SeqInteriorSeparators tokens lo hi` quantifies over EVERY gated sub-window `[a, b) ⊆ [lo, hi)`. Instantiate at a TOP-LEVEL gated window — one at depth `0` of the body, `balance lo a = 0`. The backward locator `seqEnclosingOpener_of_gate` does not know `lo`; it returns the NEAREST opener left of `a`, which for a top-level window is `p = lo - 1` — the body's OWN bracket opener, sitting OUTSIDE the body — with matching close `j = hi`. (Confirm: `balance (lo-1) a = 1 + balance lo a = 1 ≥ 1` pins `lo-1` as the nearest enclosing opener; the `.flowSequenceEnd` at `hi` with `balance lo hi = 0` pins its matching close to `hi`, so `hiE = j+1 = hi+1`.) So the enclosing window the R470/R471 siblings must deliver facts for is the FRAME `[lo-1, hi+1)`, width `(hi+1)-(lo-1) = (hi - lo) + 2` — exactly TWO wider than the body (the opener it adds left, the closer right). A strong induction keyed on the BODY width `w = hi - lo` hands an IH covering every `k < w`, and `w + 2` is never `< w` (`¬ (w+2 < w)`). The frame obligation is out of the body-width IH's reach.

**Benign in consumption, not in the type.** The width IH is actually CONSUMED only at the body's entries (all `< hi - lo` — the `#guard`-style probes were right that every USED sub-window is strictly narrower), so a `< hi-lo` IH suffices operationally. But to INHABIT the obligation's type one must supply a term at every index `< hiE - p = (hi-lo)+2`: at width exactly `hi - lo` the only inhabited frame-interior window is the body `[lo, hi)` ITSELF — whose `RecSeqBody` is the pair's OTHER half, a genuine self-reference that does not reduce by the `<` guard — and at width `hi - lo + 1` no valid `FlowBodyWindow` ending on the close exists (vacuous, the END-dual [[ref-boundary-residual-end-dual]]). Discharging both gap widths by hand is possible but fiddly, and is the signal the measure is wrong.

**The PIVOT — re-key on the ENCLOSING-FRAME width.** Make the recursion's object the FRAME `[p, hiE)`, not the inner body. Then the OUTERMOST frame — the whole document bracket `[1, size - 1)` — is the LARGEST, the base case; every nested frame inside a body is strictly NARROWER (the body of a frame is its child `[p+1, hiE-1)`, width `frameWidth - 2`, and any nested frame inside that body has width `< frameWidth`); and `h_widthEnc`'s per-window obligation is ITSELF frame-shaped (`[p, hiE)`), so the IH guard and the obligation index COINCIDE — no `+2` gap, no self-reference, no vacuity bookkeeping. The measure choice IS the de-risk's deliverable. New memory [[ref-enclosing-frame-rekeys-width-recursion]] (sharpens [[ref-width-recursion-combinator-before-grammar-step]] — pick the metric before the grammar step — and [[ref-probe-deferred-universal-before-producing]]; the gap-width vacuity is [[ref-boundary-residual-end-dual]]; runs the de-risk queued by [[ref-boundary-inclusive-sibling-cascade]]).

Concrete: body `[2,6)` width `4`, frame `[1,7)` width `6 = 4 + 2`; `solveFrame 6 = 3` (`6 → 4 → 2 → 0`, three nested frame levels). ### Reflection 421 — trigger-coincidence RELOCATES the obligation: mirroring a gated-adjacency producer's token-CONCRETE wrap/seam layer CONSERVES the content-start obligation but moves it to whichever emitted token coincides with the NEW trigger (and excises that seat from the tail bridge's domain)

R420 localised the non-free work to the token-CONCRETE wrap/seam/glue layer (the combinator layer below clones verbatim). R421 is the SHAPE of that work, landed: it is **not** "re-derive each wrap/seam/glue lemma from scratch" — it is "relocate ONE conserved obligation to the trigger-coinciding seat, vacate the sibling's old seat, and restrict any 'last ≠ trigger' tail bridge to exclude that seat." The obligation count is INVARIANT across the mirror; only its POSITION moves, governed by which emitted structural token coincides with the new trigger. **For `OpenerAdj`** the trigger `.flowSequenceStart` coincides with the block OPENER (head of a `wrap`) → `OpenerAdj_wrap_seq` carries the head obligation `h_head`, and the `.flowEntry` SEAM is inert (`OpenerAdj_seam` discharges its seam by the tail bridge `feTok ≠ .flowSequenceStart`). **For `SepAdj`** the trigger `.flowEntry` coincides with the SEAM → `SepAdj_wrap_seq`/`_wrap_map` SHED `h_head` (vacuous head, identical to `OpenerAdj_wrap_map`, AND drop `h_cl`), while `SepAdj_seam` GAINS the obligation `h_head_rest`. Net: same obligation, moved head↔seam — the wraps got SIMPLER, the seam got HEAVIER; `SepAdj_map_single` stayed a verbatim clone because its `.key`/`.value` tokens coincide with NEITHER trigger (no emitted token hits the trigger ⇒ no relocation). **Corollary (tail-bridge domain restriction):** a "last ≠ trigger" tail bridge over a shape whose seam IS the trigger (`a ++ [feTok] ++ rest`, feTok = trigger) has NO sound analogue at `rest = []` — the last token is then the trigger seam itself, so the fact is FALSE; `OpenerAdj`'s `lastNonOpener_append3` covered `rest = []` (inert seam ≠ opener) but the `SepAdj` version's domain restricts to `rest ≠ []` (sound: the emitter never trails a separator). So trigger-coincidence relocates the obligation AND excises the trigger-coinciding seat from the tail bridge's domain. **Replay test:** before mirroring a wrap/seam/glue lemma to a sibling trigger, enumerate the shape's emitted tokens (opener, seam, retro key/value, close) and find which one coincides with the NEW trigger — THAT seat is obligated, the sibling's obligated seat goes vacuous, and any "last ≠ trigger" tail bridge over a shape ending in the new-trigger token loses its empty-tail case. You CAN still price the layer by counting obligations (the count is invariant); you just cannot assume they sit where the sibling's did. Refines [[ref-adjacency-mirror-corner-is-layer-scoped]] (R420 says WHERE the work is; this says WHAT it is — relocate one conserved obligation + restrict the tail bridge); same structural move as [[ref-lift-once-mirror-the-easy-edge]] ("the easy edge degrades to the hard edge's MIRROR — same restriction, only the head-seating field swapped"); shares the arity-reads-a-storage-fact flavour of [[ref-mirror-constructor-arity-reads-storage]] (here the wrap/seam hypothesis-arity delta reads off which emitted token coincides with the trigger). Demo: `Tests/Reflections/TriggerCoincidenceRelocatesObligation.lean` — a toy `Tok` with parametric `adj trig gate`, a headed wrap `adj_wrap_headed` and a seam glue `adj_seam` (each with its head obligation GATED on token = trigger); at trigger = OPENER the obligation sits on `adjA_wrapHeaded_obligated` and `adjA_seam_vacuous` needs none; at trigger = SEAM they SWAP (`adjB_wrapHeaded_vacuous` / `adjB_seam_obligated`) — the relocation made literal; plus a NEGATIVE `seamTrailing_last_is_trigger`/`_not_ne_trigger` showing the tail bridge is unsound at `rest = []` when feTok = trigger, recovered by `seamNonTrailing_last_ne_trigger` (the `rest ≠ []` form). New memory [[ref-trigger-coincidence-relocates-obligation]].

### Reflection 420 — a gated-adjacency mirror's non-cloning BOUNDARY corner (R418) is LAYER-SCOPED: the token-opaque list-combinator layer clones VERBATIM under a uniform (trigger, gate) substitution; the corner bites only where the discharge inspects a CONCRETE token

R418 warned: do NOT price a gated-adjacency producer mirror by its skeleton — the pre-close BOUNDARY cell does not clone. R420 scopes that warning: **it is a property of the LAYER, not the mirror.** The list-COMBINATOR layer below the global producer — the predicate + `nil`/`singleton`/`cons`/`append`/`array` — clones VERBATIM under a single uniform (trigger, gate) token substitution, because every combinator proof is TOKEN-OPAQUE structural induction over LIST POSITION. Building the seq separator field's combinator layer `SepAdj` (trigger `.flowEntry`, gate `≠ .key`) as the mirror of R408's `OpenerAdj` (trigger `.flowSequenceStart`, gate `≠ .flowSequenceEnd`), all five bricks cloned with NO proof edits and built green on the FIRST attempt — including `SepAdj_append`, whose `a`-last-token boundary case is the combinator analogue of the cell R418 says does not clone. **Why it clones here but not at the global layer:** the combinator proofs never inspect the trigger/gate token values (those live only in the field's premises/conclusion, threaded as opaque hypotheses `hsep : … = .flowEntry`, `hne : … ≠ .key`, `h_head`, `h_tail`); the `_append` boundary refutes the trigger premise against an ABSTRACT tail-bridge hypothesis `≠ trigger`, never a concrete token; `_array` uses only positional lemmas (`getElem!_pos`/`List.getElem_drop`/`Array.getElem_toList`). The `OpenerAdj` field is ORTHOGONAL to the balance carrier (R397) and must land ATOMICALLY across the mutually-recursive value↔list predicates (the item's `OpenerAdj` is not derivable from existing fields — no split is possible on `OpenerAdj` itself). **The move:** its CONSUMER wrap-lemma `OpenerAdj_wrap_seq` needs two BOUNDARY side-inputs about the body (`h_head` content-start, `h_tail` last-not-opener) that are NOT `OpenerAdj` but strictly WEAKER facts, DERIVABLE from the producer's EXISTING per-item fields (content-start head + the R400 tail-not-opener) — so land those side-input fields FIRST, on the body predicate only, as a separate green increment. Pay-off twofold: (1) the side-inputs ride the SAME `block₁ ++ [.flowEntry] ++ block_rest` recursion-append structure `OpenerAdj` will traverse, so landing them PROVES the shared append/last-element machinery before the harder threading; (2) the atomic field increment shrinks to just the field. This is a STAGING application of [[ref-bridge-derivable-from-invariant]] (the side-inputs are bridge-style derivable facts) and a consumer-first variant of [[ref-consumer-joint-before-producer]]. **Two tactical nuggets:** (a) the producer's body term is LEFT-ASSOCIATED (`(block₁ ++ [feTok]) ++ block_rest`), so a boundary-fact helper must be stated in that EXACT term shape — rewriting a list under the dependent `length-1` getElem hits "motive is not type correct"; discharge a LAST-element fact via `getLast?` COMPOSITION (`getLast?_append` ⇒ `.or`, `getLast?_cons_of_ne_nil`, `getLast?_concat`) + a `getLast?`↔`getElem` bridge pair, never getElem manipulation (a HEAD fact's `[0]` index is constant ⇒ `getElem_append_left` is motive-free). This EXTENDS [[ref-bridge-derivable-from-invariant]]'s grep-by-field-ending over-match caution to `replace_all`-by-shared-binder-names; same root: parallel predicates with structurally identical destructure tails.
